entries.sought: The national number French Polynesia gives its people: its name, issuer, format, when it's given and what needs it

sources.title: Institut de la statistique de la Polynésie française, Numéro NIR
sources.said: Décret n° 2006-278 du 8 mars 2006 modifiant le décret n° 82-103 du 22 janvier 1982 relatif au répertoire national d'identification des personnes physiques et portant extension à l‘Outre-mer de l'identification au répertoire ... Le NIR (numéro d'inscription au répertoire) est un identifiant unique des personnes inscrites au répertoire national d'identification des personnes physiques (RNIPP) géré par l'INSEE. ... il est composé de 15 chiffres ... En Polynésie française, il servira aux personnes évasanées pour leur traitement médical en Métropole et à certains retraités locaux, ainsi qu'aux étudiants polynésiens ... L’ISPF centralise les informations reçues des communes en vue de l'immatriculation des individus nés en Polynésie française et les transmet à l’INSEE. Ainsi, toutes les naissances enregistrées par les communes donnent lieu à l’attribution automatique du NIR par l’INSEE.

sources.said: ມາດຕາ 14 (ປັບປຸງ) ອາຍຸຂອງຜູ້ສອບເສັງເອົາໃບຂັບຂີ່ ... - ແຕ່ ສິບແປດ ປີ ຂຶ້ນໄປ ສຳລັບລົດຈັກ ຄວາມແຮງ ແຕ່ 125 cc ຂຶ້ນໄປ, ລົດສາມລໍ້, ລົດໄຖນາທີ່ແກ່ລໍ້, ລົດຕ່ອງໆ, ລົດຂົນສົ່ງສ່ວນຕົວ ແລະ ລົດຂົນສົ່ງສະເພາະ ບໍ່ເກີນ ເກົ້າ ບ່ອນນັ່ງ ລວມທັງຜູ້ຂັບຂີ່ ຫຼື ນ້ຳໜັກລວມບໍ່ເກີນ 3.500 ກິໂລກຣາມ ... ມາດຕາ 15 (ໃໝ່) ໃບຂັບຂີ່ ... ໃບຂັບຂີ່ພາຍໃນ ແມ່ນ ອອກໃຫ້ແກ່ພົນລະເມືອງລາວ, ຊາວຕ່າງດ້າວ, ຄົນບໍ່ມີສັນຊາດ, ຄົນຕ່າງປະເທດ ທີ່ໄດ້ຜ່ານການສອບເສັງ ຢູ່ ສປປ ລາວ ... ມີອາຍຸການນຳໃຊ້ ຫ້າປີ ແລະ ສາມາດຕໍ່ໄດ້ຄັ້ງລະ ຫ້າ ປີ. ... ມາດຕາ 16 ... B: ລົດເບົາ ນ້ຳໜັກລວມ ຕ່ຳກວ່າ 3.500 ກິໂລກຣາມ, ບໍ່ເກີນ ເກົ້າ ບ່ອນນັ່ງ ລວມທັງຜູ້ຂັບຂີ່

entries.foundInPart: Read 2026-11-03 in the Libyan legal compilation al-Majma' al-Qanuni al-Libi (lawsociety.ly), which names no gazette it reproduces: Law No. 11 of 1984, art. 26(a), no driving licence under eighteen Gregorian years (a decision may raise it); art. 23, class one category B for private cars; Decision No. 253 of 1994, LD 15 for a duplicate and LD 5 for the medical. The licence's fee and term weren't found, and the compilation is a lead, not the primary.

entries.foundInPart: Progress (2026-11-03): the Republic of Palau Social Security Administration's own application form (ROPSSA 500-02, Rev.10/14) names the number (the Republic of Palau Social Security Number) and its issuer, and says Palauans apply with a birth certificate or passport, others with a passport or provisional visa and permit; the Bureau of Revenue and Taxation's Tax-100 (2019) reads the number's first three digits as a citizen code (006, 040) and asks for its last six. sources.title: Revenue Services Administration Regulations 2021 (Tonga), Part 2: Taxpayer Identification Numbers
sources.said: 3 (1) An application for a Taxpayer Identification Number shall be – (a) in the following form – (i) for an individual whose only income is employment income, Form 1 in Schedule 1 ... 4 (3) An application for a Taxpayer Identification Number by an individual who is not a Tongan citizen shall include a certified copy of the individual's residency visa or work permit. ... 6 (1) Each Taxpayer Identification Number issued by the Minister shall be a unique number and two persons shall not be issued with the same Taxpayer Identification Number.

entries.foundInPart: Progress (2026-11-03): Tonga's Revenue Services Administration Regulations 2021 (regs 3 to 6, the Ministry of Revenue and Customs' own copy) set the TIN's application, on Form 1 (an individual whose only income is employment income), Form 2 (any other individual) or Form 3, a non-citizen adding a certified copy of a residency visa or work permit, and say each TIN the Minister issues is unique. Under the lead's ruling of 2026-11-03 the Ministry's Registration Listing by Tax Type (2021), whose TINs are six digits, is a lead, not a stated length. Still missing: the length in the Ministry's words, and any check digit.

entries.foundInPart: Niue's Immigration Act 2011, published by the Immigration Department on the Ministry of Finance's site, gives the routes: a temporary permit (a work permit for employment or the provision of any services, or a student permit), granted at the Chief Immigration Officer's discretion for the period and on the conditions it states, applied for on arrival or renewed in Niue with two character references, a police report, health clearances and, where the temporary entry guidelines require, a sponsor; and the permanent residence certificate, granted by Cabinet at its discretion only after ten years' continuous residence on a temporary permit, which allows any lawful activity without another permit. Every application is made 'with any applicable fee', and the fees are set by the Immigration Regulations 2011, which no reachable copy holds (the Department's 'Fees & Charges' page lists none), so the routes aren't whole and Niue's residence stays unkept.

sources.title: Niue, Immigration Act 2011 (2011/309, 7 April 2011), as consolidated in the Niue Legislation Act 2019, published by the Niue Immigration Department (Ministry of Finance)
sources.said: s7(1) every person must hold a valid permit to remain in Niue. s14(7) 'There are the following types of temporary permits: (a) work permits for persons intending to undertake employment or provide any services in Niue; (b) student permits ...'; s14(2) grant is at the Chief Immigration Officer's discretion; s14(4) the permit states its expiry and conditions; s14(9) valid until the earlier of departure or the stated expiry. s15(1) apply on arrival to the Immigration Officer 'together with any applicable fee'; s16 further temporary permits applied for in Niue 'with any applicable fee'; s16A two character references, a police report and health clearances; s17 a sponsor acceptable to the Chief Immigration Officer if the temporary entry guidelines require. s20(1) a permanent residence certificate entitles the holder to remain and travel indefinitely and 'undertake any lawful activity in Niue without the need for any other permit'; s20(2) granted by Cabinet at its discretion; s20(5)(a) only after the applicant 'has resided continuously on Niue on a temporary permit for a period of not less than 10 years'; s21(1) applied for in Niue on a valid temporary permit 'with any applicable fee'.

entries.sought: Whether a national rule (Ley 5016/2014 Nacional de Tránsito y Seguridad Vial, its regulation, or the Agencia Nacional de Tránsito y Seguridad Vial) fixes for all of Paraguay the private-car licence's category, the age it is held from, its term and its fee, so that Paraguay could be kept whole rather than by the municipalities that issue it.

attempts.tried: https://www.antsv.gov.py/, https://antsv.gov.py/, http://www.antsv.gov.py/ (redirects to https://antsv.gov.py/) and https://www.antsv.gov.py/licencia (the ANTSV); https://mopc.gov.py/?s=5016 and https://mopc.gov.py/institucional/marco-juridico/ (Ministry of Public Works, which the ANTSV answers to)
attempts.result: Every ANTSV address failed with 'Connection reset by peer' in the TLS handshake; the MOPC answers, but its search for 5016 lists only road-safety news and its legal-framework page carries no traffic-law text.

attempts.tried: SILpy, the Congress's legislative system (rendered honestly with Playwright): https://silpy.congreso.gov.py/web/ley/136008 (Ley 5016: sanctioned 31/07/2013, promulgated 16/05/2014, published 21/05/2014), its scanned text https://silpy.congreso.gov.py/web/descarga/ley-136008 (saved as dl/lpy/ley5016.pdf, pp. 12-14 read by eye), its regulating decree https://silpy.congreso.gov.py/web/descarga/decreto-100059 (Decreto 3427/2015, saved as dl/lpy/dec3427.pdf, text layer read), and the law search for Ley 5799 (the amendment of arts. 22, 27 and others); https://www.bacn.gov.py/conoce-tu-ley/12070/tr-nsito-y-seguridad-vial and the BACN's Ley 5016 pages; https://www.gacetaoficial.gov.py/
attempts.result: Read: Ley 5016 art. 22(g) fixes 18 for the 'Particular' category nationally ('Dieciocho años para la licencia de conducir de categorías "Particular", "Motociclista" y "Extranjero"'); art. 24(a) has the municipalities issue it, (b) on a unified model whose standards the ANTSV approves, and (c) 'Las licencias podrán otorgarse por una validez de hasta 5 (cinco) años'. The regulation, Decreto 3427/2015 Annex art. 7(c): 'Serán otorgadas por el plazo máximo de cinco (5) años, y en ningún caso podrá ser menor a un (1) año. Quedará a cargo de la Autoridad de aplicación determinar el tiempo de validez de cada Licencia de Conducir.' So the term is not fixed nationally (one to five years, set licence by licence), and neither text sets a fee. Ley 5799, which would have amended arts. 22 and 27, was objected in total by the Executive (message 671, 05/10/2017) and its bills are archived; no enacted amendment of art. 24 was found among the law's related bills. bacn.gov.py answered Cloudflare's 'error code: 523' (origin unreachable) on every page; gacetaoficial.gov.py reset the connection (https) and answered 503 (http).

entries.sought: Kosovo's hours of sunshine as normals, which the WMO's sets, the Deutscher Wetterdienst's and the World Weather Information Service don't give

value.note: Kosovo's monthly hours of sunshine, 1961-1990, at Priština, Peć and Prizren, from the Republic Hydrometeorological Service of Serbia (RHMZ Srbije), Normale za sinoptičke stanice: each station's page 'Srednje mesečne, godišnje i ekstremne vrednosti 1961 - 1990', row 'Trajanje sijanja sunca, Prosek' (hours a month; each row's twelve months sum to its annual value: 2123.3, 1983.5, 2137.4). Coordinates and heights are the pages' own (Priština 42°39'N 21°09'E 573 m; Peć 42°40'N 20°18'E 498 m; Prizren 42°12'N 20°43'E 402 m), turned to decimal degrees. Only sun is taken: Kosovo's temperatures, precipitation and days already come from the sets before. Readings for the lead: the institution is Serbia's service, which ran these stations in 1961-1990, not IHMK (Kosovo's own service, whose site carries a Cloudflare script and publishes only a 2024 yearbook); the pages are HTML tables, parseable, so a parser could replace the hand entry. Prizren's January (100.2) exceeds its February (92.0): that is what the page says.

entries.sought: The Solomon Islands' hours of sunshine as normals, which the WMO's sets, the Deutscher Wetterdienst's and the World Weather Information Service don't give

value.note: The Solomon Islands' sunshine at Henderson Airport, Guadalcanal, from JICA's 2006 study for the Solomon Islands Water Authority (Supporting Report S-1, page 13, table S-1-5): mean daily hours of sunshine, each year 1986-1998 and their 'Mean' row, turned to monthly hours by the month's days (February's 28.25), as R-0057 does for Nepal. Readings for the lead, all material: (1) the table's header says 'Year: 1986 - 1996' but its rows run to 1998 and its means are of 1986-1998 (January's 13 values average 5.95, the row's 6.0), so the period written is 1986-1998; (2) the sunshine page names no source: the next page (S-1-6, rainfall) is headed 'Solomon Islands Meteorological Service', which is the likely but unstated source; (3) thirteen years is short of a normal by WMO-No. 1203's rule, which the engine applies to GHCN-Daily only; (4) it is a consultant's compilation (secondary). If the lead holds it, the attempts below stand as the blocker.

entries.sought: Vanuatu's hours of sunshine as normals, which the WMO's sets, the Deutscher Wetterdienst's and the World Weather Information Service don't give

value.note: Vanuatu's monthly hours of sunshine at Port Vila, from the Vanuatu Meteorological Services' own page 'Climate for Port Vila (Efate)' ('Your Climate when Visiting Port Vila, Efate'), on its former site www.meteo.gov.vu, read in archive.org's snapshots of 2009-09-15 and 2017-03-29 (the page's figures are the same in both; the CDX index lists eleven captures between, the last on 2017-03-29). Each month's 'Climate Averages' gives 'Average Sunshine Hours' (198 to 139, summing to 2,152 a year), with rainfall, mean maximum and minimum temperature and humidity, all whole numbers. The current site (vmgd.gov.vu) carries no such table; a later text was looked for there (R-0105's attempts of 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-30) and in today's searches, and none was found. Only sun is taken: Port Vila's temperatures already come from the WWIS (wwis:673), and the sought days of at least 1 mm are not on the page. Readings for the lead, all material: (1) the page states no period, so period is null (the form allows it; the lead's rule asks for a stated period); (2) 'Average Sunshine Hours' is read as the month's total hours (the values, 139 to 208, fit monthly totals of about 4.6 to 6.7 hours a day, not daily means); (3) the page names Port Vila, not a station: the place written is the WWIS's for Port Vila (-17.73, 168.32, Vanuatu's own submission), which is the same city's station, and no height is given; (4) the source is an archived copy of a page the service no longer serves (2017 at the latest). Still blocked for VU: days of at least 1 mm (attempts below). On 2026-11-02 neither archived copy (2009-09-15, 2017-03-29) could be read: web.archive.org reset the connection from this environment (three tries), a browser got 502 and archive.org's availability API answered 429, so the vendored copies weren't compared again; they are themselves the archive's, so no other archive applies. The World Weather Information Service's city 673 still gives Port Vila at -17.73, 168.32.

sources.said: § 602. Conditions of observance. entries.foundInPart: Read 2026-11-03 on the Nitijela's own site (rmiparliament.org): the majority, eighteen (Domestic Relations Act, 26 MIRC Ch. 1, s. 107, as amended by P.L. 2023-63), is held in research/sources/papers/ages/MH.json (papers.ages.MH). The working age isn't: the Child Rights Protection Act 2015 defines a child as below eighteen and names children's work 'not in accordance with the regulations of this Law' as exploitation, but sets no minimum age of employment, and no minimum-age statute is in the Nitijela's list of Acts by title (its labour Acts are the Collective Bargaining Relations Act 2022, the Minimum Conditions Inquiry Act 1983 and the Non-Resident Workers Act 2018). No military service law was read; the Youth Service Corps Act 2016 is voluntary youth service. Read 2026-11-03 besides: the Labor (Minimum Conditions) Inquiry Act 1983 only lets its commission recommend minimum ages for employment, setting none; that no statute holds the age isn't established, since no text that would hold it was read whole, so the working age stays blocked. The Constitution, art. II § 11, bars conscription save in war or imminent danger of war that the Cabinet certifies, so there is no military service in peace; it isn't held, since the game doesn't read service.

entries.foundInPart: Read 2026-11-03 on the Pakistan Code: the Majority Act 1875, s. 3, eighteen, which the person research (person.ages.PK) already gives. The working age is set by province since the 18th Amendment: Punjab's Restriction on Employment of Children Act 2016 (a Punjab Local Government host's copy) bars an occupier from employing or letting work in an establishment any child under fifteen, with no exception for performing; the federal Employment of Children Act 1991 ('child' under fourteen) bars children only from the occupations and processes of its Schedule, work in cinemas among them, sets no general age, and runs only where a province hasn't replaced it. The form holds the working age by country, not by province, and Sindh's, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's and Balochistan's Acts weren't read, so Pakistan's isn't held. No national service law appeared in the Pakistan Code's list.

entries.foundInPart: Read 2026-11-03 in the Congress's library (BACN): the majority, eighteen (Ley 2169 of 2003), is held in research/sources/papers/ages/PY.json (papers.ages.PY). The working age isn't: the Labour Code as Ley 496 of 1995 amends it, art. 36, lets minors over twelve and under eighteen contract work with an authorisation their legal representative may condition, limit or revoke; art. 119 bars those under fifteen from industrial firms; and an employer of children under twelve is fined. The person research (person.ages.PY) reads the Code's work outside industry from fourteen to eighteen; which of twelve and fourteen is the general age, and whether the Código de la Niñez y la Adolescencia (Ley 1680/01) or Paraguay's ratification of ILO C138 sets another, wasn't settled, and no rule for a performer was found. Military service wasn't read.

sources.title: Ley Nº 496 que modifica, amplía y deroga artículos de la Ley 213/93, Código del Trabajo (promulgada 22-08-1995), Biblioteca y Archivo Central del Congreso Nacional

La misma podrá ser condicionada, limitada o revocada por el representante legal del menor. ... "Art. 119.- Los menores que no hayan cumplido quince años de edad no podrán trabajar en empresa industrial pública o privada o en sus dependencias, salvo lo establecido en el artículo siguiente". ... Al empleador que ocupe a niños menores de doce años, se le impondrá multa de cincuenta jornales mínimos

entries.foundInPart: Read 2026-11-03: the Ministry of Law's Second Reading speech on the Civil Law (Amendment) Bill (19 January 2009) says the age of majority is twenty-one and the Bill lowers the age of contractual capacity to eighteen (land dealings and leases over three years excepted); the Civil Law Act, s. 35, as in force wasn't read (SSO answered 403), and the form's majority (full age and contracts in one's own name) splits there, so neither age is held. National Service: male citizens and permanent residents register at 16½ and are enlisted from eighteen (MFA, CMPB); the full-time term and the upper age weren't read on an official page.

sources.title: Ministry of Law: Second Reading Speech on Civil Law (Amendment) Bill by Senior Minister of State Assoc Prof Ho Peng Kee, 19 Jan 2009
sources.said: the current minimum age of contractual capacity is tied to the age of majority, which is 21 years in Singapore. ... this Bill seeks to de-link the age of majority from the age of contractual capacity, reducing the age of contractual capacity from 21 to 18 years. ... clause 6 provides that every contract entered into by a minor who has attained the age of 18 years will have effect as if he were a person of full age, unless otherwise provided. ... the ability of an 18-year old to contract will not apply to contracts for the sale, purchase, mortgage, assignment or settlement of any land or a lease of land for more than 3 years.

entries.foundInPart: Read 2026-11-03 in a print of the People's Assembly's own page for Law No. 17 of 2010, the Labour Law, marked in force (parliament.gov.sy doesn't resolve today): art. 113(a), no juvenile may be employed before finishing basic education or turning fifteen, whichever is later; art. 113(b) leaves the system of their employment to a decision of the Minister (Decision No. 12 of 2010, not read). Art. 5(a) leaves casual work, and part-time work of no more than two hours a day, outside the Law, those workers held to their contracts (art. 5(b)), so whether its bar reaches a child engaged for a single performance isn't settled, and the working age isn't held. The majority (eighteen, the Civil Code's art. 46) was seen only on a law site that gives no address for the primary it reproduces, a lead.

entries.foundInPart: Read 2026-11-03: the Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 in the Department of Labour Protection and Welfare's own consolidated English text (as amended to B.E. 2553, with Ministerial Regulation No. 14 B.E. 2555; February B.E. 2557, FAOLEX's copy), s. 44: no employer may employ a child under fifteen; the Act makes no exception for performing (s. 47 lets a performer under eighteen in film or theatre work at night, s. 160 kept those of thirteen and fourteen already employed before the Act). Not held: the text predates the Act's later amendments, which weren't read for s. 44. The majority (Civil and Commercial Code) and military service weren't read.

sources.title: The Labour Protection Act B.E. 2541 (as amended to B.E. 2553 and Ministerial Regulation No. 14 B.E. 2555), consolidated English text by the Department of Labour Protection and Welfare, February B.E. 2557 (FAOLEX's copy)
sources.said: Section 44. An Employer shall not employ a child under fifteen years of age as an Employee. ... Section 47. An Employer shall not require a young worker under eighteen years of age to work between 22.00 hours and 6.00 hours unless written permission is granted by the Director-General ... The Employer may require a young worker under eighteen years of age who is a performer in film, theatre or other similar acts to work during such hours; provided that the Employer shall provide the young worker with proper rest periods.

entries.foundInPart: Read 2026-11-03: the Norfolk Island Applied Laws Ordinance 2016 (compilation No. 18, 28 January 2022) suspends in the Territory every New South Wales law but those it lists, among which neither the Minors (Property and Contracts) Act 1970 nor the Children and Young Persons (Care and Protection) Act 1998 is; the 2023 Suspension amendment runs the suspension to the end of 31 December 2026. The Federal Register of Legislation's versions of the Ordinance, read the same day, end at compilation No. 19 (28 June 2023) with no amendment unincorporated, so no extension had been registered. Work so rests on the Employment Act 1988 (NI), which sets no general minimum age, and the majority on the Island's own continued law, not found.

sources.title: Norfolk Island Applied Laws Ordinance 2016, Compilation No. 18 (compilation date 28/01/2022, Authorised Version F2022C00166), Federal Register of Legislation
sources.said: Schedule 1, item 1(1): The operation of the legislation of New South Wales, other than an Act specified in the following table or legislation made under such an Act, is suspended in the Territory for the period: (a) beginning on the day this item commences; and (b) ... ending immediately before the start of 1 July 2023. [Never-suspended table: Health Services Act 1997, Interpretation Act 1987, Local Government Act 1993, Long Service Leave Act 1955; subitem (3) table: Anti-Discrimination Act 1977, Crimes (Domestic and Personal Violence) Act 2007, Education Act 1990, Education Standards Authority Act 2013, Electoral Funding Act 2018, First State Superannuation Act 1992, Government Information (Public Access) Act 2009, Government Sector Employment Act 2013, Industrial Relations Act 1996, Law Enforcement (Powers and Responsibilities) Act 2002, Lobbying of Government Officials Act 2011, Public Finance and Audit Act 1983, Public Health Act 2010, Superannuation Administration Act 1996, Teaching Service Act 1980, Workers Compensation Act 1987, Work Health and Safety Act 2011, Workplace Injury Management and Workers Compensation Act 1998.] Schedule 1A item 33 refers care proceedings to 'section 59 of the Child Welfare Act 2009 of Norfolk Island'.

sources.title: Norfolk Island Applied Laws Amendment (Suspension) Ordinance 2023 (F2023L00869, registered 27/06/2023)
sources.said: Paragraph 1(1)(b) of Schedule 1: Omit 'ending immediately before the start of 1 July 2023', substitute 'ending at the end of 31 December 2026'.

sources.title: Screen Credits Manual - Writers Guild of America West
sources.said: Arbiters must take into consideration the following elements in determining whether a writer is entitled to screenplay credit: dramatic construction; original and different scenes; characterization or character relationships; and dialogue. … For example, many lines of dialogue may be changed, and the arbiters might still find the changes not significant enough to warrant screenplay credit. On the other hand, a small number of lines of dialogue may be changed in such a significant manner that the arbiters deem them highly contributive to screenplay credit. … The term "story" means all writing covered by the provisions of the MBA representing a contribution "distinct from screenplay and consisting of basic narrative, idea, theme or outline indicating character development and action." … A screenplay consists of individual scenes and full dialogue, together with such prior treatment, basic adaptation, continuity, scenario, and dialogue as shall be used in, and represent substantial contributions to the final script. … In the context of credit determination, “original” does not refer to the unique creative quality of a screenplay, but rather to the absence of assigned source material. … Arbiters should give weight to any writer's original and unique utilization, choice, or arrangement of source material when it is present in the final shooting script … If the writer is furnished source material of a story nature but takes from it only a springboard, a characterization, an incident, or some equally limited contribution, creating a substantially new and different story from the source material, the writer may receive "Screen Story by" credit, but only as the result of arbitration. … However, the Guild recognizes that there are certain unusual cases where credit is due a writer who shapes the direction of screenplay construction without qualifying for "Screenplay by" credit.

sources.title: How do the Nicholl Fellowships in Screenwriting readers judge a script?
sources.said: Does this script have vivid characters who each speak in their own voice? … Does this script genuinely make you want to keep reading? Are the themes of the story thought-provoking, across genres? Is the story “about something” that might spark discussion among friends? … Does the central character change over the course of the story? If it’s an ensemble film, does more than one character change? … Do the main characters take actions that move the story along? … Are these actions in keeping with who these people are? Or do they happen “conveniently”? … Does the conflict propel the story forward? … Does the script have a distinctive and original voice? (Or do you feel that you’ve read or seen this movie before?) … Nicholl readers use the following guidelines to judge and score screenplays during the competition. Story … Does reading the script make you think, “This person genuinely has the potential to develop into a professional writer”? … Does the story connect with you emotionally, whether it’s a comedy or drama or another genre? … Does this writer know how to use description and dialogue to create suspense, tension, drama, comedy and conflict? Does the conflict propel the story forward? … Does the story have an original premise? … Does that story idea start the movie forward? … Does the story itself have a strong beginning, middle & end? How about two out of three? If the story is non-linear, does it make sense? … Does this script make you feel that the writer is taking you on a journey? … Are the premise, story and characters new or fresh for you? … Do you want to know what happens to them? … Do the dialogue and tone seem consistent from scene to scene? … Does the way the people speak fit the tone and setting of the story? … When you finish reading the script, even if it has flaws, do you still feel that there’s something special about it? Is there an indescribable “something” that elevates this script above the ordinary?

sources.title: Screenwriting (MFA) | UCLA School of Theater, Film, and Television
sources.said: The Screenwriting program challenges students to write well-structured stories inhabited by vivid, compelling characters. The program explores the elements of character, dialogue, scene, setting, texture, style and tone. … We challenge our students to succeed through risking failure, to engage with other art forms in order to better understand the art of screenwriting, to cultivate a curiosity in global art, to develop critical thinking skills to aid in the analysis of their scripts, and to provide an ethical foundation in building a career path.

sources.title: Rechercher une certification - France compétences
sources.said: Créer les personnages principaux d’un scénario de fiction cinématographique ou audiovisuelle, ainsi que leurs histoires, enjeux et conflits, en sachant refléter la diversité sociétale le cas échéant … Développer la conception de personnages de fiction cinématographique ou audiovisuelle en précisant leurs caractéristiques, leur évolution dans le déroulement de l’histoire, leurs interactions et leur type de langage pour les rendre cohérents et crédibles. … Réécrire partiellement ou totalement un scénario de fiction, pour aboutir à une nouvelle version qui respecte la singularité et la cohérence globale du projet initial, tout en tenant compte des contraintes apportées par des professionnels avec lesquels on collabore. … Analyser les caractéristiques d’un scénario de fiction à expertiser, notamment sa problématique principale, les intentions de l’auteur, son format audiovisuel ou cinématographique, son genre, le public visé, les financeurs potentiels, pour estimer son potentiel de réalisation. … Examiner les forces et faiblesses d’un scénario de fiction, de son sujet, du récit et de la narration, des personnages et des dialogues, de l’univers visuel et sonore, pour en faire une restitution constructive dégageant des pistes d’amélioration. … Évaluer la dramaturgie d’un scénario en vérifiant la cohérence du récit et de la narration au regard de l’intention de l’auteur (les actes, le point de vue, la construction des personnages et la place du spectateur), pour apprécier sa pertinence et envisager des consignes à transmettre à l’auteur en vue de la prochaine version. … Construire un synopsis respectueux des règles dramaturgiques, décrivant les éléments clés relatifs à l’action principale du récit, aux personnages, à l'histoire, à son enjeu, et au contexte géographique et temporel d’une fiction, pour préparer la rédaction de la continuité dialoguée. … Développer les différents textes (synopsis, traitement, séquencier) d’une fiction cinématographique ou audiovisuelle, en y adjoignant la description des images et des sons, pour donner la possibilité aux professionnels (producteur, réalisateur, diffuseur…) d’imaginer le film en devenir, de la manière la plus précise possible. … Élaborer l’enchainement des scènes d’une fiction cinématographique ou audiovisuelle à partir d’actions décrites en images et en sons, pour aboutir à une continuité dialoguée. … Élaborer un traitement du projet de fiction longue pour exprimer visuellement l’univers de la fiction. … Élaborer le séquencier du récit d’une fiction cinématographique ou audiovisuelle, en constituant un enchaînement d’actes formant une progression dramatique, afin de créer une temporalité fictionnelle tenant compte de la place du spectateur et d’avoir une présentation générale des scènes. … Rédiger la note d’intention d’un scénario de fiction, pour la transmettre à des partenaires potentiels : producteur, réalisateur, diffuseur, membres de commissions de subventions. … Évaluer les forces et les pistes d’amélioration du projet de scénario d’un pilote de série, dans une fiche de lecture, en expertisant l’univers et l’arène, la thématique, le ou les personnages principaux et leur trajectoire, les antagonistes, les conflits des personnages, la structure dramaturgique, l’originalité du projet et la cible afin d’orienter le développement du projet. … Analyser un pilote de série en se référant aux outils de la dramaturgie sérielle et en le résumant afin de guider la réécriture de l’auteur et apporter un point de vue permettant de préciser le concept et l’idée motrice de la série. … Il doit être capable de gérer la segmentation des commandes d’écriture (synopsis, traitement, séquencier, continuité dialoguée). … Organiser les étapes et la segmentation des différentes commandes d’écriture (synopsis, traitement, séquencier) pour aboutir au scénario (continuité dialoguée). … Conceptualiser le sujet d’un scénario de fiction longue, en déterminant une histoire, un genre, un univers esthétique et un angle singulier, afin d’élaborer un projet original au regard de la production cinématographique et audiovisuelle existante. … Déterminer la méthodologie de recherche la plus adaptée à un projet d’écriture de scénario, selon son sujet et son contexte, en répertoriant et hiérarchisant les sources d’informations potentielles, afin d’optimiser la pertinence de celles-ci. … S’imprégner d’univers en lien avec un projet de scénario de fiction, au moyen d’enquêtes de terrain, d’entretiens, de repérages, d’observations et d’analyses portant sur des personnes, situations, milieux, codes sociaux, lieux ; afin de pouvoir retranscrire ces univers de façon réaliste et crédible au sein du projet en question. … Collecter des éléments bibliographiques, filmographiques et iconographiques pour préciser l’univers visuel et sonore d’une fiction, et enrichir l’histoire et les personnages. … Identifier les films, séries ou autres œuvres portant sur le thème du projet, afin de veiller à l’originalité de son propre scénario. … Se représenter les implications dramatiques de changements demandés, en imaginant des solutions, pour faire des propositions de réécriture de différents éléments d’un scénario de fiction. … Le scénariste doit être apte à travailler sur plusieurs projets simultanément, dans une temporalité souvent longue pour le cinéma, plus courte pour la télévision et la série. … Remettre en question son approche d’un scénario de fiction et les choix correspondant, à la suite de retours de collaborateurs artistiques et/ou financiers, pour envisager l’évolution de l’écriture du scénario dans une nouvelle version. … Préconiser des pistes de réécriture d’un scénario, sous format d’un livrable comprenant le résumé et l’analyse du scénario ainsi que les propositions d’amélioration, afin de les transmettre à l’auteur … Présenter l’histoire et les intentions d’un scénario de fiction dans un pitch oral, en mettant en valeur les lignes de force et la singularité du projet, pour communiquer instantanément les atouts du projet et susciter l’intérêt d’un partenaire potentiel. … Construire et entretenir un réseau professionnel de producteurs, réalisateurs, directeurs de collection, agents et diffuseurs (cinéma, télévision, plateformes…), pour optimiser ses opportunités de commandes d’écriture et de contrats d’auteur. … Identifier les différentes sources de financements de l’écriture cinématographique et les structures d’accompagnement (commissions d’aides et/ou résidences d’écriture) correspondant à un projet de scénario, afin d’établir un plan d’actions de recherche de financements. … Réaliser une première estimation du budget d’un projet de fiction cinématographique ou audiovisuelle, en évaluant les coûts générés par les contraintes de production, pour vérifier sa faisabilité financière et adapter les orientations prises, le cas échéant. … Vérifier la disponibilité et les coûts de droits d’auteur, en cas d’adaptation cinématographique ou audiovisuelle d’une œuvre littéraire ou lyrique préexistante pour obtenir les autorisations nécessaires et évaluer l'incidence budgétaire.

sources.title: What Our Readers Look For - Austin Film Festival
sources.said: STEREOTYPICAL CHARACTERS – This is an epidemic of having underdeveloped characters. … Inconsistency in tone can really confuse a reader and really question what kind of story the writer is trying to tell. … Scenes in a story need to have urgency and ultimately help move the story along to the next scene and so on and so on. … READS LIKE A NOVEL AND TOO MANY “UNFILMABLES” – Scripts need to be written in a visual way that can translate to film, television, and the stage. … WHERE’S THE CONFLICT? – Conflict is what keeps a story engaging and pushes it forward. … Audiences don’t want to be spoon fed emotions; they want to feel them organically through visuals, action, and subtext. … Is there a strong, distinctive voice? … Even if it has impeccable structure but doesn’t have the most compelling story and follows the standard formula, the script may not necessarily showcase the writer’s original voice or present a unique perspective. … At AFF, story comes first and foremost above all else. … Does the script at least serve as a strong writing sample that showcases the writer’s talent? … Do you get lost in the story (in a good way) and forget you’re reading a script? … Does it rise above the expectations for the genre or other similar stories? … Does it have at least one strong element that makes the script truly stand out? (Strong dialogue, memorable characters, scene descriptions provide a rich texture and distinctive voice, etc.) … THE STORY BEGINS TOO LATE – Stories don’t begin on page 1 of a script; it truly revs into motion when we reach the inciting incident. … Every story needs to build to a climax with a satisfying ending. … POOR FORMATTING – Incorrect sluglines or lack of any sluglines, not capitalizing character’s names when they are first introduced, and incorrect line spacing and margins are among many possible formatting errors.

sources.title: USC Cinematic Arts | Learning Objectives
sources.said: Proficient in the creation of compelling characters that have a strong emotional core that universally speaks to the human condition. Specialization in the development of characters and inter-personal relationships within the story. … Understanding of the core fundamentals in writing visually for a screen including character, world, theme, tone, atmosphere, subtext, and plot. … Proficient in the creation and development of unique and original worlds that function within the working structure of the screenplay with thematic unity. … Understanding the many formats of television as well as how to create an original television pilot in half-hour or hour-long formats with strict adherence to engine, characters, and world. … Advanced emphasis of economy of words and efficiency in developing compelling characters, inter-personal relationships within the story, and multiple storylines in a concise format. … Knowledge of how to access the student’s emotional core to better understand the world of performance as they learn to inhabit the roles of created characters. … In-depth understanding and confidence in their creative voice. … A broad knowledge in physical production including camera work, set design, lighting, editing, directing, and producing. … A broad knowledge of the history of cinema including a canon of work in both film and television that students can reference in their writing. … Understanding the business of motion pictures, television, and online industry as it relates to the student's portfolio of work. … Knowledge of the production aspect of an original half-hour or hour-long television show including working with actors, rewrites, collaboration, physical production, editing, set design, and conflict resolution. … Ability to use analytical and critical thinking to deconstruct the elements of successful story in a contained episode or motion picture screenplay.

sources.title: Scénariste | CPNEF de l'audiovisuel
sources.said: Rechercher et analyser des informations pour alimenter la construction d'un sujet … L'élaboration d'un sujet consiste à rechercher et analyser des documentations, mener des entretiens et des observations en lien avec l'idée, puis à déterminer l'angle du sujet. … Construire une intrigue et la développer, notamment en rédigeant des dialogues … La rédaction du synopsis consiste à décrire les éléments principaux relatifs aux personnages, à l'histoire et aux temps forts du film et/ou du programme audiovisuel. … Imaginer un projet en langage visuel et sonore … Enfin la rédaction de la continuité dialoguée, appelée aussi scénario dialogué, consiste à présenter l'histoire en une suite ordonnée de scènes numérotées et dialoguées, formant le scénario complet. … La rédaction de la bible pour les séries consiste à écrire un document de promotion qui décrit le projet dramatique et notamment les prémisses des personnages principaux, leurs éventuelles évolutions dans la saison et des exemples-types d'intrigues. … La rédaction du traitement (synopsis détaillé) consiste à décrire l'histoire et la narration de manière linéaire et détaillée, avant son découpage en séquences … La rédaction du séquencier consiste en un enchaînement ordonné des séquences qui composent le scénario sous forme d'un résumé sans dialogue, formant la construction dramatique de l'histoire. … La rédaction de la note d'intention consiste à argumenter le projet. … La rédaction du pitch consiste à présenter succinctement le concept et la nature du projet. … Élaborer le concept d'un film et/ou d'un programme audiovisuel en anticipant les contraintes de production. … Dégager une thématique et déterminer l'univers du sujet. … Ecrire un scénario original et respectant les attentes et sources.title: What’s My Job as a Staff Writer?
sources.said: Don't show up late, even if everyone else does. Do be enthusiastic and grateful to be there. Don't suck the energy out of the room with negativity. … Since every writers’ room is unique, with its own unspoken rules and dynamics, part of your job is to figure out how to navigate it. … Do your research about the showrunner and get to know their voice.

sources.title: WGAW Screenwriters Handbook (updated November 2025)
sources.said: If a particular note doesn’t work, be respectful and carefully explain why it didn’t work. Don’t be defensive and don’t feel like you have to solve everything during a notes meeting. Listen and ask for clarification, then take some time to come up with comprehensive solutions. … As is the case with any professional relationship, open communication is vitally important. Be realistic with your timelines, try to keep producers and executives updated throughout your writing process, be honest and straightforward when things aren’t working … Remember, being a writer is a lot like being a doctor. Your patient will tell you what’s bothering them, but it’s up to you to figure out what’s really causing the problem and how best to treat it. … Don’t ever feel like you have to be a rubber stamp for someone else’s creative agenda. … Come prepared. Make sure to read the screenplay or the prompts for the mini-room to ensure you’re clear on the specific goals for the session. … Try to maintain professional relationships and don’t burn any bridges. That way, executives and producers will be inclined to hire you on future projects. … Research the company and executives you’re meeting beforehand, be pleasant and professional, see if you click creatively, and try your best to be seen as someone collaborative who’d be fun to work with. … It’s your responsibility to properly communicate what you need and what you expect to be done on your behalf.

sources.said: During the development/pilot phase, the producer may conceive of the program’s concept or format and pitches the project to networks and/or distributors. … select the pilot’s writer(s) and conceives of, or helps to create, a series “bible.” … During the production phase, the producer may select key members of the creative team, approve all storylines and scripts, participate in all department meetings … supervise and approve the programming budget … contact with the Production Company, network, studio and/or distributor … supervise and approve all location scouting and the selection of both stage and production facilities as well as vendors … They may also select the director, principal cast and other members of the producing team … view the dailies as well as the director’s cut, participate in the approval of the final cut of each episode … offer general supervision of the day-to-day operations of the shooting company as well as all talent and crafts … particularly where a showrunner guides a successful series in its initial season(s), creating crucial templates for later seasons to follow. … During the post-production/delivery phase, the producer may serve as the primary point-of-contact for delivery requirement issues, including final cuts, release dates and standards and practices … select or approve the choice of post-production facilities and negotiate any deals for their use … provide ongoing consultation regarding the marketing of the program … they must demonstrate a significant and dedicated commitment of time and resources to the production of the series or special beyond and in addition to their duties as an executive/employee. … The PGA may take special notice of any Participant who hinders the production process through unwelcomed intrusion into aspects of the process outside … their appropriate responsibilities. Should the PGA determine that a Participant has engaged in such detrimental behavior, it may, at its discretion, choose to deny awards eligibility to that Participant. … A Participant may not withhold or misstate information material to the eligibility determination process or materially interfere with the PGA’s efforts to gather accurate and confidential information. … supervise or approve the use of sound materials (including music, effects, and ADR)

sources.title: Producing Credits for Episodic Television (Scripted) | Producers Guild - Producers Guild (PGA Code of Credits, as of 9/24/2024)
sources.said: A Producer in a creative producing role from ideation & pitch through all phases of production and/or responsible for packaging and selling the series to the network or studio. … A person responsible for the creation of the series, including its concept, format and characters. … The Line Producer (or “Produced By”) reports directly to the Executive Producer and has the primary responsibility for the budget and logistics of the scripted series production, from pre-production through delivery of each episode. … Showrunner (or Co-Showrunner) which has overall creative authority and management responsibility for the entire scripted series. … The Co-Executive Producer reports directly to the Executive Producer, from whom the Co-Executive Producer assumes direct supervisory responsibilities for above and below-the-line operations.

sources.title: Fiction Producing Lab - Film Independent

sources.title: PRODUCING: Curriculum | AFI CONSERVATORY (First and Second Year course descriptions), read 2026-10-31
sources.said: The practical aspect of the class involves writing log lines, creating a writer’s list, reviewing and critiquing screenplays, and introducing the fellow to the basic skill of pitching. … The lectures will delve into learning how to pitch as a team, the evolving changes in pitching strategies, the importance of concept in a pitch, as well as creating visual materials to use in various pitching forums. … The instruction includes modules on securing intellectual property rights (i.e., books, articles, etc.), above-the-line talent deals (actors, director, producer, writers, etc.), financing structures, distribution models (both traditional and next-gen), and various in-class negotiation exercises. … The Portfolio is a requirement for graduation and should reflect the Fellow’s skill, taste and understanding of the market. … In individual meetings, the Producing Discipline Head will discuss the Fellow’s growth over the past year and provide constructive direction to succeed in second-year curriculum and their thesis projects, while also building a slate of projects to shape their futures as producers. … The course examines the question of how to choose and work with a writer and the creative collaboration that follows. … With the benefit of classroom instruction and individual meetings with Faculty, each Producing Fellow prepares a Producing Portfolio demonstrating his or her ability to identify and present material for at least two projects. … In a combination of individual and group sessions which strengthen storytelling and writing skills, Producers and Directors initiate and develop a compelling and viable story that they control. … Key areas that are explored include the basics of business affairs (ownership and copyright, rights agreements); talent and key crew agreements; learning how to raise film financing; examining financial streams from a global perspective, from crowdfunding to foreign pre-sales and equity; … By dissecting the rapidly changing landscape, learning both from the past and the present, Fellows will gain an understanding of how the industry’s business models have evolved and how the economic viability of a project is determined. … Expanding on Boot Camp fundamentals, Fellows will develop production-ready budgets and schedules; learn how to secure locations and navigate FilmLA; understand how to complete required paperwork, permits, contracts, and deliverables; and manage creative teams while protecting story and vision. … Topics will include budgeting and scheduling feature-length films, evaluating film incentives and how to choose a shooting location, understanding the ins-and-outs of working with unions, setting up an LLC and tax preparation, how to run payroll, and reading cost reports. … Fellows will be exposed to financing waterfalls and distribution profit participation statements to understand how money flows once a film is released and how a financier recoups their investment. … Fellows will develop foundational skills in television-specific budgeting and scheduling, production management, and coordination across departments for multi-episode storytelling. … Accepted Fellows produce a look book based around their pilots written for SCR 631 & 632 and preside over a table read, tone meeting and production meeting in a workshop environment intended to emulate the writers room experience. … Fellows will learn the strategies and tactics of a film’s release including positioning, creative assets, audience identification, marketing, publicity, and distribution. … The course also builds marketplace literacy, guiding Fellows to identify television buyers across broadcast, cable, and streaming platforms and understand the types of projects those buyers are seeking. … This course is dedicated to the fundamentals of film financing and distribution covering topics such as private equity, foreign sales, distribution windowing, film festivals and markets, and who the players are in these spaces. … Producers must understand the writing process and develop a facility in the arena of story to evolve a shared vocabulary with creative collaborators. … A Producer who doesn’t understand the Post process is less able to help manage the process. … It is the culmination of the AFI Conservatory experience and demonstrates the Producer’s ability to work independently, incorporate feedback, refine concepts and assemble a professional presentation. … Producing Fellows will read unproduced film and television treatments and scripts with considered analysis, verbally present and discuss critical insights in a group setting, and synthesize their feedback and in-class discussions into follow-up written notes. … One of the first and most important practical skills an effective producer must possess and cultivate is the ability to carefully read, thoughtfully consider, and constructively critique screenplays and related materials to further their creative development. … Fellows will learn to manage writers’ rooms, support showrunners, and balance story development with production feasibility. … This course unpacks the story and craft logic of scenes and sequences from contemporary feature films, shorts and TV in order to give filmmakers a wider vocabulary and set of tools to develop the voice and vision of stories and deepen their professional practice.

sources.title: RNCP42775 - Grade_Master - Production audiovisuelle (certificateur: Institut National de l'audiovisuel), état Active, France compétences, read 2026-10-31
sources.said: Présenter - “pitcher”- un projet audiovisuel, pour convaincre de potentiels partenaires (diffuseurs, coproducteurs, distributeurs, financeurs) de s'engager dans le projet … Croiser exigences créatives, ressources nécessaires, partenaires potentiels et publics visés afin d'évaluer la viabilité technique et financière du projet. … Définir sa stratégie de production et construire le dossier de production en rédigeant les différentes pièces qui le composent en vue de sa présentation aux partenaires potentiels. … Construire une stratégie de développement et de pérennisation de l'entreprise en développant un portefeuille de projets et en mettant à profit les outils de pilotage budgétaire pour assurer la viabilité et la rentabilité de l'activité. … Analyser un scénario en dégageant ses forces et ses faiblesses pour identifier les réécritures à initier et accompagner l'auteur dans les différentes phases du développement du projet … Lire un projet audiovisuel d'un point de vue artistique en mobilisant sa culture générale pour estimer sa singularité et son potentiel. … Sur la base de l’analyse des partis pris esthétique et technique et du dépouillement du scénario, établir un devis prévisionnel tenant compte des financements envisagés. … Solliciter les différents guichets de financement et /ou partenaires potentiels pour obtenir les moyens nécessaires. … Sur la base des coûts prévisionnels du projet, définir sa stratégie de production pour construire son plan de financement … Recruter les chefs de poste et les prestataires pour affiner avec eux les hypothèses de fabrication en prenant en compte l'impact écologique du projet afin de valider les coûts envisagés. … Sur la base du devis validé et des engagements pris avec les différents partenaires, planifier les étapes de fabrication du projet en collaboration avec les équipes de production, pour livrer le projet conformément aux attendus et dans les délais prévus. … Organiser la sortie d’une œuvre audiovisuelle et sa promotion, en lien avec les différents partenaires en vue d’assurer sa visibilité et de lui faire rencontrer son public. … Sur la base du/des public(s) cible(s) et du positionnement dans le paysage audiovisuel, définir les conditions juridiques et économiques d’exploitation de l'œuvre avec les ayants droit en vue de sa diffusion dans les différents circuits d’exploitation. … Assurer la direction et la supervision du travail des différentes équipes, en veillant au respect du droit du travail et des conventions qui régissent le secteur, pour mettre en œuvre le projet. … Communiquer à des fins de formation ou de transfert de connaissances, par oral et par écrit, en français et dans au moins une langue étrangère … Gérer des contextes professionnels ou d’études complexes, imprévisibles et qui nécessitent des approches stratégiques nouvelles … Respecter les principes d’éthique, de déontologie et de responsabilité sociale et environnementale … Prendre en compte la problématique du handicap et de l'accessibilité dans chacune de ses actions professionnelles … Définir et négocier avec les différents partenaires financiers le cadre et le périmètre de la collaboration afin de contractualiser dans l'intérêt du projet et le respect de la réglementation en vigueur … Mettre en œuvre un management responsable articulant obligations d’employeur, qualité de vie au travail et communication interne pour fédérer une équipe autour d'un projet commun. … Mettre en place des processus de travail permettant la bonne information des équipes, un climat d'écoute, pour prévenir les conflits, les VHSS et faciliter la réalisation du projet audiovisuel. … Définir et structurer l’organisation administrative, juridique et financière pour créer et gérer une entreprise de production en conformité avec le cadre juridique et réglementaire. … Définir la stratégie éditoriale et économique de l'entreprise de production et son positionnement dans le paysage audiovisuel pour s'assurer de la faisabilité du projet.

sources.title: Producers Program (MFA) | UCLA School of Theater, Film, and Television, read 2026-10-31
sources.said: In the spring quarter of their first year, students will pitch a slate of at least three projects to a panel of industry professionals. … Students also may take courses that take a comprehensive look into the independent film world, what it is like to be a showrunner for a television series, feature film marketing, how to develop television projects from IP, intellectual property and film festival strategies. … Having optioned a screenplay or teleplay at the end of their first year, students will further develop that project and design a financing strategy that is realistic in the contemporary marketplace. … Students also learn the basics of producing: from inception of an idea through development, procuring talent and financing to planning and executing a production to marketing and distribution of the final product. … A feature project consists of an optioned screenplay that the student will further develop with the screenwriter and a comprehensive strategy that discusses how to package, finance, budget, market and distribute the project. … In addition to Introduction to Producing series, students in their first year also take lecture and seminar courses dealing with a variety of topics, including feature film and television development, studio and network management, production planning/budgeting, entertainment law and business negotiations, international financing and distribution, film festival strategies and the new CMS Common Course taken by all MFA students in the school of Film, Television and Digital Media. … This way, producing students can meet their classmates from the other TFT programs and start building a professional network in the classroom. … The student assists the director in realizing their creative vision and manages physical production. … Producers have to be able to conceptualize and oversee the entire life cycle of a creative project, and the Producers Program’s curriculum reflects just that.

sources.said: Development. Developing the film’s concept, securing rights and initial funding, selecting the writer, and guiding the development process. … direct responsibility for hiring, or causing the Production Company to hire, one or more writers who retain any form of writing credit on the finished Motion Picture … Director personally was involved with the project prior to all other producers, or created, identified, or secured the intellectual property on which the project was based. … Director personally resurrected an otherwise stagnant project, or significantly reimagined the script or production, before the film was greenlit or the financing was obtained. … Director personally secured a critical element of the film, such as writer(s), key cast member(s), or financing before the film was greenlit or a majority of the financing was obtained. … Writer personally secured a critical element of the film, such as director, key cast member(s), or financing before the film was greenlit or a majority of the financing was obtained. … consulting on and approving costumes, make-up, and hair; viewing and commenting on dailies; and consulting on the edit. … whether such decisions extended beyond oversight of financing into detailed management of the budget throughout the production in service of creation of the Motion Picture. … Production. Overseeing daily operations, consulting with and resolving issues raised by the key physical production and creative staff, and liaising with financial, studio and/or distribution partners. … Pre-production. Selecting key creative and physical production team members, location scouting, and overseeing the final script, final schedule, and final budget. … selecting and approving principle cast and crew (e.g., director, cinematographer, editor) … responsibility for overseeing digital effects work may be weighed more heavily on a production with a higher proportion of special effects shots … Post-production & Marketing. Engaging closely with post-production teams and strategizing on marketing and distribution. … consulting on the overall edit with the director, editor, studio, etc. … Producers Mark Standard. Performance of a major portion of the producing functions on the Motion Picture in a decision-making capacity. … The Produced By credit applies to individuals primarily responsible for the origination and/or management of a Motion Picture’s production and delivery. … This role involves personally making regular, continuous, and substantial decisions regarding creative, production, budgetary, and legal concerns in a constructive and responsible manner across the film’s four stages of production. … Director demonstrated that they personally made regular, continuous, and substantial decisions regarding production, budgetary, and legal concerns in a constructive and responsible manner. … a significant and dedicated commitment to production of the Motion Picture that goes beyond safeguarding the financing … To be eligible for the Producers Mark, the producer should always place what is best for the production above all other considerations. … The Panel may take special notice of any credited Produced By who hinders the filmmaking process through unwelcomed intrusion into aspects of the process outside their appropriate responsibilities or through the creation of an inhospitable work environment. … A Produced By seeking awards eligibility may not knowingly withhold or misstate information material to the certification process … the effectiveness (or ineffectiveness) of each Produced By’s contributions. … any specific or unique contributions made by a Produced By that had a significant impact on the production (i.e. cultural/qualitative contributions that shaped the film) … a Produced By’s efforts to promote respect, safety, diversity, equity, and inclusion within the hiring process and throughout the making of the film.

sources.title: Producing Credits for Feature Films | Producers Guild - Producers Guild (PGA Code of Credits, as of 9/24/2024)
sources.said: Development: Developing the film's concept, securing rights and initial funding, selecting the writer, and guiding the development process. … Making a significant contribution to the development of the literary property, typically including the securement of the underlying rights to the material on which the feature film is based. … Being an advocate or champion during the early production phases by lending their expertise, counsel, influence, and resources in service towards the legitimacy and manifestation of the production, and securing financing during those early phases (i.e., ideation, development, pre-production), assuming risk prior to the attraction of financing entities during later phases of the production; AND … The financing secured is an essential portion (no less than 25%); -AND/OR- … The Line Producer/Co-Producer is the single individual who has the primary responsibility for the budget and logistics of the feature film's production, from pre-production through completion of production. … Pre-production: Selecting key creative and physical production team members, location scouting, and overseeing the final script, final schedule, and final budget. … The "Produced By" credit applies to individuals primarily responsible for the origination and/or management of a motion picture's production and delivery. … This role involves personally making regular, continuous, and substantial decisions regarding creative, production, budgetary, and legal concerns in a constructive and responsible manner across the film’s four stages of production. … the individual receiving Producer credit has the primary responsibility for ensuring that the creative vision of the primary producing Executive Producer and Director are faithfully executed within the approved budgetary parameters. … the credit of Co-Executive Producer is given only in rare or unique circumstances to an individual who reports directly to and works directly with the primary producing Executive Producer, assuming direct supervisory responsibilities for significant producing functions, encompassing both above and below the line operations.

sources.title: Producers Program - sundance.org (2027 Feature and Documentary Producers Track guidelines and FAQs)
sources.said: Candidates must have a legal agreement in place through which they control the project (e.g. an option, attachment, or shopping agreement). … Recognizing the crucial role that independent producers play in finding, shaping, and championing original filmmaking voices, the Sundance Institute Producers Program supports both fiction and nonfiction producers at all stages of their feature-length projects and their careers. … Through a year-round continuum of support — including grants, labs, fellowships, networking events, funding, and educational resource opportunities — producers are given the opportunity to build community with fellow producers and industry members, hone creative skills, gain additional knowledge of the field, and develop strategies for pitching, producing, financing, and releasing their films. … The program is designed to hone emerging producers’ creative instincts and evolve their communication and problem-solving skills at all stages of their next feature film. … Candidates must possess a distinct cinematic vision. … Some things to think about while applying to any of our programs include your personal connection to the material, why you are passionate about this particular story, how you intend to realize the project creatively and logistically, and the impact you hope to have on audiences. … The program is designed to hone emerging producers’ creative instincts and evolve their communicating and problem-solving skills at all stages of their next feature-length fiction or documentary film project. … You will be asked to answer a series of seven essay questions that will allow us to better understand your point of view as a producer and also why you want to make the project you are applying with. … Candidates must exemplify intention to evolve their producing practice as a lead nonfiction producer beyond the project they are applying with. … While the specific criteria for participation differs across our various programs, we are seeking passionate, bold, risk-taking, and creatively rigorous artists for all of our initiatives. … The lab is designed, in part, to focus on your creative input and communication with your director and screenwriter on your project, starting from the project development stage. … Candidates must be actively pursuing relationships with U.S. entities (funders, entries.sought: How a screenwriter's attributes make the quality of a script, how long a draft takes, how far a revision carries it, and how fast doing the work raises the attributes
entries.why: What stands on sources is theirs: the facets each attribute is made of and the readers who grade each (R-4607); a feature's eight weeks and an episode's 2.4, a rewrite's and a polish's share of a draft's time and what each may change (the MBA), the Black List's weights, the overall's place between the weakest and strongest component, its score spread and its readers' agreement, and two decades to professional skill (R-4608). No source gives how much a writer's level in an attribute makes of a facet, the spread of a draft at a level, a pilot's or a short's writing time, how far a revision carries, or how far off a writer's own read is: the game reckons those, so that a writer at 100 throughout writes at the top of every reader's scale and lower levels correspondingly worse (a writer at 53 averaging the Black List's 5.74), balanced later at the owner's word, and the player is told the reckoning is the game's own.

value.facetMix: 60% the part's attribute, 25% Writing, 15% the attributes a source ties to the facet (Innovation and Research where their own facets name the part); 70/30 where none is tied
value.processFacets: an attribute's facet 75% the attribute, 25% the attributes a source ties to it
value.rushed: a draft given part of its days keeps 40% to 70% of the shortfall's worth by Perseverance
value.pilotAndShortDays: 12.6 and 10 at the top (no source; R-4608 blockers)
value.slowest: twice the top's days at 0 in Writing and Time Management
value.revisionReach: 30% to 80% by Revision, toward the writer's level plus 5; Taking Notes keeping 50% to 100% of the work on the noted facets
value.ownRead: off by up to 20 points, by Story Critique (70%) and Critical Thinking (30%)
value.tasteFitted: a read's lenience 0.75, each criterion 0.6, the overall's residual 0.4, on the 1 to 10 scale, fitted to the Black List's agreement (R-4608)
value.overallBlend: half the weighted components, half their place 0.38 from the weakest
value.growthReading: Kellogg's two decades read as 10 to 80 over twenty years of daily work

entries.sought: How a solo screenwriter's attributes that work with people decide a script's documents, the contacts networking makes, the requests to read a script sent out, and a pitch's sale
entries.why: What stands on sources is theirs: the WGA's minimums (R-4241); the studios reading nothing unsolicited, cold queries' 1 to 2% read requests, a third of the specs taken out selling (2012), the treatment step's 6.1 weeks (R-4608); the facets of the attributes that work with people (R-4607). No source gives how likely a day's networking makes a contact, a contact asks to read or a meeting of a given skill sells: the game reckons those, balanced later at the owner's word, and the player is told the reckoning is the game's own.

value.contactADay: 5% for a writer at 0 to 50% at 100, by Networking 60%, Speaking 20%, Social Perceptiveness 20%
value.warmRequest: 0.4 x (0.5 to 1.5 by Promotion and the best query document) x (50% to 100% by the script's grade)
value.coldRequestScale: the sourced 1.5% times the same 0.5 to 1.5
value.sale: the sourced third at a script of 75 and a middling meeting, by the script's quality squared and 0.5 to 1.5 by the meeting (Pitching 50%, Speaking 20%, Persuasion 20%, the best pitch document 10%)
value.documentDays: logline 1, short synopsis 1, one-page 2, outline 5, scene breakdown 10, series bible 14, pitch document 3, statement of intent 1, scriptment 21 at the top (no source)

sources.title: Judging Procedure | PAGE International Screenwriting Awards: Screenplay Contests
sources.said: CHARACTERS: Personalities that are distinctive, compelling, multi-layered, and unpredictable. … A protagonist and antagonist with clear and active goals. … PACING: The timing of the action, unfolding of plot elements, and pace of character development. … DIALOGUE: Voices that are natural, succinct, and unique to each character. … Use of language that effectively reveals character and moves the story forward. … STRUCTURE: The framework of the script. Effective use of three-act (most common), odyssey, linear, or non-linear story progression. … PLOT: The actions, events, conflicts, and turning points that propel the story forward. … How the story unfolds (points for originality/unpredictability). … THEME: The underlying message of the story as revealed through plot, dialogue, and visual elements. … PREMISE/CONCEPT: The idea behind the story. What the movie is about. The “hook.” … STYLE/TONE: Overall quality of the writing. Tone that is appropriate to the material and narrative that is distinct, cinematic, and effectively conveys the mood or “feel” of the movie. … narrative that is distinct, cinematic, and effectively conveys the mood or “feel” of the movie. … PRESENTATION : Standard spec screenplay or teleplay format (12 pt. Courier font, correct margins, etc.), as well as spelling, punctuation, grammar, and usage. … Standard spec screenplay or teleplay format (12 pt. sources.title: How do the Nicholl Fellowships in Screenwriting readers judge a script?
sources.said: Does this script have vivid characters who each speak in their own voice? … Do you want to know what happens to them? … Do the main characters take actions that move the story along? … Are these actions in keeping with who these people are? Or do they happen “conveniently”? … Does the central character change over the course of the story? If it’s an ensemble film, does more than one character change? … Does this writer know how to use description and dialogue to create suspense, tension, drama, comedy and conflict? … Do the dialogue and tone seem consistent from scene to scene? … Does the way the people speak fit the tone and setting of the story? … Does the story itself have a strong beginning, middle & end? How about two out of three? If the story is non-linear, does it make sense? … Does the conflict propel the story forward? … Does this writer know how to use description and dialogue to create suspense, tension, drama, comedy and conflict? Does the conflict propel the story forward? … Are the premise, story and characters new or fresh for you? … Does the script have a distinctive and original voice? (Or do you feel that you’ve read or seen this movie before?) Are the premise, story and characters new or fresh for you? … Does this script make you feel that the writer is taking you on a journey? … Does this script genuinely make you want to keep reading? … Are the themes of the story thought-provoking, across genres? Is the story “about something” that might spark discussion among friends? … Does that story idea start the movie forward? … Does the story have an original premise? … Does the script have a distinctive and original voice? (Or do you feel that you’ve read or seen this movie before?)

sources.title: Screenplay Format, by Matt Carless (BBC Writers, standard format for films and single TV drama)

sources.title: An 8+ Score Is Rare (As It Should Be.) (The Black List, 2026-03-06)
sources.said: What that means for the rest of us is that the most common score for a film evaluation on the Black List is a 6. It accounts for 38.0% of all evaluations. Add in the 5s (24.4%) and the 7s (20.9%), and those three scores alone make up 83.3% of everything our readers have ever scored. The mean is 5.74. The median is 6. … Now look at the right tail of the chart: An 8 accounts for 3.5% of all film evaluations. A 9 is 0.3%. A 10 is one evaluation in every 9,261. Combined, scores of 8 or above represent 3.8% of all film evaluations we have ever conducted. Out of 92,613 reads, 3,553 resulted in an 8 or higher. … The mean is 5.66 — slightly lower than film — and the median is the same: 6. The distribution is a touch wider (standard deviation of 1.19 vs. 1.14 for film), meaning television scores are spread out slightly more at both ends. … At the right tail: 4.7% of film projects and 4.8% of television projects have an 8 as their highest score. Add in 9s and 10s, and 5.3% of all projects in both formats have ever received a single evaluation of 8 or above. That’s roughly one in nineteen. … Drama leads in both mean score (5.83) and 8+ rate (5.1%), followed closely by Mystery & Suspense (5.77, 3.6%). … A project that scores a 6 on its first read has an 84.1% chance of landing within one point on its next one. … Combined, scores of 8 or above represent 3.8% of all film evaluations we have ever conducted. Out of 92,613 reads, 3,553 resulted in an 8 or higher. … The 8+ rate for television is 4.2%, modestly higher than film’s 3.8%. … Add in 9s and 10s, and 5.3% of all projects in both formats have ever received a single evaluation of 8 or above. … This is why we promote every 8+ score to our industry members via email and social media, and why every evaluation that receives an 8+ overall score results in that project being offered a month of free hosting and two free evaluations.

How Consistent Are Black List Evaluations? (The Black List, 2026-02-18)
sources.said: When two Black List readers independently evaluate the same screenplay, they score it within one point of each other on overall quality 73.8% of the time. For television pilots, it’s 74.1%. … 30% of the time, they give the exact same score. Another 44% differ by exactly one point. A 6 and a 7. A 5 and a 6. … A two-point gap — a 5 and a 7, for example — happens about 19% of the time. Three points, about 5.5%. Four or more points: 1.5%. … The Black List’s reliability coefficients are 0.290 for film and 0.366 for television — at or above the average across published peer review studies. … After a single evaluation, the “true” score — the average you’d get if dozens of qualified readers evaluated the same script — falls within one point of your score about 75% of the time.3 After two evaluations averaged together, that range tightens to about 0.6 points. After three, about 0.4. After four, about 0.25. … For film, the third score falls within the range set by the first two reads 83.5% of the time. For television, 82.0%. … which is also why if a writer receives two successive evaluations that differ by 3 or more points on overall quality, we offer the next evaluation at a significant discount, the exact price we pay our readers.

sources.title: The Anatomy of a Score - Part 1 (The Black List, 2026-03-24)
sources.said: That overall score agreement rate is actually higher than for any individual dimension — premise (70.5%), setting (69.9%), characters (65.9%), plot (65.4%), and dialogue (65.2%) all show more reader-to-reader disagreement than overall does. … The five sub-scores explain 89% of the variance in overall scores. That number is the same for both film (R² = 0.886) and television (R² = 0.890). … In film, characters (23.4%) outweigh dialogue (21.9%). In television, dialogue (22.6%) outweighs characters (19.9%). … Premise accounts for about 13% of the explained variance in both formats. … Setting contributes the least — 10.2% in film, 12.2% in television. … Plot is the dimension most strongly tied to overall score. Its correlation is 0.85 in both film and television — higher than any other dimension. Characters (0.83 film, 0.82 TV) and dialogue (0.81 in both) are close behind. Premise (0.71) and setting (0.72 film, 0.73 TV) sit noticeably lower.
