sources.said: Film under denne overenskomst omfatter fiktionsproduktioner med en varighed på 75 minutter eller derover, som er beregnet for biografdistribution (spillefilm) … De af organisationerne udarbejdede standardkontrakter skal benyttes. … Nærværende overenskomst træder i kraft den 1. januar 1996. … Pr. 1. januar 1998 og hver efterfølgende 1. januar, så længe overenskomsten er i kraft, reguleres minimumshonorarernet med 2,5%, dog at der sker regulering efter nettoprisindekset … Overenskomsten kan opsiges med 6 måneders varsel til udløb ved et kalenderårs udgang … vederlaget for adaptation andrager 3/5 af det i overenskomsten anførte mindstevederlag … Ved indgåelse af aftalen betales 50% af beløbet. De resterende 50% forfalder ved aflevering af synopsis. … Producenten skal være berettiget til én revision af treatment uden yderligere vederlag til forfatteren. … Producenten er berettiget til to revisioner af det endelige manuskript uden yderligere vederlag til manuskriptforfatteren. … skal producenten til manuskriptforfatteren erlægge en royalty på 5% - ved adaptation 3% - når indtægterne har dækket den af producenten investerede kapital … bekræfte antagelse eller meddele afslag inden for den i standardkontrakten fastsatte frist, der højst kan være 3 måneder regnet fra aflevering af synopsis. … bekræfte antagelse eller meddele afslag af dette senest 3 måneder efter modtagelsen. … overdrager manuskriptforfatteren til producenten indspilningsretten til manuskriptet i 5 år, med mindre en længere periode er angivet i standardkontrakten. … Såfremt producenten ikke udnytter indspilningsretten inden for den i stk. 1 nævnte periode, tilbagefalder samtlige rettigheder til manuskriptforfatteren … Producenten har ret til i 20 år efter filmens biografpremiere at foretage en genindspilning på grundlag af manuskriptet. sources.title: ALMA, Convenio colectivo (página del sindicato)
sources.said: Se aplican a guionistas con contrato laboral, es decir, que trabajan por cuenta ajena. … Porque el propio Convenio al que se incorporan los guionistas es el de «la industria de producción audiovisual» y no contempla ni radio, ni videojuegos. … Están excluidos expresamente porque normalmente no suelen tener una relación laboral (facturan como autónomos) y no les son aplicables las condiciones propias de los rodajes, reguladas por el Convenio. … A pesar de ser el sindicato mayoritario de guionistas, necesitamos que la ley reconozca esta realidad y ser un interlocutor con capacidad de decisión en este convenio colectivo. … Desde este III convenio (abril de 2024), las pagas están calculadas en su importe bruto mensual, incluyendo la prorrata de las dos pagas extras anuales y el complemento de flexibilidad. Por eso ahora esos importes se multiplican por 12 mensualidades. … Según el Convenio la jornada laboral es de 40 horas semanales de trabajo efectivo en cómputo anual … No, es lo mínimo que se puede pagar. El guionista con experiencia o créditos nunca debería cobrar el mínimo del Convenio. … No, sólo a guionistas contratados por cuenta ajena, con contrato laboral y nómina, no a los autónomos. … Hasta que se logren acuerdos con empresas, solo es posible informar de precios medios de mercado.

sources.title: La profesión de guionista en España. Un estudio socioprofesional (UC3M para DAMA y Fundación SGAE, mayo de 2025)

Solo el 17,9 % supera los 60 mil euros al año. … el 54,7 % reside en la Comunidad de Madrid y el 19,8 % en Cataluña. … alternancia lingüística, con los trabajos en televisión en la lengua cooficial mientras que los trabajos en cine han tendido a ser en castellano.

entries.sought: How the game reads the twenty writer markets' research where it leaves a choice: which agreement a script is sold under, how a running time maps to an agreement's listed slots, what a spec sale pays now, how long an option runs.
entries.why: The research gives each agreement's minimums; it doesn't say how a spec script meets them, so these readings are the game's own until the owner rules. The world round (2026-11-01, every country beyond the first markets): The research gives each country's findings; it doesn't say how a spec script meets a wage floor, which kind a genre is, which language a multilingual market's scripts are in, or what a territory engaged on another's terms sells under. These are the game's readings until the owner rules (merge into R-5229's value).

value.writesIn: a script is offered only in a language the writer speaks at C1 or better (the actor's FLUENT level)
value.slots: an agreement listing fees by running time (30, 45, 60 minutes) covers each listed length from the one below it (CA's own rule, '30 minutes or less'); the first from 1 minute; RTL's 22.5-minute sitcom slot as 1 to 22 minutes
value.budgetTiers: a tier's bounds are whole units of the currency; a shared end point ('0.575m' ending one tier and opening the next) goes to the higher tier, except 'up to' tiers (Netflix DE, Pact's £750,000-£2m) which keep it
value.pilot: a pilot is paid as an episode of its running time wherever the agreement sets no pilot rate
value.rtlBudget: RTL's budget tiers read the episode's budget
value.frTv: France's TV writing envelope is paid whole to the solo writer: 3% of the budget (read as the direct costs), at least EUR 27,550 and at most EUR 1.2m an hour, left to negotiation under EUR 600,000 an hour (exempt); no room, original work
value.zdf: ZDF pays its package (buy-out) minimum; its first-fee model's repeat fees aren't modeled
value.ard: ARD's prime-time and early-evening tables are two agreements (de-ard, de-ard-early)
value.sweden: SVT and the producers' agreement pay their group 1 (the game doesn't track the produced works group 2 asks)
value.nrk: NRK's per-minute rights fee is the minimum a sale pays (the solo writer holds all three thirds); its work fee is negotiated
value.heldForPhotography: the share or amount an agreement pays on the first day of photography (RTL 40%, ProSiebenSat.1 50%, Pact features over £2m £4,800) isn't paid by a sale: a script sold isn't shot in the game
value.gbLowerTiers: Pact features of £2m or less pay their £14,000 whole at the sale (the research gives no photography stage for them)
value.dates: the minimum in force is the latest begun by the sale's day; past an agreement's term its last stands; before its first, the offer and the sale are refused
value.optionPrice: Canada's IPA: 5% (features) or 10% (TV) of the script's minimum for the year; Norway's film agreement: 10% of its film-right minimum for the first year; negotiated (no price) where the research's own finding on options says nothing sets it; refused elsewhere, told where its blockers name the option
value.optionLapse: an option lapses at its year's end and the script is back on the market (no film is made of it in the game); it may be offered and optioned or sold again
value.unknownAgreements: Australia's AWG, Japan's guild and Mexico (agreement unknown) refuse a script offered there, telling the player what isn't known. The world round: 188 countries whose research couldn't find whether any agreement, guild rate or law sets a writer's terms, the fees, whether any fund, guild or agreement serves a writer, or whether another country's agreements reach it (blockers fees, terms, none, follows) have one agreement of their own (the lower-case code), all forms, its figures unknown: an offer is refused and told
value.default: a script never offered is sold under the WGA's terms (the US's), as before
value.meeting: a sale's meeting is one day where the market is (MEETING_DAYS, for the permit)
value.follows: a market whose research says a writer there is engaged on another's terms sells under that market's agreements, in its own country (taxed and visited there): BL, GF, MF, PM, YT on France's (fr-film, fr-tv); CC, CX, NF on Australia's (au-awg, unknown, told as Australia's); PR on the US system's (the WGA's). One hop only. GP and RE hold a 'follows' blocker (France's screenwriter agreements cover French-law contracts and name no territory): each has its own agreement, unknown, refused and told.
value.noMarket: no agreement to sell under: AQ, GS, HM, UM (no people), IO (no civilian population), AN and CS (dissolved; their successors' markets stand), JE (the research names no pay agreement or its absence), TH (its blocker is the guild's; told by aboutCountry)
value.none: 22 countries (and Switzerland's series) whose research says no agreement sets a writer's pay (a figure of none, or a place in a figure that is null, or the finding's own words: AT 'No collective agreement sets an Austrian screenwriter's fee', PH 'no guild agreement sets a fee above it', CH TV 'No agreed minimum for documentaries or series') leave it to negotiation
value.dayFloor: Andorra's Llei 46/2022 art. 25.1 names the screenwriter; its floor, the minimum wage a day of 8 hours (EUR 72.40 from 2026-07-01), is paid for each day given to the script (its first draft's and every revision's: Script.days); before 2026-07-01 no minimum is known and the offer is refused
value.kinds: a script's kind, where an agreement sets minimums by kind (Azerbaijan, Switzerland), is its genre's BFI group: Documentary (documentary, nature-documentary, rockumentary, concert-film) a documentary, Animation (animated, anime, isekai) an animation, every other genre fiction
value.azOriginal: Azerbaijan's state-order minimums are read for an original screenplay (the game has no adaptation); a pilot is an episode of a series
value.chDocumentary: Switzerland's fiction feature screenplay minimum is CHF 75,000 from 2025-08-05; a documentary feature has no agreed minimum (negotiated); an animated feature and a short have none set (refused); series are negotiated (ch-tv, none)
value.languages: an agreement's scripts may be written in any of its languages: from the country's own research (the actor's language figure) where it names them (AD ca, AT de, AX sv, AZ az, BA bs hr sr, BE nl fr, BN ms, CH de fr it, FI fi sv, GI en, LI de, PA es, PN en, TZ sw en, UA uk, AI en, AS sm en); the game's own where it doesn't (BW en tn, CL es, MS en, NC fr, PH fil en, SH en, VA it, VG en); an unknown agreement names none
value.minimumWage: a general minimum wage the research gives without its source naming the writer (AI, AS, GI, MS, NC, SH, VG) isn't read as a writer's floor

entries.sought: How the director's engine reads the twenty markets' agreements where the research leaves a reading open
entries.why: The agreements price weeks, months, hours and tiers in their own words; the game counts days and needs one reading of each, told as its own. The world round (2026-11-01, every country beyond the first markets): The new research prices a floor by the hour, day or month, by evaluation levels and seniority steps the game doesn't model, and many files say only that nothing was found; the game needs one reading of each, told as its own.

value.weekDays: 5: a week of the engagement is five of its days (the actor's WEEK_DAYS); the research's weeks of guaranteed prep-and-shoot and cut (DGC Quebec/AQPM) read as 5 days each
value.monthDays: 21 (the actor's UNIT_DAYS.month) unless the agreement says: Virke TV drama 21.67 (its 'monthly rate / 21.67'), Medieföretagen 21 (its '1/21 of monthly pay')
value.engagementDays: prep + shoot + cut; a pay by the week, month or hour is pro rata of the days of the stages it pays
value.qcSeriesGuarantee: DGC Quebec/AQPM's 10 (half-hour) and 18 (hour) guaranteed days read as the episode's prep and shoot together; prep = guarantee - shoot
value.qcSeriesCut: '1 + up to 1' read as 2 days, as the engine reads the DGA's identical clause
value.qcFeaturePeriod: the guaranteed prep-and-shoot weeks are the job's prep and shoot: prep = weeks x 5 - shoot; a shoot longer than the guarantee is refused
value.bvrLowLow: 'low-low budget' read as a budget below EUR 800,000 (the next tier's start)
value.netflixExperienced: the Netflix/BVR/ver.di minimums applied to every director (the rule's 'experienced' isn't defined in the research)
value.nlLevel: the fair-pay start rate at level J, the lower of the director's two levels (J, K), as the least the guideline lets a director be paid; applied only where the job names nl-fair-pay (Film Fund or NPO funding)
value.frFiveMonths: 105 days (5 months of 21) divides the weekly from the monthly minimum
value.arrqPrep: the three prep half-days the recording day includes read as three for the engagement; each further prep half-day paid
value.firstJobCut: 'may be cut up to 25%' (Medieföretagen's first directing job, SVT's first time) read as a minimum of 75% on a director's first job (no earlier film)
value.seCap: Medieföretagen: by the minute from 15 to 73 minutes, the cap above 73
value.years: the director's whole years in the work: since the first film or episode prepped (Virke's seniority tiers)
value.pastTerm: shortcut: past an agreement's term its last amount is kept (SVT's to 2025-03-31, DGC Quebec/AQPM's to 2025-11-30, BR's to 2026-04-30), as person.markets.model holds. The world round: shortcut: an amount stands from the date the research dates it; before it no minimum is known and the job is refused (AD before 2026-07-01, PH before 2026-09-26, BE before 2026-06-01, AS before 2024-09-30), as the twenty's are
value.noneAndUnknown: an agreement the research says sets nothing (none) and one whose terms it couldn't find (unknown, a blocker standing for it) pay no minimum; aboutMarket tells the player what isn't known
value.statuteFloor: a statutory minimum wage is read as a director's floor only where the research gives it as theirs (item 'rates': Andorra's Llei 46/2022 art. 25.1, EUR 72.40 a day; the Philippines' Eddie Garcia Act, PHP 755 a day, Metro Manila's rate for the whole market; American Samoa's Miscellaneous Activities rate, USD 5.80 an hour at the game's 8 hours a day). Anguilla's and every other general minimum wage the research files under 'none' is not read.
value.cubaLevel: Cuba's scale read at its lowest level (3, group XIV, CUP 6,130 a month on the 44-hour week): the least a subsidised director is paid; the levels 1-2 turn on an artistic evaluation the game doesn't model; a month is the actor's 21 days
value.belgiumScale: SCP 303.01: the production manager's category 10 at its fixed-term start (EUR 1,237.47 a week), the least of the scale at any seniority (the research gives only the start and the 40-year step); a feature may instead name the flat fee (EUR 20,000, be-303-flat); both dated from the 2026-06-01 indexation the page states them at
value.azerbaijan: the state-order minimum (AZN 9,000 a feature, 1,400 an episode) applies only where the job names az-state-order; any other film there names az-screen (the guild publishes no fee terms: none)
value.dacFloor: Argentina's DAC 'piso de negociación garantizado' (March 2026) paid as the minimum: an episode's total by running time (to 20, 21-60, 61-90 minutes), its prep and cut; a feature's 50 days of prep apart from the shoot and the cut by running time (5/10/15/20 days); the pilot's and the monthly floors, the shoot minimums (3.5 to 22 days) and the feature's 10% of below-the-line are not read
value.noneAtAPlace: a market's pay is left to negotiation where a guild's, a law's or a fee's figure writes no minimum at its place (null, false, or the research's 'freie Vereinbarung (none)'): AT, AZ (outside state order), BA, CH (features), HK, LV, ME, PA, SK; Switzerland's television isn't addressed by its research, so no agreement covers it
value.noneWithBlocker: a 'none' figure that a 'none' or 'terms' blocker stands beside (AI, BN, GI, MS, SH, VG; HU now that its interview-only figure is a blocker) is read as terms unknown, as Nigeria's was
value.registerOnly: a market whose research found nothing (204 blocked, no file cited) is read from its register blocker alone, what isn't known as each attempt's 'not found: <items>' names it; its agreement is unknown (no minimum) and the player is told
value.follows: a territory whose research says a director's work there follows its sovereign's terms takes the sovereign's market as compiled, each agreement as its own (<cc>-<id>, the work and its pay in the territory), and is told what isn't known of the sovereign's with its own: AX (FI), BL GF GP MF PM RE YT (FR; GP and RE cite Code du travail L1521-1, L2621-1, L2222-1 and IDCC 3097/2642), CC CX NF (AU), as the actor's engine reads them. PR (follows US) is not: the US is the DGA's, kept by the engine for the US alone; reading PR as the DGA's would be a change to the DGA terms (proposed, not made)

entries.sought: How a producer's project in each of twenty markets beyond the UK reads its market's public fund, cap on public aid, production incentive, fee and overhead caps and release rate (research/sources/person/markets/producer-<CC>.json, R-5135 to R-5154; Telefilm's, the CNC's and Screen Australia's terms from R-4612).
entries.why: Every rate, share, cap, sum and bound is the research's own, read at its place (tools/person/markets-producer/readings.json) or written in the reading and found standing in the figure; how they are applied to one project where the research gives a rule, not a project, is the game's reading, named here so the player is told it is the game's own. The world round (2026-11-01, every country beyond the first markets): The research gives each figure at its place; these are the game's own choices in reading them, told to the player as the game's (add to the existing entry, R-5231's value)

value.award: A fund's yes pays the most its terms allow for the budget (its share of the budget, at most its cap, or its fixed sum), held to what the market's cap on all public aid leaves after the credit; where the fund sets no share of its own (the CNC's avance, the FFA's jury fund) the aid cap alone bounds it; refused where the credit takes all the aid.
value.shares: The Netherlands Film Fund's award at the 42% its supported features of 2024 drew on average (as the BFI's 22%); Norway's at the market assessment's low level (50%, NOK 9.8m); Italy's at the first and second features' 40% to EUR 4m for every project; Japan's at the general grant (not the young-film-maker grant or the 30% certified uplift); Canada's Telefilm at its English low-budget stream's 11.1% for every budget and its cap for languages other than French (the market's language is English).
value.credit: The incentive counts the whole budget as qualifying spend in the market except where the research gives the share counted (France and the Netherlands, 80%); a threshold on spend is read on the budget; Korea at a small company's base 15% (not the further 15%); Ireland at Section 481's 32% (not the Scéal uplift); France at the French-language film's 30% (the market's language); the United States at California's independent-film credit (Los Angeles is the market's city).
value.fees: The fee and overheads at each cap a funder sets, read on the budget: Germany's fee net of its own 5% as the research's example counts it (EUR 3.25m, EUR 154,375); Ireland's 15% (eligible spend over 80%); the Netherlands' 17.5% together under EUR 750,000; where a market sets none, no fee is carried.
value.release: Italy's 82% of the year's classified films reaching cinemas read as a project's chance of a cinema release, moved by the film and its campaign as the BFI's are; earning back twice the budget is told only in the UK.
value.shared: The option is the WGA's in every market; the market's money is sought in the EAO's shares and the producer's own 18% (European films') in every market; a market's months run in its city's zone as the actor's market there keeps it.
value.zone: A market's months run in the actor's market city's zone where the actor's engine keeps a market there (or its own three agreements); else in the zone of the country's most populous place on the map (GeoNames, first of the most populous in the gazetteer's file); none (refused at option) where the map has no place: BV, HM, UM. Needed because the actor's readings leave many countries unread (no zone).
value.currency: A market's currency is its country's (the gazetteer's) unless every term the engine reads is in another: AE, DO, JO, MN, MU, TT in USD; MD, MK, RO, RS in EUR.
value.spendIsBudget: An incentive's base (spend in the country) is read as the budget, as the twenty's are: the project is made in the market.
value.baseRate: Where a rate rises by points, bonuses or uplifts, the base (standard, minimum) rate is read: AE 35%, AM 25%, MT 30%, MU 30%, GE 20%, HR 25%, MD 25%, RS 25%/30%, TH, JO's third tier 35% (its 35-45%), PT's rebate 25%.
value.tiersNotBands: JO's and TH's rates by spend are read as tiers (the whole spend at the rate its level sets), not bands.
value.localProducer: Where a threshold differs for a local and a foreign production, the local's: MU's USD 50,000, TT's local 35% on US$15,000 to 8m; PL's feature (co-)production's over PLN 4m, not the service production's PLN 1m; CH's majority fiction CHF 1.2m; CO's CINA (35%, COP 3,151,629,000) and not the Fondo Fílmico (two rates by kind of spend).
value.portugal: Portugal: the Cash Rebate (25% from EUR 500,000 to EUR 1.5m) below EUR 2.5m, the Cash Refund (30% of the first EUR 2m, 25% above, to EUR 6m) from it, the two not combinable and the refund the greater.
value.panama: Panama's 15% to productions spending more than B/.3m up to B/.40m: none beyond B/.40m.
value.moldovaRelease: Moldova's release rate: 50 released of the 62 finished of the 102 projects backed 2017-2024 (a film released is one finished).
value.sloveniaRate: Slovenia's fund rate: 14 funded of 37 eligible in the 2026 fiction production call (features and shorts together).
value.austriaFees: Austria's fee and overheads caps read from EUR 2.5m (5% and 7.5%, to EUR 250,000 and EUR 375,000); below it the ÖFI's table gives single rows, not a rule, so no cap is carried there.
value.fundMostOnly: A fund's award given only as a most (Slovenia's EUR 1m, Senegal's CFA 150m) is awarded at that most, held to the cap on all public aid where there is one.

entries.sought: The game's own readings where the tax research gives a rule and not how a life meets it
entries.why: The research (money.tax.<CC>) gives each country's figures; how a screen worker's life meets them (who is resident, which work is wages, when a fee is paid, how a year is reckoned) is the game's, told to the player as the game's. The world round (2026-11-01, every country beyond the first markets): The research gives each country's figures as its law or source writes them; where they are written per month, per city, per family share, or with a year or currency left unsaid, the engine reads them one way, and the player is told the reading is the game's (tax.model) and what isn't modeled (tax.unkept).

value.residence: Where the person lives is the country of their first citizenship until a residence is held (no residence is held yet: src/person/identity residenceOf); resident there, a non-resident everywhere else.
value.employed: A performer's and a director's pay are an employee's wages (social contributions withheld at source, the employee's scale); a producer's fee and an author's sale or option are a self-employed worker's (contributions at the year's reckoning, the self-employed scale). Where the readings say the trade works freelance (IN, JP, KR, NZ: their withholding covers every kind of work as fees), none is wages.
value.cumulative: An employee's contributions at source are the year's scale on the pay so far, less what the year's earlier pay bore (a ceiling or a threshold read over the tax year, in the work country).
value.perPayment: A withholding scale is applied to each payment as the research gives it per payment (Japan's million yen, Brazil's monthly IRRF table taken as the month's pay, Germany's 250 euros per performance); the UK's and India's thresholds over the year's payments in the country.
value.directorsFee: A director's fee is paid as the work is done: prep, shoot and cut each pay their days' share (in hundredths of a day), the periods the agreement guarantees.
value.currency: Pay is made in the work country's currency, at the day's rate where the agreement pays in another (src/money/rates); carried into an account kept in another currency at the day's rate with the bank's share for spending in another currency (its debit card's fx, src/money/banks), none where the bank states none. The world round: Where the research names no currency, the map's; where it writes a currency at par with the map's (Gibraltar's, St Helena's pounds, Panama's balboa), the map's; Somalia and Zimbabwe keep the US dollars their law writes.
value.credit: Tax withheld abroad is credited against the tax at home, up to it (as a treaty's credit gives it); never refunded at home.
value.vat: A resident freelancer's fee bears VAT once the tax year's fees in the country pass the threshold (or from the first where none is set), at the author's own rate where the law sets one; collected into the account and paid over with the year's return.
value.returnDue: The balance is paid or refunded on the return's due date: the day the research gives, so many years after the year's end (Mexico's April return month read as its last day); where none is given (France), the return is reckoned and nothing is settled.
value.owed: Where the account can't pay the balance within its overdraft, it is owed and the player told; no penalty or interest is reckoned.
value.conversionFee: A cost in another currency is carried into the account's at the day's rate, the bank's card share beside it.
value.permitFees: A permit's fee the research names as the employer's or the sponsor's (paid by the employer, paid by the sponsor, an employer's fee) is the engager's; the worker pays the rest where the worker applies.
value.unionDues: A union's initiation fee and the first year's dues are paid on joining; the dues of the years after aren't charged yet.
value.children: The person has no children: Germany's care contribution for the childless is taken.
value.regional: Only the national scale (and a regional or municipal rate that applies everywhere: Italy's 1.23%, Copenhagen's for Denmark, Sweden's average) is taken until a residence within the country is held.
value.rounding: Each figure is reckoned exactly and rounded half to even to the currency's minor unit; a country's own rounding (to the whole euro, the hundred yen) isn't modeled.
value.yearNotGiven: Where the research gives no tax year, the year is counted from 1 January and no return is due (told: year), except where the country levies no income tax, which has no return to tell of.
value.periodTables: A monthly, fortnightly or annual withholding table is read on each payment as it stands (the ledger's reading for Brazil, kept for every country).
value.periodCeilings: A monthly ceiling is read over the year as twelve months, a weekly one as 52 weeks, a quarterly one as four quarters.
value.placeRates: Where the rate turns on the city or municipality, the capital's is read (Croatia: Zagreb; Greenland: Sermersooq; Montenegro: Podgorica; China's contributions: Beijing; Bosnia and Herzegovina: the Federation), or the research's published average (Åland, Finland, Iceland, Belgium's communes), or the lowest the research names for all (Liechtenstein's 150%); told: regional.
value.familyShares: A scale applied per family share is read for a single person (one share).
value.thresholds: A threshold is passed above its figure: at the figure itself nothing is charged (the US Virgin Islands' USD 225,000, Burkina Faso's XOF 50,000, Ethiopia's ETB 10,000, Saint Lucia's XCD 10,000, Guernsey's £2,500).
value.selfEmployed: A fee's VAT, receipts tax and self-employed contributions fall on the work a country's employees don't do (performer and director are employees unless the readings say otherwise; Portugal and Saint-Martin: none).
value.chile: Chile's scale in UTA is read as the SII's November 2026 monthly table in pesos over twelve months.
value.indonesia: Indonesia's 50% base for a non-employee's fee is read as half the fee deducted.
value.citizenship: Where a contribution or rate turns on citizenship (the Gulf states' social security, Singapore's CPF, Malaysia's EPF, Monaco's French nationals, Seychelles' first band), the citizen's is read where given and the rest told; the game does not read citizenship here.
value.oneOfTwo: Where the research gives two readings of one figure (Tuvalu's weekly rebate, Lesotho's VAT threshold, Liberia's services rate, French Polynesia's franchise, Greece's employee contribution as Deloitte prints it), the figure is not modeled, or the one the research quotes from the source is read, and the other told.

sources.said: চলচ্চিত্র নির্মাণে সরকারি অনুদান প্রদান নীতিমালা | ফাইল সমূহ | তথ্য ও সম্প্রচার মন্ত্রণালয় … ফাইলের ধরন: (নেই) স্বল্পদৈর্ঘ্য চলচ্চি... পূর্ণদৈর্ঘ্য চলচ্চিত... স্বল

sources.title: পূর্ণদৈর্ঘ্য চলচ্চিত্র নির্মাণে সরকারি অনুদান প্রদান নীতিমালা, ২০২৫ (Ministry of Information and Broadcasting, Film-2 Branch; Bangladesh Gazette extraordinary, 5 March 2025), linked from the ministry's grant-policy files page
sources.said: প্রজ্ঞাপন তারিখ: ১৩ ফাল্গুন ১৪৩১/ ২৬ ফেব্রুয়ারি ২০২৫ পূর্ণদৈর্ঘ্য চলচ্চিত্র নির্মাণে সরকারি অনুদান প্রদান নীতিমালা, ২০২৫ … প্রতি অর্থবছরে প্রাপ্ত বরাদ্দের আলোকে সর্বোচ্চ ১২(বারো)টি পূর্ণদৈর্ঘ্য চলচ্চিত্রকে … ৪.১। অনুদানপ্রাপ্তির জন্য মনোনীত চলচ্চিত্রের প্রযোজককে অনুদান নীতিমালার আওতায় সর্বোচ্চ ৭৫.০০ (পঁচাত্তর) লক্ষ টাকা পর্যন্ত অনুদান প্রদান করা হবে। … চলচ্চিত্রের গল্প লেখককে ২.০০ (দুই) লক্ষ এবং চিত্রনাট্যকারকে ৩.০০ (তিন) … সাইনিংমানি (১ম কিস্তি/প্রি- প্রোডাকশন) হিসেবে অনুদানের ২০% অর্থ প্রদান … (প্রোডাকশন) হিসেবে ৫০% অর্থ প্রদান করা হবে। … অনূর্ধ ২০% অর্থ প্রদান করা হবে। … সংক্রান্ত প্রমাণক মন্ত্রণালয়ে দাখিলের পর অবশিষ্ট ১০% অর্থ প্রদান করা হবে।

sources.title: Fédération Wallonie-Bruxelles, Chambre de Concertation Cinéma: Conditions de travail (April 2024)
sources.said: La durée du travail hebdomadaire est de 38 heures, réparties sur 5 ou 6 jours par semaine. … La durée maximale de travail par jour, dans le cadre de la convention 303.01, est de 11 heures et la durée légale par semaine ne peut pas dépasser les 53 heures de travail. … rémunérée comme telle, c’est-à-dire à 150%, s’il s’agit d’un jour de semaine ou d’un samedi, ou à 200% s’il s’agit d’un dimanche ou d’un jour férié. … Les barèmes journaliers négociés entre les sociétés de productions et les technicien.nes et artistes engagé.e.s sous contrats de travail intègrent cette dimension. … Le contrat RPI n’est pas un contrat professionnel. Il permet le défraiement de prestations artistiques effectuées par des personnes possédant une « Carte Artiste ». S’il peut s’appliquer à certains rôles sur les tournages, comme par exemple les figurant.es, il ne peut servir à rémunérer des technicien.ne.s ou artistes professionnel.le.s engagé.e.s dans le cadre d’une production de long métrage ou série.

sources.title: Screen Flanders: Tax Shelter
sources.said: Unlike many other incentive systems within Europe, the Tax Shelter is not a cash or tax rebate expressed as a fixed percentage. … producers can finance between 38% and 40% of eligible Belgian expenditure through the Tax Shelter mechanism. … This interest is calculated according to the average 12-month Euribor rate, increased by 450 basis points, over a maximum period of 18 months. … the Belgian (co-)producer must make the eligible expenses within 18 months (24 months for animation) of signing the framework agreement. … The Belgian Tax Shelter system has been in place since 2003

sources.title: Стани член (САБ)
sources.said: Кандидатите за членство в САБ трябва да отговарят на следните критерии: 1.Да прилагат активно професионалните си умения в съответната сфера на сценичните изкуства. 2.Да са навършили 18 години. … Те заплащат 30 лева от членския внос. В този случай САБ гарантира минималните работни ставки, договорени с ТВ-канали и филмови к … за да членуват пенсионерите заплащат 15 лева. редовен членски внос – 55 лева. … Членският внос се заплаща еднократно за всяка една календарна година, като това трябва да става не по-късно от 15 декември на предходната година.

sources.title: Belize Film Commission: Frequently Asked Questions
sources.said: The completed application with the required fee and documentation can be submitted to the Belize Film Commission by the Local Coordinator before arrival or upon arrival of a film crew in Belize. sources.title: Schauspielgagen audiovisuelle Produktionen | SSFV
sources.said: Wir empfehlen Schauspieler:innen, Filmproduzierenden, öffentlichen und privaten Vergabestellen von Fördermitteln die folgenden Gagen im professionellen Filmschauspiel einzuhalten. Sie basieren auf den Ergebnissen der Einkommensstudie des SSFV (2021) und umfassen drei Tarife, um sowohl der Berufsausbildung als auch der zunehmenden Berufserfahrung Rechnung zu tragen: Tarif A: Fr. 1'650 brutto Einstiegsgage nach abgeschlossener Schauspielausbildung oder bei Erfüllung von definierten Alternativkriterien Tarif B: Fr. 1'950 brutto Für erfahrene Schauspieler:innen mit 10 - 15 Jahren Berufserfahrung Tarif C: Fr. 2'350 brutto Für sehr erfahrene Schauspieler:innen mit mehr als 15 Jahren Berufserfahrung Es gibt keine Halbtagesgagen. … Weil das Filmland Schweiz nicht nur sehr klein, sondern auch noch in verschiedene Sprachregionen aufgeteilt ist, können Schauspieler:innen i.d.R. nicht allein vom Schauspiel in Schweizer Filmproduktionen leben.

sources.said: Der jährliche Mitgliederbeitrag für Aktivmitglieder beträgt CHF 420.- (monatlich CHF 35.-). Neue Aktivmitglieder bezahlen im ersten Jahr der Mitgliedschaft einen reduzierten Beitrag von CHF 210.-. Der jährliche Mitgliederbeitrag für Nachwuchsmitglieder beträgt CHF 75.- … Dem Antrag muss eine vollständige Filmografie beiliegen. Unvollständige Anträge werden nicht berücksichtigt. sources.title: Communiqué: Accord sur les salaires et honoraires pour la fiction et le documentaire
sources.said: Pour le scénario d’un long-métrage de fiction destiné au cinéma, les deux parties ont convenu d’un honoraire minimal de 75'000 CHF. Ce montant constitue un plancher, susceptible d’augmenter selon des critères tels que l’expérience, la notoriété ou la nature du projet. … Des négociations séparées sont en cours pour le développement et la production de séries.

sources.title: ARF/FDS Long métrage de fiction : calculateur de temps de travail
sources.said: L’ARF/FDS recommande 90’000 CHF et une participation d’au moins 5 % aux recettes nettes comme base de négociation appropriée. En accord avec les associations de producteur.trice.s, un honoraire minimum de 75'000 CHF a été convenu.

sources.title: Die Mitgliedschaft | ARF/FDS
sources.said: Voraussetzung für die Aufnahme in den Verband ist eine professionelle Tätigkeit als Filmurheber:in in den Bereichen Regie, Drehbuch oder Autorenproduktion. Die filmische Tätigkeit bildet die ökonomische Existenzgrundlage und macht mindestens 50% des Verdienstes aus. Mindestens ein Film muss öffentlich aufgeführt worden sein (Kino, Festival, Fernsehen). … In den ersten drei Jahren der Mitgliedschaft ist der Mitgliederbeitrag um 50% reduziert und beträgt nur CHF 250.– pro Jahr. … Der jährliche Beitrag für Nachwuchsmitglieder beträgt CHF 100.– .

sources.title: Die Schweizer Filmförderung: Verteilplan und Höchstbeiträge 2026 (BAK)
sources.said: Selektive Filmförderung 16 344 000 … Schweizer Film mit verantwortlichem Schweizer 1 200 000 Innovative Formate … Drehbuchförderung 30 000

sources.title: Selektive Filmförderung (BAK)
sources.said: Mit der selektiven Filmförderung werden Drehbuch und Produktion sowie - bei Dokumentar- und Trickfilmen - die Projektentwicklung von Filmen unterstützt. Die beim Bundesamt für Kultur eingereichten Gesuche ( siehe entsprechende Formulare ) werden von einer Fachkommission beurteilt.

sources.title: Filmstandortförderung Schweiz (FiSS) (BAK)
sources.said: Der Förderbeitrag beträgt 20% der anrechenbaren Kosten. Bei minoritären Koproduktionen und technischen Kosten gilt ein erhöhter Ansatz von 40%. Bei majoritären Koproduktionen gilt ein Ansatz von 50% für filmtechnische Leistungen. Der Höchstbeitrag beträgt 600 000 Franken. 80% des Förderbeitrags wird zugesichert. … Von der Filmstandortförderung profitieren Filme, die zu einem wesentlichen Teil in der Schweiz hergestellt werden und bereits zu 75 % finanziert (ohne Standortförderung) sind. Spielfilme müssen grundsätzlich mindestens fünf Drehtage in der Schweiz aufweisen. … Spiel- und Animationsfilme müssen folgende anrechenbaren Kosten nachweisen: 1 200 000 Franken für majoritäre Koproduktionen, 300 000 Franken für minoritäre Koproduktionen. … Jährlicher Kredit 6 Millionen Franken pro Jahr. … Falls nur FISS gefördert, können bis 5% oder 50'000 Franken für das Produktionsteam angerechnet werden.

entries.sought: The terms a professional actor is engaged on in Chile

sources.title: El Ciudadano, 29/09/2014: Subdirectora de Cultura releva puesta en marcha de mesa de trabajo entre actores y productores — quoting the SIDARTE–APCT protocolo de acuerdo of 29 September 2014 (its text is not published; SIDARTE's site)
sources.said: el Sindicato de Actores (Sidarte) y la Asociación de Productores de Cine y Televisión de Chile, A.G. (APCT), firmaron este lunes un protocolo de acuerdo, para establecer una mesa de trabajo entre ambos gremios.

sources.title: SIDARTE: Salarios mínimos sugeridos
sources.said: SALARIOS SUGERIDOS POR SIDARTE VALORES( LÍQUIDOS) … Jornada Laboral Teleserie 160,000 Jornada Laboral Miniserie/Unitario 120,000 Jornada Laboral Corto Universitario 100,000 Jornada Laboral Cine 130,000 Bolo Teleserie 100,000 Bolo continuidad 130,000 Bolo Miniserie/Unitario 90,000 Spot Publicitario 540,000 Spot Web 330,000 Video Corporativo 280,000 Jornada Laboral Teatro 80,000 Jornada Laboral Teatro 130,000 Hora Ensayo Teatro 17,000 … Los traslados y la alimentación les corresponden a la parte contratante.

sources.title: SIDARTE: Hazte Socio
sources.said: Nuestros nuevos estatutos, que entraron en vigencia en Septiembre de 2019, permiten que nuestro sindicato abra las puertas a todos y todas los/as trabajadores/as del teatro … Fotocopia simple de certificado de egreso o título. Documentación Currículum Vitae. … Haber estado activo durante los últimos 12 meses previo a la presentación de los antecedentes al sindicato. … Se avisará a la o el postulante si es aceptado o no, en un plazo de 7 días hábiles. … El valor de la cuota de inscripción es de $24.000 (veinti cuatro mil pesos), lo que cubrirá los primeros 6 meses de cuotas sindicales y el carnet de socio. Cuota mensual La cuota sindical está fijada en $3000 (tres mil pesos).

sources.title: Ministerio de las Culturas: resultados del Fondo de Transición Industria 2021
sources.said: El 40% de los recursos fueron destinados a empresas y productoras fuera de la Región Metropolitana, lo que busca disminuir las brechas socioeconómicas y territoriales.

sources.title: Ministerio de las Culturas (09/09/2025): segunda convocatoria del programa IFI Audiovisual 2025
sources.said: incluyó un incentivo regional para proyectos realizados fuera de la Región Metropolitana, donde el reembolso puede alcanzar hasta un 40% de los gastos calificados, incentivando la descentralización

sources.title: Ley 1835 del 9 de junio del 2017 (Ley Pepe Sánchez), summary sheet (Universidad del Rosario)
sources.said: Estipula que en la presunción de cesión de los derechos de los autores, se conservará el derecho a recibir una remuneración equitativa por los actos de comunicación pública, incluida la puesta a disposición y el alquiler comercial al público que se hagan de la obra audiovisual, remuneración que será pagada directamente por quien realice la comunicación pública.

sources.title: Pepe Sánchez Law: 8 years of a hard-won right (FESAAL, 2025-06-07)
sources.said: The law guarantees audiovisual authors—specifically directors and screenwriters—the right to receive payment when their works are publicly used for commercial purposes. This non-waivable remuneration must be managed collectively by entities created for this purpose such as DASC (Directores Audiovisuales Sociedad Colombiana de Gestión) and REDES (Red Colombiana de Escritores Audiovisuales), who began collecting and distributing rights in 2019.

entries.sought: The terms a producer works on in Colombia

sources.title: Ley 1556 de 2012 (DIAN normograma, compiled text)
sources.said: Las empresas productoras de obras audiovisuales, rodadas total o parcialmente dentro del territorio colombiano que celebren los Contratos Filmación Colombia, tendrán una contra prestación equivalente al cuarenta por ciento (40%) del valor de los gastos realizados en el país por concepto de servicios cinematográficos contratados con sociedades colombianas de servicios cinematográficos y al veinte por ciento (20%) del valor de los gastos en hotelería, alimentación y transporte … Solo se podrán aprobar proyectos cuando el productor cinematográfico vaya a invertir en su producción en territorio colombiano como mínimo mil ochocientos salarios mínimos legales mensuales vigentes (1.800 smlmv), recursos que deberán manejarse a través de una fiducia administrada por una sociedad fiduciaria vigilada por la Superintendencia Financiera

sources.title: Incentivo CINA, Certificado de Inversión Audiovisual (Comisión Fílmica Colombia, Proimágenes)
sources.said: Es un descuento tributario del impuesto de renta equivalente al 35% de los gastos de las producciones extranjeras efectuados en Colombia en servicios audiovisuales y logísticos. Estos títulos son transferibles a personas declarantes del impuesto de renta en Colombia a través del mercado de valores. Para obtener el incentivo CINA, se debe realizar un gasto mínimo en servicios audiovisuales y logísticos en Colombia de la siguiente manera: Obras audiovisuales o películas 1.800 SMLMV equivalentes a COP 3.151.629.000 (USD $856.388*). Series 1.800 SMLMV equivalentes a COP 3.151.629.000 (USD $856.388*) con un costo promedio por capítulo de 450 SMLMV equivalentes a COP$787.907.250

sources.title: Convocatoria FDC 2026: Producción de largometrajes de ficción, categoría 1

sources.title: Convocatoria FDC 2026: Producción de largometrajes de ficción, categoría 2
sources.said: El monto total destinado es de tres mil ciento cincuenta millones de pesos ($3.150.000.000), otorgando estímulos de mil cincuenta millones de pesos ($1.050.000.000).

sources.said: Durante el año llegaron a cartelera 408 películas, 3% más que en 2024. La producción local estuvo marcada por la diversidad de géneros, con 33 documentales y 26 dramas como formatos predominantes … Asimismo, 22 de las películas colombianas estrenadas correspondieron a óperas primas … La asistencia a películas nacionales se redujo 36,6% … Durante el año se beneficiaron 144 proyectos con estímulos por $151.213 millones

sources.title: Nový Státní fond audiovize přináší vyšší podporu a výhodnější pobídky (SFA press release, 2025-01-15)
sources.said: Procento u pobídek bylo zvýšeno z 20 na 25 procent, u animovaných a nové kategorie digitálně produkovaných projektů dokonce na 35 procent. Maximální výše pobídky u jednoho projektu se zvyšuje ze 150 milionů na 450 milionů korun. … Novela zákona o audiovizi změnila od 1. ledna 2025 Státní fond kinematografie na Státní fond audiovize (SFA). … Zásadní změnou na příjmové straně je sjednocení výše takzvaných parafiskálních poplatků na 2 procenta. … odvodem ve výši 3,5 %, který bude kombinací povinného odvodu do Fondu a přímých investic do místní tvorby. Povinný odvod je stanoven ve výši 1 procenta a zbývajících 2,5 procenta je ponechán na rozhodnutí každé platformy. … Nový systéme rozděluje podporu do čtyř kategorií: Kinematografie, Televizní díla, Animace a videohry a Infrastruktura audiovize. … Každá ze čtyř kategorií bude mít vlastní radu s pěti radními

sources.title: Novela zákona o audiovizi: Pobídky 2026 (SFA presentation, Pavla Mrázková, 2025-12-17)
sources.said: zvýšení základní sazby z 20% na 25% • zavedení vyšší sazby 35% pro animovaná AVD a novou kategorii projektů bez natáčení živé herecké akce • zvýšení max. částky filmové pobídky na jeden projekt na 450 mil. Kč

sources.title: Doprovodná informace ke Sdělení ředitelky SFA o zastavení příjmu žádostí o zápis pobídkového projektu (SFA, March 2026)
sources.said: Dne 27. 3. 2026 od 9.00 hod. byl v souladu s § 51 odst. 5 zákona o audiovizi v platném znění dočasně zastaven příjem žádostí o zápis pobídkového projektu. Státní fond audiovize (dále jen „Fond“) musel k tomuto opatření přistoupit z důvodu vyčerpání finančních prostředků dotace ze státního rozpočtu účelově určené na filmové pobídky pro rok 2026, která dle schváleného zákona o státním rozpočtu ze dne 21. 3. 2026 činí 1 611 972 229 Kč

sources.title: Zákon č. 496/2012 Sb., o audiovizuálních dílech a podpoře audiovize (zákon o audiovizi), consolidated text (Zákony pro lidi)
sources.said: § 13 Rady (1) Rady rozhodují o a) formě podpory audiovize, b) podpoře projektů a její výši, c) náročnosti audiovizuálního díla nebo projektu, připouští-li to jeho povaha, a o výši intenzity veřejné podpory, … § 57a Intenzita veřejné podpory (1) Intenzita veřejné podpory, jíž se pro účely tohoto zákona rozumí objem veřejné podpory poskytnuté na projekt, na jehož realizaci byla poskytnuta podpora podle tohoto zákona, nesmí přesáhnout limit stanovený v přímo použitelném předpisu Evropské

sources.title: Výzva k podávání žádostí o podporu audiovize: Výroba celovečerního hraného filmu, 2026-A-2-8-37 (Státní fond audiovize)
sources.said: Evidenční číslo výzvy 2026-A-2-8-37 … Celkový objem podpory audiovize 100 000 000 Kč … Maximální intenzita veřejné … 50 % celkových nákladů projektu, resp. 60 % celkových nákladů projektu v … případě přeshraničních koprodukcí … Intenzita veřejné podpory může být zvýšena na 90 % celkových nákladů … Forma podpory audiovize: Investiční dotace … Správní poplatek 20 000 Kč … Celovečerním kinematografickým dílem se pro účely Státního fondu audiovize (dále jen „Fond“) rozumí dílo se stopáží delší než 60 minut.

sources.title: Crédito Fiscal Transferible en la legislación tributaria de la República Dominicana (Asociación Interamericana de Contabilidad, 2025)
sources.said: De acuerdo con el Artículo 39 de la Ley No. 108-10, modificado por la Ley No. 82-13, pueden beneficiarse del crédito fiscal (25%) las personas naturales o jurídicas que produzcan obras cinematográficas y audiovisuales, tanto dominicanas como extranjeras, en el territorio dominicano. … La legislación permite que una misma persona acumule varios proyectos para alcanzar el monto mínimo exigido por la ley (párrafo II, articulo 39). Esto facilita a los productores la obtención del crédito fiscal transferible. El monto mínimo exigido es de USD500,000.00 … como películas para televisión, telenovelas, documentales, series, miniseries y videos musicales, pueden acogerse a los incentivos fiscales.

sources.title: Dirección General de Cine celebra 15 años de la promulgación de la Ley 108-10 (Presidencia de la República Dominicana)
sources.said: Más de 5,600 personas y empresas han sido registradas en el sector, y 134 proyectos han sido impulsados por el Concurso Público Fonprocine , una iniciativa clave para estimular la creación local. … el artículo 39 permite competir a nivel internacional en la atracción de inversión extranjera … Desde 2021, el Cipac ha revisado 333 proyectos , con 596 validaciones emitidas

sources.title: IFAIC (Instituto de Fomento de las Artes, Innovación y Creatividades): Preguntas Frecuentes
sources.said: ¿Quiénes pueden solicitar el Certificado de Finalización de Producciones Audiovisuales y Cinematográficas para la Devolución del 50% del IVA? Las sociedades que se dediquen exclusivamente a la producción de audiovisuales, videos musicales, telenovelas, series, miniseries, reality shows o producciones cinematográficas que efectúen sus rodajes en Ecuador. Las sociedades que se dediquen a las actividades de programación y trasmisión aun cuando tengan a su cargo actividades de producción no podrán aplicar a este beneficio, conforme lo estable segundo artículo innumerado a continuación del artículo 74 de la Ley de Régimen Tributario Interno. … Si la ejecución del proyecto cinematográfico o audiovisual tiene una duración menor a 9 meses podrá solicitarse el certificado por las tres etapas en conjunto. … Persona natural o jurídica con nacionalidad ecuatoriana o extranjeros con residencia permanente en el Ecuador, que sean mayores de edad; de acuerdo a cada base técnica del concurso a aplicar. … Ecuatorianos y/o extranjeros legalmente residentes en el Ecuador, en los principales oficios de la producción cinematográfica o audiovisual bajo un sistema de puntajes. … La Dirección de Fomento Cinematográfico y Audiovisual emitirá la Certificación de Coproducción en el término de 10 días una vez presentados todos los documentos.

sources.said: ويؤدى طالب التصريح للنقابة مقابل متابعتها تنفيذ العقد مبلغًا من المال – حسب التصنيف الفئوى – لا يجاوز عشرة آلاف جنيه. وإذا كان طالب التصريح من غير المصريين يكون الحد الأقصى عشرين ألف جنيه. وتحدد اللائحة الداخلية لكل نقابة التصنيف الفئوى. ويحظر التعاقد أو التشغيل لغير الأعضاء العاملين بالنقابة أو غير الحاصلين على تصاريح عمل مؤقتة. مادة (5) مكررًا: يعاقب بالحبس مدة لا تقل عن شهر ولا تزيد على ثلاثة أشهر وبغرامة لا تقل عن ألفى جنيه ولا تزيد على عشرين ألف جنيه

sources.said: Islam is the religion of the state and Arabic is its official language. … Cairo is the capital of the Arab Republic of Egypt.

sources.title: France's Constitution of 1958 (rev. 2024) (Constitute Project, English translation)
sources.said: Guadeloupe, Guyane, Martinique, La Reunion, Mayotte … In the overseas departments and regions, statutes and regulations shall be automatically applicable. They may be adapted in the light of the specific characteristics and constraints of such communities.

sources.title: Code du travail, article L1521-1 (Code du travail numérique, Ministère du Travail): individual labour relations apply overseas
sources.said: Les dispositions de la présente partie s'appliquent en Guadeloupe, en Guyane, en Martinique, à Mayotte et à La Réunion, à Saint-Barthélemy, à Saint-Martin et à Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, sous réserve des adaptations prévues par le présent titre.

sources.title: Code du travail, article L2621-1 (Code du travail numérique, Ministère du Travail): collective relations (part 2) apply overseas on the same terms
sources.said: Les dispositions générales prévues par les articles L. 1521-1 à L. 1521-4 sont également applicables aux dispositions du présent titre.

sources.title: Code du travail, article L2222-1 (Code du travail numérique, Ministère du Travail): national-scope agreements apply overseas unless they say otherwise
sources.said: Les conventions et accords collectifs de travail dont le champ d'application est national s'appliquent, sauf stipulations contraires, en Guadeloupe, en Guyane, en Martinique, à Mayotte, à La Réunion, à Saint-Barthélemy, à Saint-Martin et à Saint-Pierre-et-Miquelon, dans un délai de six mois à compter de leur date d'entrée en vigueur. … Le dernier alinéa est applicable à compter du 1er avril 2017, pour les conventions et accords conclus après cette date en Guadeloupe, en Guyane, en Martinique, à La Réunion

sources.title: Assemblée nationale, question écrite n° 32791, réponse du ministère du Travail (JO 26 avril 2022)
sources.said: Conformément aux dispositions de l'article L. 2222-1 du code du travail tel qu'issu de la loi n° 2016-1088 du 8 août 2016, dite « Loi Travail », les conventions et accords collectifs, dont le champ d'application est national, s'appliquent, sauf stipulation contraire, aux départements et régions d'outre-mer (DROM) … A ce jour, dix-neuf conventions collectives de travail nationales sont applicables, de jure, à Mayotte et recensées dans le tableau ci-dessous. … 1285 ARTISTIQUES CULTURELLES ENTREPRISES

sources.title: SPI (signatory): Convention collective nationale de la production cinématographique du 19 janvier 2012 (IDCC 3097), version consolidée juin 2024, Titre I, article 1 (champ d'application)
sources.said: La convention collective nationale de la production cinématographique, ses avenants et annexes, sont applicables : … aux entreprises françaises de production de films cinématographiques de long métrage … quels que soient les lieux d'exécution du contrat de travail, à savoir sur le territoire français, en ce compris les départements d'Outre … produisant tout ou partie d'un film sur le territoire français, en ce compris les départements d'Outre-mer

sources.title: Fiche-Paie.fr: CCN de la production audiovisuelle (IDCC 2642), article I.1, champ d'application, in force from 18 April 2024 (KALI text from Légifrance/DILA, updated 11 October 2026)
sources.said: Sur le territoire national au sens des dispositions de l'article L. 2222-1 alinéa 3 du code du travail, elle régit les relations entre : – d'une part, l'ensemble des salariés, quel que soit leur contrat de travail et le lieu de son exécution (France ou étranger)

sources.title: Fiche-Paie.fr: CCN des entreprises du secteur privé du spectacle vivant (IDCC 3090), article 1er, champ d'application territorial et professionnel (KALI text from Légifrance/DILA, updated 11 October 2026)
sources.said: La présente convention et ses annexes règlent, sur le territoire national (France métropolitaine et DOM), les rapports, les conditions de travail et de salaire

sources.title: Fiche-Paie.fr: CCN des entreprises artistiques et culturelles (IDCC 1285), article I.1, champ d'application, in force from 28 March 2018 (KALI text from Légifrance/DILA, updated 11 October 2026)
sources.said: La présente convention et ses annexes règlent sur le territoire national les rapports entre, d'une part, le personnel artistique, technique et administratif

sources.said: South Georgia & the South Sandwich Islands are only accessible by sea. There is no visitor accommodation ashore … All visitors are subject to the Entry Control Ordinance 2022.

sources.title: GSGSSI: About SGSSI
sources.said: There are no permanent residents in the Territory but the British Antarctic Survey (BAS) operates two bases on South Georgia.

sources.title: GSGSSI: Frequently Asked Questions
sources.said: There is no permanent human population on South Georgia.

sources.said: Every feature film, TV series, and documentary that incurs production costs in Iceland qualifies for a 25% reimbursement. There is no minimum spend requirement and no cap on the total amount. … Production costs incurred in Iceland must be at least ISK 350 million. A minimum of 30 working days in Iceland, either shooting days or defined post-production days, of which at least 10 must be shooting days. At least 50 crew members working directly on the project for a minimum of 50 working days, with all salaries and contractor payments taxed in Iceland. … The current legislation is valid through 31 December 2028.

sources.title: Film Financing & Incentives (Film Jamaica, JAMPRO Film Commission)
sources.said: The CHASE Fund was originally enabled in 2002 from provisions from the betting and gaming industry but is now operated through The Consolidated Fund. The Fund currently allots 15 percent of its grants & contributions towards Arts & Culture and such applications may be made on an ongoing basis through its website for creative projects. CHASE has already shown its support of the developing local film industry through its partnership with JAFTA and JAMPRO on the PROPELLA! script to screen programme to encourage emerging filmmakers. On a case by case basis local producers, content creators, animators and filmmakers may also submit proposals for all or part funding of projects or the research and development of projects.

sources.title: Jamaica Film & TV Industry (Film Jamaica)
sources.said: The main industry association covering film and television is the Jamaica Film and Television Association (JAFTA). It’s members feature a cross-section of stakeholders in the industry who possess a wealth of skills and resources. JAFTA became an organised group in 2015. In collaboration with The Film Commission and The CHASE Fund, JAFTA has initiated PROPELLA!, an annual initiative aimed to encourage and support new filmmakers and expand the pool of creative producers working in the film and television industry.

sources.title: JAMPRO, «Update on the Jamaica Screen Development Initiative (JSDI)», 18 February 2025
sources.said: The JSDI’s first call for applications in March 2024 resulted in 406 submissions, with 269 validated for further assessment. … For the 2024/25 Financial Year, JAMPRO received a budget allocation of J$234 million for JSDI. Of this amount, J$233,421,600.00 was disbursed for the first production rebate for Bob Marley: One Love , which was approved in 2023 by Cabinet to receive the maximum amount of US$1.5 million based on their over US$20m production expenditure in Jamaica.

sources.title: The Gleaner, «Film spending slashed in half to US$4.9m», 23 October 2026 (reporting the PIOJ's Economic and Social Survey Jamaica)
sources.said: 90 film and screen projects have been selected for funding under the Government’s Jamaica Screen Development Initiative (JSDI), a $1-billion programme aimed at strengthening the country’s screen-based industries. The selected projects span five categories: development, production, completion, film festival and market attendance, and production rebates. The programme, administered by JAMPRO, received 406 applications following its 2024 call.

sources.title: Ministry of Culture of Lebanon: Artists Syndicates and Mutual Fund
sources.said: Law No. 56/2008 on the organization of artistic professions was promulgated on 27/12/2008. This law regulates the formation, activity and membership of these syndicates. … Eight artists' syndicates are duly registered in the Ministry of Culture. These syndicates receive membership applications according to their field of work and then file them to the Ministry of Culture - Directorate of National Cooperation and Coordination - for approval after verifying that the required conditions are fulfilled. … This fund accepts memberships after verifying that the required conditions are met, especially that the applicant is a member of a formal syndicate. … Fix a retirement pension for the members. … A tax of two percent on all event tickets (theater, concerts) and all artistic activities … A tax of ten percent on foreign artists contracts collected by the Ministry of Finance and transferred monthly to the fund.

sources.title: Mongolia set to launch 30% location incentive – Screen Global Production (13 Sep 2021, quoting the culture minister Nomin Chinbat)
sources.said: The stand-out is a 30% location incentive scheme for qualifying and accredited film and television productions that take place in the country. Open to productions with a minimum spend of $500,000, the system is a cash rebate that is not linked to the tax system or other credits. In addition, a 30% rebate system being established for film and TV projects which use a substantial number of Mongolian personnel for post-production. There’s also a 10% cultural incentive for productions that highlight Mongolia’s unique culture and heritage. Plus a 5% Foreign Crew and Talent cash rebate for qualified foreign cast and crew. … Significantly, the three schemes may be combined to generate rebates of 45% for particular projects that tick all the boxes. Alternatively, there will also be a 20% Mongolia Film Incentive, which applies to local or joint-film productions that promote Mongolian culture and heritage to international audiences.

entries.sought: The terms a producer works on in Martinique

sources.title: Fonds territorial d’aide à la création et à la production (Collectivité Territoriale de Martinique)
sources.said: Dans le cadre de la convention de coopération 2023-2025 pour le cinéma et l’image animée entre la CTM, l’ÉTAT et le CNC, la Collectivité Territoriale de Martinique met en place un fonds territorial d’aide à la création et à la production. Ce fonds est consacré à l’aide à l’écriture, l’aide au dévelop … l’aide à la production et l’attribution de bourses de résidence. … Sur la base de ces avis, les projets sont ensuite examinés par le Conseil Exécutif qui prend la décision finale d’attribution des aides.

sources.title: Règlement du fonds territorial d’aide à la création et à la production d’œuvres cinématographiques et audiovisuelles, convention CNC/État (DAC)/CTM 2023-2025 (CTM, uploaded January 2025)
sources.said: a) Catégorie « COURT METRAGE » Le montant des aides publiques ne peut excéder 80% des coûts admissibles. … >100 % du montant de l’aide octroyée à la production de l’œuvre doit être investi en terme de dépenses en Martinique. … b) Catégorie « LONG METRAGE » Le montant des aides publiques ne peut excéder 50% des coûts admissibles. … - > 160 % du montant de l’aide octroyée à la production de l’œuvre doit être investi en terme de dépenses en Martinique … > Le dépôt du dossier de demande d’aide financière doit faire apparaître l’engagement d’un partenaire financier (CNC, distributeur, chaîne TV, SOFICA).

sources.title: Annexe: plafonds des aides, fonds territorial cinéma et audiovisuel (CTM, January 2025)
sources.said: Aide à la production Court métrage Cinéma 40 000 € … Série (tout format) 200 000 € … Long métrage cinéma 250 000 € Long métrage animation 350 000 € … Aide à l’écriture Court métrage cinéma et animation 4 000 € … Long métrage cinéma 40 000 € Long métrage animation 80 000 €

sources.title: European Commission, State aid SA.61114 (2021/X): Martinique, Fonds territorial d'aide à la création et à la production d'œuvres cinématographiques et audiovisuelles (GBER summary)
sources.said: Durée jusqu'au 31.12.2023 … Montant annuel total du budget prévu au titre du régime EUR 0.5 (millions) … en faveur des œuvres audiovisuelles (art. 54) 100 %

sources.title: RCI: Des réalisateurs martiniquais en désaccord avec la politique cinématographique locale
sources.said: Ces aides portent sur l'écriture, le développement et la production. En 2018, sur 58 projets étudiés, 21 ont été soutenus pour un montant global de 997 000 euros.

sources.title: Submission Procedures: Film Rebate Scheme (Economic Development Board Mauritius, 31 January 2020)
sources.said: The Film Rebate Scheme, implemented in 2013, was a first step towards the development of a cinematographic industry in Mauritius, under which film makers benefit of 30% rebate on all the qualifying expenditures incurred in Mauritius. A new band of 40% rebate has been introduced in the National Budget 2016-2017 on all qualifying expenditures incurred by a feature film in Mauritius (Minimum QPE of USD 1,000,000). This new band has been extended, through the National Budget 2018-2019, to high-end Television Series (Minimum QPE of USD 150,000). The Regulation is cited as the Economic Development Board (Film Rebate Scheme) Regulation 2018. … Category of Production Minimum QPE (USD) Eligible for 30% rebate Foreign Production Local Production Feature film (including animation) 100,000 50,000 Television drama series or single drama 20,000 (per episode) 20,000 Television documentary programme 20,000 20,000

sources.title: Creative Industry (Economic Development Board Mauritius)
sources.said: The Film Rebate Scheme is managed by the Economic Development Board. sources.title: Namibia Film Commission: Funding
sources.said: The Film and Video Fund, initiated by the Namibia Film Commission (NFC), plays a crucial role in the establishment and growth of the film industry in Namibia. The fund is designed to provide financial assistance to Namibian film producers, enabling them to develop, produce, and distribute captivating film, video, and television projects of Namibian origin.

sources.title: Namibia Film Commission: Funding Criteria
sources.said: The NFC gives priority to project funding in the areas of feature films, drama, documentary, and animation. … Preference will be given to projects that involve Namibian writers, directors, and/or producers. … All funded activities, including industry and audience development activities, must take place within Namibia … with a minimum requirement of two screen credits to qualify as an experienced filmmaker.

sources.title: Namibia Film Commission: Funding Opportunities
sources.said: Applications for this year closed on 10 August 2026 .

sources.title: Namibia Film Commission: Need to Know
sources.said: Filmmakers are generally required to obtain a film permit from the Namibian Film Commission (NFC) before commencing any filming activities in Namibia. … Working with a local production company is a requirement when obtaining a film permit.

sources.title: Namibia Film Commission: Local Crew
sources.said: the use of Namibian crew is a requirement unless there is skills deficit.

sources.title: Namibia Film Commission: Frequently Asked Questions
sources.said: All non-Namibian crew, even crew from SADC countries, require work visas to film in Namibia, even if it is only for a 1-day shoot.

sources.title: Семь деятелей кино исключены из Союза кинематографистов России (Эксперт, 30 января 2026)
sources.said: Подчеркивается, что причиной исключения стала многолетняя задолженность по членским взносам, что нарушает внутренние правила организации. Союз кинематографистов России — общероссийская общественная организация, объединяющая около 5 тыс. профессионалов кино. Союз основан на индивидуальном членстве, включает 13 гильдий (от режиссеров и актеров до киноведов и продюсеров) и представлен в большинстве регионов страны. Крупнейшие региональные подразделения организации находятся в Москве, Санкт-Петербурге и Свердловской области.

sources.title: Оплата членских взносов (Союз кинематографистов России)
sources.said: Вступительный взнос — 8 000 рублей. Оплата только после положительного решения о приеме. Ежегодный членский взнос — 2 000 рублей, для пенсионеров — 250 рублей. Освобождаются от уплаты ежегодных членских взносов члены Союза кинематографистов, достигшие 75-летнего возраста.

sources.title: Innst. 383 S (2024–2025), Innstilling frå familie- og kulturkomiteen om å innlemme Svalbard i Norsk filminstitutts forskrifter
sources.said: viser til at Svalbardloven § 2 annet ledd slår fast at offentligrettslige reguleringer utover straffe- rett og rettergangslovgivning ikke gjelder på Svalbard, med mindre det er særskilt fastsatt. Siden det ikke er fastsatt i Norsk filminstitutts (NFI) forskrifter at de skal gjelde for Svalbard, følger det av Svalbardloven § 2 at de ikke gjelder der. … Statsråden tilrår difor ikkje å endre forskrifta slik at Svalbard vert omfatta. … Stortinget ber regjeringen endre virkeområdet for Norsk filminstitutts relevante forskrifter om støtte til film- og serieproduksjon til også å omfatte Svalbard, slik at kostnader påløpt på Svalbard regnes som kostnader påløpt i Norge. Oslo, i familie- og kulturkomiteen, den 20. mai 2025 … I løpet av de siste 30 årene har det allerede blitt spilt inn over 450 filmer på Svalbard, inkludert naturdokumentarer, norske drama- serier og filmer samt internasjonale dramaserier og spil- lefilmer i ulike skalaer. … dette har Sysselmesteren en rekke ferdselsrestriksjoner som håndheves og som selvfølgelig gjelder for alle, in- kludert filmnæringen, på øygruppen.

sources.title: Stortinget, minutes of 3 June 2025, item 2 (Innst. 383 S (2024–2025): bringing Svalbard into the Norwegian Film Institute's regulations)
sources.said: Komiteens flertall foreslår i innstillingen å be regjeringen endre virkeområdet for Norsk filminstitutts relevante forskrifter om tilskudd til audiovisuell produksjon og forskrift om insentivordningen for film- og serieproduksjon til også å omfatte Svalbard. … Endelig sikrer vi flertall for at de ordningene Norsk filminstitutt har, også skal omfatte Svalbard.

sources.title: FOPICA: Qui sommes-nous ?
sources.said: est un mécanisme de financement du cinéma, de l'audiovisuel et de la création numérique mis en place par l'État du Sénégal à travers le Ministère de la Culture. sources.title: FOPICA: Aide à la production — Long métrage
sources.said: **Plafond d'intervention :** jusqu'à 150 millions FCFA par projet. **Modalités de versement** (selon la convention, durée 24 mois) : - 20 % à la signature de la convention ; - 50 % une semaine après le démarrage du tournage ; - 20 % une semaine après le démarrage de la postproduction ; - 10 % à la livraison du film. … **Sont exclus du système d'appui :** captations, talkshows, magazines, reportages télévisuels, émissions de flux, sitcoms, clips musicaux, films institutionnels et/ou didactiques, publicités.

sources.title: FOPICA communiqué (18 mars 2026): Résultats 2023 — 49 projets retenus sur 213

sources.title: Terres australes et antarctiques françaises, home page (TAAF administration)
sources.said: Territoire sans population permanente ni élus, les TAAF sont placées sous l’autorité d’un préfet, administrateur supérieur, qui y exerce l’intégralité de l’action publique

sources.title: Recrutement (TAAF administration)
sources.said: Saint-Pierre de La Réunion (siège des TAAF)

sources.title: L'intelligibilité du droit dans les Terres australes et antarctiques françaises, rapport (Loïc Peyen, Université Toulouse 1 Capitole, 2022), extract published by the TAAF
sources.said: L’article L. 1511-1 du code du travail spécifie le champ d’application territorial du code s’agissant des territoires ultramarins. Repris par l’ensemble des dispositions relatives à l’outre- mer, cet article ne mentionne pas les TAAF, ce qui emporte l’inapplicabilité du code dans le territoire. … Les TAAF, comme d’autres territoires soumis à la spécialité législative, relèvent en fait de la loi n° 52-1322 du 15 décembre 1952 instituant un code du travail dans les territoires et territoires associés relevant des ministères de la France d’Outre-mer

sources.title: TAAF site search "code du travail": excerpt of the TAAF administrator's order of 13 January 2011 fixing the regime of district contracts

sources.title: Law on Cinematography No. 05/2022/QH15 (English translation, Apolat Legal)
sources.said: The Cinematographic Development Support Fund is an off-budget state financial fund supported by the State with charter capital … Section 43. The Cinematographic Development Support Fund aims to: 1. Provide support for projects on experimental films, debut films, and films of young authors. 2. Provide support for authors, film production projects, and outstanding Vietnamese films that participate in film festivals, film awards, film competitions, film fairs, film programs, and film weeks abroad. … Article 41. Incentive regulations for foreign organizations using film production services in Vietnam Foreign organizations producing films with the use of backgrounds in Vietnam or film production services provided by Vietnamese organizations may receive tax incentives according to laws on tax.

sources.said: Article 43 Tipus de gravamen El tipus de gravamen de l’impost és el 10 per cent. … Els obligats tributaris poden reduir la base de tributació general, en concepte de reducció per mínim personal exempt, en un import de 24.000 euros. … es dedueix de la quota de tributació una bonifica- ció del 50 per cent de la quantitat que resulti d’aplicar el tipus de gravamen de l’impost sobre l’import de la base de tributació general de l’obligat tributari, minorada en la quantitat de 24.000 eu- ros corresponents a la reducció prevista en el primer paràgraf de l’apartat 1 de l’article 35 a què tingui dret. sources.title: Taxation | The Official Portal of the UAE Government
sources.said: The UAE does not levy income tax on individuals. However, it levies 5 per cent value added tax on the purchase of goods and services.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: United Arab Emirates, Taxes on personal income
sources.said: There is currently no personal income tax in the United Arab Emirates. As such, there are no individual tax registration or reporting obligations. … Under the UAE CT Law, natural persons who conduct a business or business activity in the United Arab Emirates will be subject to UAE CT at 9% where the total turnover derived from such business or business activity exceeds 1 million UAE dirham (AED). For this purpose, wages, personal investment income, and real estate investment income will not be considered for determining such turnover.

sources.title: Corporate tax (CT) | The Official Portal of the UAE Government
sources.said: Scope CT will apply to: all businesses and individuals conducting business activities under a commercial licence in the UAE … Foreign entities and individuals only if they conduct a trade or business in the UAE in an ongoing or regular manner … CT Rate As per Ministry of Finance, CT rates are: 0 per cent for taxable income up to AED 375,000 9 per cent for taxable income above AED 375,000

sources.title: GPSSA reviews the most prominent features of Federal Law No. (57) of 2023
sources.said: Contribution rates As per the 2023 law, the total contribution rates have become 26%, out of which the insured bears 11% and the employer (government and private sector entities) bears 15%. The UAE government supports private sector entities employing Emiratis whose contribution account salaries are less than Dh20,000, by paying 2.5% out of the employers 15% share.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: United Arab Emirates, Other taxes
sources.said: There is a social security regime in the United Arab Emirates that applies to qualifying UAE and other GCC national employees only. Non-GCC nationals are not subject to social security in the United Arab Emirates.

sources.title: Corporate Tax in the UAE | Ministry of Finance
sources.said: Non-resident persons that do not have a Permanent Establishment in the UAE or that earn UAE sourced income that is not related to their Permanent Establishment may be subject to Withholding Tax (at the rate of 0%).

sources.title: Value Added Tax (VAT) | Ministry of Finance
sources.said: Value Added Tax (VAT) was introduced across the UAE on 1st January 2018 at a standard rate of 5%. … A business must register for VAT if their taxable supplies and imports exceed the mandatory registration threshold of AED 375,000. They may also opt for voluntary registration if their taxable supplies and imports are below the mandatory threshold but exceed the voluntary registration threshold of AED 187,500.

sources.title: FTA urges Natural Persons to register for Corporate Tax before end of March 2025 to avoid Administrative Penalties | Federal Tax Authority
sources.said: The guide explains that the first potential Tax Period for a natural person conducting a Business or Business Activity is the 2024 Gregorian calendar year. … their total Turnover in that calendar year exceed ed AED 1 million, they are a Taxable Person, who must register for Corporate Tax no later than 31 March of the calendar year following the year in which their total Turnover exceeded the AED 1 million threshold … they are required to submit an application to register for Corporate Tax no later than the 31 March 2025, and, consequently, submit a Corporate Tax Return no later than 30 September 2025.

sources.title: Bahrain Highlights 2026 (Deloitte International Tax)
sources.said: Individual taxation There is no individual income tax. … Withholding tax There are no withholding taxes. Bahrain has announced it intends to introduce withholding tax on certain cross-border payments to corporate entities on Bahrain-source income. The rate would be 0% for dividend payments, and 5% for interest, royalty, and service payments. … For Bahraini nationals, the employer’s social insurance contribution is 15% and the employee’s contribution is 8%, which covers old age, disability, death, and unemployment. The employer’s share will increase by one percentage point each year between 2024 and 2028, bringing the total percentage of the employer’s share to 20% in 2028. For expatriate employees, the employer’s social insurance contribution is 3%, which covers employment injuries. Expatriate employees contribute 1%, which covers unemployment. The maximum monthly earnings subject to contributions are capped at BHD 4,000. … The standard rate is 10% and applies to most goods and services. … Registration: Businesses with an annual VAT taxable turnover exceeding or expected to exceed BHD 37,500 must register for VAT within 30 days of the date when the threshold is exceeded or expected to be exceeded. Taxable persons may voluntarily register for VAT if the annual VAT taxable turnover and/or annual expenses subject to VAT in Bahrain exceed or is expected to exceed BHD 18,750.
