entries.sought: The tax on a screen worker's pay in Belize

sources.title: Taxes in Belize (BELTRAIDE, Belize Trade and Investment Development Service)
sources.said: Income tax is levied at a rate of 25% on the taxable income of employed residents in Belize whose annual earnings exceed BZ$26,000 (US$13,000). Individuals earning less than this amount are exempt from income tax. The basic allowance is BZ$25,600 (US$12,800). … Income Tax 25% on incomes above BZ$29,000 per year. … This tax, known as PAYE, applies exclusively to employee income and is not considered a cost to be borne by the employer or business. … Businesses, companies, and self-employed persons with annual earnings exceeding BZ$75,000 are required to pay business tax. … Professional Services 6.0% Commissions & Royalties 5.0% - 15.0% … Belize's General Sales Tax (GST) is a 12.5% consumer tax on goods and services. … Businesses with annual turnover exceeding $75,000 (US$37,500) from taxable activities must register for GST with the Department of GST.

sources.title: Contribution & Benefit Schedule, effective 4 April 2022 (Social Security Board, Belize)
Income and Business Tax Act, Chapter 55, Revised Edition 2020 (laws as at 31 December 2020), Attorney General's Ministry of Belize
sources.said: does not exceed twenty six thousand dollars … $25,600.00 … in the case of all other employed individuals … $19,600.00 … income of every employed person shall be charged at the rate of … twenty-five per centum of the chargeable income … “basis year” means the calendar year coinciding with the year of … last day of the third month following the end of the basis year a … return of income for that year in the form prescribed and … employee need not file a return if his only income was … A person not resident in Belize, in this section referred … to as a non-resident person, shall be assessable and chargeable … Every person who pays any management fees, rental of … plant or equipment, or charges for technical services and … insurance premium to a non-resident shall deduct therefrom tax … at the rate of twenty-five percent of such payment … “management fees” means payment for the provision of … industrial or commercial advice or for management or technical … services or similar services or facilities … withholding tax at the rate of three per centum of such payments … Where the gross contract payment is less than three … thousand dollars the provisions of this section shall not apply

sources.title: Income Tax Threshold Raised, Wider Relief for Middle-Class Workers (The Reporter, 22 September 2024)
sources.said: Effective Janu … ary 1, 2025, Be … lizean workers earning less than $29,000 annually will be exempt from paying in … come tax

sources.title: Belize Tax Service, File Your Personal Income Tax Form
sources.said: Persons earning below $26,000 personal relief is $25,600 Persons earning between $26,000.01 and $27,000 personal relief is $24,600 Persons earning between $27,000.01 and $29,000 personal relief is $22,600 Persons earning $29,000.01 and over, personal relief is $19,600 The rate for Employee Income Tax is 25% of the Chargeable Income.

sources.title: Czech Republic Highlights 2026 (Deloitte International Tax)
sources.said: The 23% tax rate is applicable to income exceeding 36 times the average wage for the calendar year (CZK 1,762,812 for 2026). … Tax year: The tax year is the calendar year. … Where a tax return is required, it generally must be filed and any tax liability must be paid by 1 April of the following year. The deadline is 1 May of the following year if a tax return that is not filed by 1 April is subsequently filed electronically by the taxpayer, or 1 July of the following year if a tax return that is not filed by 1 April is subsequently filed by a tax advisor. … Tax on employment income is withheld by the employer and remitted to the tax authorities. Self- employed individuals (entrepreneurs) generally must file a tax return but have the option to be subject to a lump-sum tax … An employer contributes 9% of the employee’s gross salary to the state health insurance funds and 24.8% of the employee’s gross salary to the state social security funds. An employee contributes 11.6% of gross income (4.5% health insurance, 6.5% old-age pension, 0.6% sickness insurance). A self-employed individual is subject to a mandatory contribution of 42.7% (13.5% health insurance, 28% old-age pension, 1.2% unemployment) on the assessment base (determined as at least 55% of the income tax base). … There is no maximum assessment base for health insurance purposes. The maximum assessment base for social security purposes (i.e., old-age pension contributions and unemployment insurance, applicable in the case of both the employee and the employer, as well as for a self-employed individual) is 48 times the average wage for the calendar year (CZK 2,350,416 for 2026). … A 35% rate applies where dividends are paid to a resident of a non- EU or non-EEA jurisdiction with which the Czech Republic does not have a tax treaty or a tax information exchange agreement (TIEA). … The standard VAT rate is 21%. A reduced rate of 12% applies to certain supplies … A Czech company must register for VAT if its supplies in the Czech Republic exceed CZK 2 million in a calendar year. In this case, the Czech company will become a VAT payer starting from 1 January of the following year. However, if a Czech company’s supplies in the Czech Republic exceed CZK 2,536,500 in a calendar year, the company will become a VAT payer on the date immediately following the date this threshold is exceeded.

sources.title: Loi n° 21-16 du 30 décembre 2021 portant loi de finances pour 2022, Journal officiel de la République algérienne n° 100 (copy held by SIPRI)
sources.said: Le revenu net annuel tel que déterminé par les dispositions de l’article 85 du présent code est soumis à l’impôt sur le revenu global au lieu du domicile fiscal, suivant le barème progressif ci-après : FRACTION DU REVENU IMPOSABLE EN DINARS TAUX D’IMPOSITION N’excédant pas 240.000 DA de 240.001 DA à 480.000 DA de 480.001 DA à 960.000 DA de 960.001 DA à 1.920.000 DA de 1.920.001 DA à 3.840.000 DA Supérieure à 3.840.000 DA 0% 23% 27% 30% 33% 35% … III. POUR LES REVENUS REALISES PAR LES PERSONNES PHYSIQUES N’AYANT PAS LEUR DOMICILE FISCAL EN ALGERIE : … 24%, pour les revenus énumérés à l’article 33 du présent code, versés par des débiteurs établis en Algérie ; … 15%, pour les sommes versées sous forme de cachets ou droits d’auteur, aux artistes ayant leur domicile fiscal hors d’Algérie. Toutefois, ne sont pas comprises dans la base de l’impôt sur le revenu global (IRG), les sommes perçues par ces mêmes artistes lorsqu’ils interviennent dans le cadre d’accords d’échanges culturels, des fêtes nationales, festivals et manifestations culturelles et artistiques, organisés sous la tutelle du ministère de la culture et de l’office national de la culture et de l’information … « Art. 31 bis. — Les contribuables réalisant des revenus relevant de la catégorie des bénéfices des professions non commerciales prévus à l’article 22 ci-dessus, sont soumis au régime simplifié des professions non commerciales. Ces contribuables doivent mentionner sur une déclaration spéciale, le montant des recettes encaissées, celui des dépenses décaissées et le résultat réalisé au titre de l’année considérée. Ils sont tenus de souscrire et de faire parvenir cette déclaration au service des impôts du lieu d’activité, au plus tard, le 30 avril de chaque année. … Sont exclus de ce régime d’imposition : … 9-les professions non commerciales.

sources.title: Tax rates (Estonian Tax and Customs Board)
sources.said: 2026 The rate of withheld income tax is 22%. The basic exemption is 700 euros per month, i.e. 8,400 euros per year, or 776 euros per month, i.e. 9,312 euros per year at pensionable age . … The rate of social tax is 33 per cent. The monthly rate of the minimum social tax obligation is 886 euros , i.e. the minimum obligation of social tax is 292.38 euros per month. The unemployment insurance premium rates are 1.6% for the employee and 0.8% for the employer (the same as in 2025). … The funded pension contribution rate is 2%, 4% or 6%, depending on a person's application to the registrar. If a person has not made an application to use a higher rate, the default contribution rate is 2%. … VAT rates are 24% (standard rate) , 13%, 9%, and 0%.

sources.title: Calculation of basic exemption (Estonian Tax and Customs Board)
sources.said: From 2026, the basic exemption is 700 euros per month, i.e. up to 8,400 euros per year. The difference compared with previous years is that the basic exemption no longer depends on a person's income … If employees do not submit an application for using basic exemption, employers must withhold income tax from the first euro (basis: subsection 2 of § 42 of the Income Tax Act ).

sources.title: Estonia - Individual - Taxes on personal income (PwC, reviewed 29 May 2026)
sources.said: Local income taxes There are no local taxes on income.

sources.title: Estonia - Individual - Other taxes (PwC, reviewed 29 May 2026)
sources.said: Social tax paid by employers is not capped and mainly applies to salaries, directors’ fees, and service fees paid and fringe benefits granted to individuals. The period of taxation is a calendar month. The net business income derived by individuals registered as sole proprietorships is also subject to 33% social tax (capped). Sole proprietorships are required to make quarterly advance payments of social tax in fixed amounts

sources.title: Estonia - Corporate - Withholding taxes (PwC, reviewed 29 May 2026)
sources.said: Payments for the activities of non-resident artists or sportsmen carried out in Estonia are subject to a 10% WHT rate. … Royalties (including payments for the use of industrial, commercial, or scientific equipment) paid to non-residents are generally subject to a 10% WHT rate under domestic law … Royalties and rental payments to resident individuals are subject to a 22% WHT rate.

sources.title: Estonia - Individual - Tax administration (PwC)
sources.said: For non-residents, the tax withheld at source at domestic or treaty rates generally constitutes final tax as regards their Estonian-source income, and the non-resident is generally not obligated to submit a tax return … The period of taxation is a calendar year. Tax returns In general, resident individuals must file an individual tax return by 30 April following the year in which the income arises. … must pay the final amount of income tax due by 1 October of the year following the period of taxation.

sources.title: Estonia - Corporate - Other taxes (PwC)
sources.said: If the taxable supplies of Estonian resident businesses or a fixed establishment of a non-resident business in Estonia exceed EUR 40,000 in a calendar year, VAT registration is required.

sources.title: Verohallinto laskee nämä vähennykset automaattisesti (Verohallinto)
sources.said: Vähennyksen määrä vuonna 2026: Työtulovähennys on enintään 3 430 euroa. Jos palkansaaja tai yrittäjä on ennen vuoden 2026 alkua täyttänyt 65 vuotta, työtulovähennys on enintään 4 630 euroa. … Vähennys on 18 % vähennykseen oikeuttavien tulojen määrästä. Vähennyksen määrää pienennetään 2,00 %:lla puhtaan ansiotulon 35 000 euroa ylittävältä osalta aina 50 550 euroon saakka. Jokaisesta huollettavana olevasta alaikäisestä lapsesta myönnetään 105 euron korotus työtulovähennyksen enimmäismäärään. … Vähennyksen määrä vuonna 2026: Vähennys on enintään 4 265 euroa. Jos puhdas ansiotulo on yli 4 265 euroa valtion- ja kunnallisverotuksessa tehtävien vähennysten jälkeen, vähennystä pienennetään 18 %:lla ylimenevän tulon määrästä. Perusvähennystä ei voi saada osittaisenakaan, jos puhdas ansiotulo on edellä mainittujen vähennysten jälkeen yli 27 959 euroa. … Saat tulonhankkimisvähennyksen automaattisesti, jos saat palkkatuloa. Vähennyksen määrä on 750 euroa.

sources.title: Käyttökorvaus (Verohallinto)

Muussa tapauksessa käyttökorvaus on veronalaista ansiotuloa, josta maksaja huolehtii työnantajavelvollisuudet samalla tavalla kuin työkorvauksista.

sources.title: Falkland Islands Government Taxation Office, Individual Information
sources.said: For 2026, the personal allowance remains at £16,860, depending on an individual’s tax residency status. The first £18,000 after the personal allowance and other allowable deductions will be taxed at 21% with any remaining amount being taxed at 26%. … A Tax Resident is someone who has been physically present in the Islands for 183 days or more during the relevant tax year. … The tax year in the Falkland Islands runs from 1 st January to 31 st December. Tax returns for individuals are issued in March following the tax year and have a submission deadline of 31 st July or 60 days from the date of issue, whichever is later. Payment of tax liabilities is 1 st October or 30 days from the date of assessment, whichever is later.

sources.title: FIG Taxation Office, Employer Information
sources.said: Payment On Account of Tax (POAT) should be applied by employers to their employees’ remuneration. The employer will take into account the personal allowance when deducting tax, however if an employee has more than one employer, only the main or full time employer should account for the personal allowance and each additional employer should strictly deduct tax a straight 21% tax from the employees gross wages. … An employer is required to submit a POAT return for each calendar month by the 14 th of the following month together with the payment for that month’s POAT. … Non-resident employees are required to have a flat rate POAT deduction from their gross wages. The employee can either accept this as their final liability to Falklands Tax or alternatively submit a tax return to receive an assessment.

sources.title: FIG Taxation Office, A General Guide to Falkland Islands Tax for Individuals (11/04/24)
sources.said: Any further Income Tax due from the individual e.g. on self-employed profits, is collected through assessment after the end of the relevant tax year. … Not resident and not ordinarily resident - assessed on income from within FI and/or for duties performed in FI. Entitled to a proportion of the PA according to the number of days present in FI during the relevant tax year … Non-resident employees should have tax deducted at a straight 21% (POAT for Income Tax). … The main taxes are Income Tax, Medical Services Tax and Corporation Tax. The FI does not have any wealth taxes, death duties, sales tax, VAT or stamp duties. … MST has been set at a rate of 0% since 1st January 2018 for both individuals and employers.

sources.title: Moving to the Faroes for work (TAKS, the Faroese tax authority), archived 10 May 2026
sources.said: If you only work in the Faroe Islands for a period of 180 days or less in a 12 month period and you do not move your permanent address to the Faroes, you are subject to limited tax liability in the Faroes. This means that you must pay a standard tax rate of 42% on all income earned in Faroes, but you remain tax liable in your country of residence. If you work onboard a FAS ship or a bareboat ship, the tax rate is 35%. … All individuals under the age of 67, regardless of whether they are subject to full or limited tax liability in the Faroe Islands, are required to contribute 3% of their income to the AM-fund. … Every time you are paid wages, your employer is responsible for making a holiday allowance contribution to TAKS' holiday fund. sources.title: TAKS (the Faroese tax authority): Tax and Royalties
sources.said: Royalties are taxed as ordinary income if the recipient is resident in the Faroe Islands This is in accordance with Sections 1 and 25 of the Tax Act. Royalty payments constitute B-income and must be reported to the Faroese Tax Authority (TAKS). … Royalties are taxed at either 0% or 25%, if the recipient is resident abroad Whether the tax rate is 0% or 25% depends on whether the country in which the recipient is resident has a double taxation agreement with the Faroe Islands. … If the recipient's country of residence does not have a double taxation agreement with the Faroe Islands, the tax rate is 25%. This is in accordance with Section 2(1)(c) of the Tax Act and Section 7 of the Withholding Tax Act. The tax is a gross withholding tax, meaning that the recipient is not entitled to deduct any business expenses that may have been incurred. The countries and territories that have double taxation agreements with the Faroe Islands are: Iceland, Denmark, Norway, Sweden, Finland, Greenland, England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland, Switzerland, India, Guernsey, Jersey, the Cayman Islands, the Isle of Man, Bermuda, and the British Virgin Islands. … The reporting deadline is 31 January of the year following the year in which the payment was made.

sources.title: BOI-IR-LIQ-20-30-10 (BOFiP-Impôts): réfaction d'impôt pour les contribuables domiciliés dans les DOM
sources.said: Dans un premier temps, l'impôt brut obtenu en appliquant le même barème qu'en métropole supporte, le cas échéant, le plafonnement des effets du quotient familial. … Dans un second temps, le montant de l'impôt ainsi déterminé est réduit : - de 30 % dans la limite de 2 450 €, pour les contribuables domiciliés dans les départements de la Guadeloupe, de la Martinique et de la Réunion ; … Les plafonds de 2 450 € et 4 050 € s'appliquent à compter de l'imposition des revenus de l'année 2018.

sources.title: BOFiP-Impôts: grille des taux par défaut du prélèvement à la source (à compter du 1er mai 2026)
sources.said: Grille des taux par défaut applicables aux contribuables domiciliés en Guadeloupe, à La Réunion et en Martinique à compter du 1 er mai 2026 Base mensuelle de prélèvement Taux applicable Inférieure à 1 875 euros 0 % … Supérieure ou égale à 27 858 euros et inférieure à 60 893 euros 38 % Supérieure ou égale à 60 893 euros 43 %

sources.title: BOI-TVA-GEO-20-10 (BOFiP-Impôts): taux de TVA en Guadeloupe, Martinique et à La Réunion
sources.said: les taux de TVA applicables dans les collectivités de Guadeloupe, de Martinique et de La Réunion sont les suivants : - taux réduit : 2,1 % ; - taux normal : 8,5 %.

sources.title: Quels sont les différents taux de TVA applicables dans les DOM ? (impots.gouv.fr, modifié le 13/10/2026)
sources.said: le taux réduit : 2,1 % pour tous les produits et services relevant en métropole du taux réduit de 5,5 % ou du taux intermédiaire de 10 %

sources.title: Artiste-auteur : fiscalité (Service Public Entreprendre)
sources.said: Guadeloupe, Martinique, Réunion Cette retenue est égale au montant de TVA calculée au taux légalement applicable sur les droits d'auteurs ( 10 % ) diminué d'un droit à déduction fixé forfaitairement à 0,40 % , soit une retenue nette de 9,60 % .

entries.sought: The tax on a screen worker's pay in Equatorial Guinea

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Equatorial Guinea, Taxes on personal income, quoting the New Equatorial Guinea Tax Code in force from 1 January 2025 (Ministerio de Hacienda y Presupuestos, minhacienda-gob.com)
sources.said: Individuals are subject to personal income tax (PIT) at the following rates. Yearly taxable income (XAF*) Tax rate (%) Over Not over 0 1,400,000 0 1,400,000 5,000,000 10 5,000,000 10,000,000 15 10,000,000 15,000,000 20 15,000,000 and above 25

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Equatorial Guinea, Other taxes, quoting the Instituto Nacional de Seguridad Social, INSESO (inseso.org)
sources.said: The employer part of contributions to the National Institute of Social Security (INSESO for its Spanish acronym) is 21.5%. The employee part is 4.5%. The employer part of contributions to the Work Protection Fund (WPF) is 1%. The employee part is 0.5%. … The standard VAT rate is 15%. A rate of 0% is applicable to a specific list of products and equipment provided in the Tax Code (e.g. certain medical products, some equipment for construction). A reduced rate of 5% is applicable to a limited list of basic consumables and books.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Equatorial Guinea, Tax administration, quoting the New Equatorial Guinea Tax Code in force from 1 January 2025 (Ministerio de Hacienda y Presupuestos, minhacienda-gob.com)
sources.said: PIT calculated in accordance with the progressive tax scale is withheld monthly by the employer and then refunded to the Public Treasury during the first 15 days of the month following the month of payment of the salaries. … The taxable period is from 1 January to 31 December.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: Equatorial Guinea, Withholding taxes, quoting the New Equatorial Guinea Tax Code in force from 1 January 2025 (Ministerio de Hacienda y Presupuestos, minhacienda-gob.com)
sources.said: According to the New EG Tax Code, there is a 10% tax withheld on the gross incomes obtained in Equatorial Guinea by non-resident entities. Therefore, as of 1 January 2025, all services provided to entities located in Equatorial Guinea will be subject to 10% WHT in Equatorial Guinea since the income is from an Equatorial Guinea source. There is a 10% WHT on royalties for non-CEMAC residents.

sources.title: Guide to the Income Tax Ordinance (Government of South Georgia & the South Sandwich Islands, 2016)
sources.said: The rate of income tax is 7%. The tax system does not give any personal allowances and does not have any additional tax bands for higher earners. The 7% rate applies to all those liable to pay tax. … A person who earns income from work carried out in the Territory will pay income tax if they are resident in the Territory for either a continuous period of 183 days or more, or several shorter periods which total 183 days in a tax year. … pay the income tax that will be due on the employee’s earnings within 14 days of the end of each quarter. The employer will then make the appropriate deduction of tax from the person's pay. … If tax is deducted, and because of a change in circumstances the employee does not reside in the Territory for 183 days or more, then any tax paid will be refunded. … the obligation to pay income tax still starts once a person has been present in the Territory for 183 days. … The tax year runs from 1st January to the 31st December each year. … Tax must be paid within 60 days from the date of the demand.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries, Guyana, Individual - Tax administration (last reviewed 02 June 2026)
sources.said: Tax returns are to be filed by 30 April following the year of income. … Self-employed persons are required to pay taxes quarterly in advance on 1 April, 1 July, 1 October, and 31 December of each year. Any outstanding balance is payable on or before 30 April in the following year. … Individuals who are employed pay taxes by payroll deduction under the pay-as-you-earn (PAYE) system. The responsibility is on the employer to deduct and remit the taxes to the tax authority by the 14th day of the month following that in which the employment income was paid.

The actual wage / salary is, at present, subjected to a ceiling of $280,000.00 per month or $64,615.00 per week for National Insurance purposes. Self-employed Persons contribute 12.5% of their declared Income as Contributions … Self-employed Contributors are not covered for Industrial Benefits.

sources.said: Skatthlutfall í staðgreiðslu samanstendur annarsvegar af tekjuskatti og hins vegar meðalútsvari (14,94%). Skatthlutfallið er 31,49% af tekjum 0 - 498.122 kr. (þar af 16,55% tekjuskattur) 37,99% af tekjum 498.123 - 1.398.450 kr. (þar af 23,05% tekjuskattur) 46,29% af tekjum yfir 1.398.450 (þar af 31,35% tekjuskattur) … Persónuafsláttur er 869.898 kr. á ári, eða 72.492 kr. á mánuði. Heimilt er að nýta allan (100%) ónýttan persónuafslátt maka á árinu 2026. … Tryggingagjald er 6,35% Sérstök trygging (0,65%) bætist við vegna launa sjómanna á fiskiskipum. Sundurliðun: - Almennt tryggingagjald 4,90% - Atvinnutryggingagjald 1,35% - Gjald í Ábyrgðasjóð launa vegna gjaldþrota 0,05% - Markaðsgjald 0,05% Samtals til staðgreiðslu 6,35%

sources.title: Iceland - Individual - Taxes on personal income (PwC, reviewed 22 June 2026)
sources.said: The municipal income tax withheld at source is 14.94% but varies from 12.44% to 14.94% in the final assessment, based on the decision of each municipality. … Icelandic-source income in the form of remuneration to non-resident directors and committee members, grants, or remuneration for independent personal services and art performances is taxed by assessment at a rate of 20% plus the average municipal income tax rate, which is 14.94% in 2026. … As of 1 January 2020, payments to authors from rightholder's associations are considered capital income and taxed at 22% after they have been made available to the public.

sources.title: Iceland - Individual - Other taxes (PwC, reviewed 22 June 2026)
sources.said: The minimum contribution is 15.5% (4% for employees and 11.5% for employers) of all employees’ and self-employed persons’ remunerations. … The payment for the assessment year 2026 is ISK 14,614.

sources.title: Iceland - Corporate - Other taxes (PwC, reviewed 22 June 2026)
sources.said: There is a National Broadcasting Fee of ISK 22,200 per year.

sources.title: Iceland - Individual - Tax administration (PwC, reviewed 22 June 2026)
sources.said: Individual income taxes are withheld at source each month. … The tax year for individuals equals the calendar year. Tax returns Individuals must file their tax returns before the end of 14 March in the consecutive year after the tax year.

sources.title: Value Added Tax (VAT) (Skatturinn, English)
sources.said: Activities of authors and musical composers and comparable artistic activities … those who sell taxable goods and services for 2.000.000 ISK or less in each twelve-month period from the beginning of their business activity … The standard rate of VAT in Iceland is 24%. The reduced rate of VAT in Iceland is 11%

sources.title: Helstu tölur og prósentur 2026 (Skatturinn)
sources.said: Skattþrep virðisaukaskatts 24% 11%

entries.sought: The tax on a screen worker's pay in Jersey

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: jersey Individual - Taxes on personal income
sources.said: Tax is payable at the rate of 20% on net income after allowances. … Tax is then computed at the marginal rate of 26%. The taxpayer’s liability is based on the lower of the tax payable at the 20% rate and tax calculated using the marginal rate. … resident in Jersey is liable to Jersey income tax on Jersey-source income, except for some specific exemptions

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: jersey Individual - Deductions
sources.said: Allowances for 2026 are as follows: Allowances GBP Child allowance (per child) 3,950 Single parent allowance 5,900 Exemption limit: Single person 21,250 … Non-residents are not entitled to Jersey personal allowances.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: jersey Individual - Tax administration
sources.said: The Jersey tax year is the calendar year. Tax returns Tax returns are issued in January following the end of the tax year. The filing deadline for these returns is 31 May for paper filing and 31 July for electronic filing.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: jersey Individual - Other taxes
sources.said: Employees are subject to social security contributions at a rate of 6% on their gross earnings, up to the monthly standard earnings limit of GBP 6,062 for 2026 (GBP 5,800 for 2025). The rate of employer contributions is 6.5%, up to the same earnings limit. Employers also have to pay a 2.5% rate of social security on earnings above the monthly standard earnings limit, up to an upper earnings limit of GBP 27,632 … Self-employed individuals are required to contribute at a rate of 12.5%, up to the standard earnings limit (GBP 72,744 for 2026) and also 2.5% on their earnings above this up to the upper earnings limit (GBP 331,584 for 2026). … Individuals are subject to long-term care contributions at a rate of 1.5% on their gross earnings up to the upper earning limit for social security (GBP 331,584 for 2026; GBP 317,304 for 2025).

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: jersey Corporate - Other taxes
sources.said: Under the Income Tax Instalment System (ITIS), the tax authority issues each employee with an effective rate notice to pass to their employer in … ng the deduction rate. If no such notice is provided, the default rate of deduction applied is 22%. … The standard rate of GST is 5%. Companies with taxable supplies of more than GBP 300,000 per annum are required to register for GST.

sources.title: PwC Worldwide Tax Summaries: jersey Corporate - Withholding taxes
sources.said: There are no WHTs on dividends, interest, or royalties paid by Jersey companies to non-residents.

sources.title: Income Tax (Jersey) Law 1961, official consolidated version showing the law from 17 June 2026 (Jersey Legal Information Board)
sources.said: Showing the law from 17 June 2026 to Current Income Tax (Jersey) Law 1961 Official Consolidated Version … (m) any royalty or other sum paid in respect of the user of a patent. … (3) Where any royalty or other sum paid in respect of the user of a patent is paid by an individual resident in Jersey wholly out of profits or gains brought into charge to tax, the person paying the royalty or sum shall be entitled, on making the payment, to deduct and retain out of it a sum representing the amount of the tax thereon at the standard rate

sources.title: Government of Jersey (gov.je), 2026 tax allowances and reliefs (rendered in Playwright)
sources.said: Standard rate: All income liable to Jersey income tax less allowable expenses and pension contributions charged at 20%. sources.title: Impôts des particuliers - Impôts de Saint-Martin
sources.said: L'impôt des résidents saint-martinois est calculé par application d'un barème progressif. L’impôt sur les revenus de l’année 2024 est calculé en appliquant à la fraction de chaque part de revenu qui excède 7 236 € le taux de : - 0 % pour la fraction de revenus inférieure ou égale à 7 236 € ; - 5,50 % pour la fraction supérieure à 7 236 € et inférieure ou égale à 14 364 € ; - 14 % pour la fraction supérieure à 14 364 € et inférieure ou égale à 31 745 € ; - 30 % pour la fraction supérieure à 31 745 € et inférieure ou égale à 85 286 € ; - 41 % pour la fraction supérieure à 85 286 €. Une réduction de 40 %, plafonnée à 6 700 €, est ensuite appliquée au montant de l'impôt ainsi déterminé. … Un avis d'imposition est en principe adressé au contribuable vers la fin du mois d'août et l'impôt dû doit être réglé avant le 30 septembre de l'année, sous déduction des acomptes provisionnels payables au plus tard les 15 février et 15 mai.

sources.title: Notice 2041-E: Personnes fiscalement domiciliées hors de France (DGFiP)
sources.said: les personnes résidant à Saint-Martin ou à Saint-Barthélemy qui ont transféré leur domicile fiscal dans ces collectivités après le 15 juillet 2007 et qui ne remplissent pas la règle de domiciliation fiscale de cinq ans dans ces collectivités(2) … Pour Saint-Martin, contrairement à Saint-Barthélemy, la règle de domiciliation fiscale de cinq ans s’applique seulement aux personnes physiques qui avaient leur domicile fiscal en France, en métropole ou dans les DOM avant de le transférer à Saint-Martin.

sources.title: Déclarer des revenus de source Saint-Martinoise (non-résidents) - Collectivité de Saint-Martin
sources.said: Si vous n'avez pas votre domicile fiscal à Saint-Martin mais que vous percevez des revenus ayant leur source à Saint-Martin (loyers d'un bien immobilier, revenus d'une activité exercée sur l'île, dividendes d'une société saint-martinoise…), vous pouvez être soumis à l'impôt saint-martinois sur ces seuls revenus. … La déclaration est à déposer annuellement, au plus tard le 31 mai, pour les revenus perçus l'année précédente. Si vos revenus de source saint-martinoise représentent au moins 75 % de vos revenus totaux, les règles de droit commun s'appliquent.

sources.title: Impôts des professionnels - Impôts de Saint-Martin
sources.said: Le système de taxe sur la valeur ajoutée (TVA) existant au sein de l’Union européenne n’est pas applicable à Saint-Martin. Toutefois, une taxe sur le chiffre d’affaires dénommée « taxe générale sur le chiffre d’affaires » (TGCA), au taux de 4 %, porte en pratique sur les ventes au détail de marchandises ainsi que l’ensemble des prestations de services.

sources.title: Déclaration de revenus (IR) - Résidents et assimilé résidents de Saint-Martin
sources.said: La déclaration annuelle doit être déposée au plus tard le 31 mai de chaque année, au titre des revenus perçus l'année précédente. Des acomptes provisionnels sont à régler au plus tard les 15 février et 15 mai.t. … L'impôt est ensuite calculé, puis recouvré par voie de rôle.

sources.title: New Caledonia - Individual - Taxes on personal income (PwC, reviewed 9 September 2026)
sources.said: Individuals, whether New Caledonian or foreign nationals, who have their tax domicile in New Caledonia are generally subject to personal income tax (PIT) on worldwide income (unless provided otherwise by a tax treaty between France and New Caledonia). … However, the tax saved from income splitting is generally limited to 300,000 CFP ( Communauté Française du Pacifique ) francs (XPF). For residents, progressive income tax rates are then applied as follows: Taxable income (XPF) Rate (%) Over Not over 0 1,000,000 0 1,000,000 1,800,000 4 1,800,000 3,000,000 12 3,000,000 4,500,000 25 4,500,000 40 … Generally, income derived by non-resident individuals is subject to a flat tax rate ( prélèvement forfaitaire ) of 25%. This tax applies to very broad types of revenues, notably employment and business or professional related income, pensions, investment income (unless subject to tax on financial incomes [IRVM]), royalties, and income from immovable property. A taxpayer is allowed to claim for the application of the progressive tax rate (as for resident) if one is in position to demonstrate that the progressive PIT would have been less than 25%.

sources.title: New Caledonia - Individual - Other taxes (PwC, reviewed 9 September 2026)
sources.said: The TGC ( taxe Générale sur la consummation ) is a value-added tax (VAT)-like tax that is applied to the consumer prices of goods and services since 1 October 2018

sources.said: Interests, royalties, and other incomes paid to non-resident individual are generally subject to a 25% flat tax.

sources.said: There are four rates of TGC: Reduced rate: 3% Specific rate: 6% Normal rate: 11% for all the operations that are not subject to another rate. Higher rate: 22%

sources.title: Questions fréquentes TGC (Direction des Services Fiscaux de Nouvelle-Calédonie)
sources.said: le bénéfice de la franchise est acquis lorsqu’il ne réalise pas un chiffre d’affaires global supérieur à 25 M XPF et si au sein de ce chiffre d’affaires, celui généré par les seules prestations de services ne dépasse pas 7,5 M XPF. … Les assujettis dont le chiffre d’affaires est inférieur aux seuils prévus à l’article Lp 509 du CINC qui le souhaitent peuvent décider d’opter pour la TGC et ce dès la création de l’entreprise. Une fois cette option choisie, elle est irrévocable

sources.title: Synthèse des nouvelles dispositions applicables à compter du 1er Juillet 2025 (TGC), DSF Nouvelle-Calédonie

sources.title: New Caledonia - Individual - Tax administration (PwC, reviewed 9 September 2026)
sources.said: Generally, the New Caledonian tax year runs from 1 January to 31 December. … each year before 1 April. … This deadline is extended to 30 June for taxpayers who do not have their tax domicile in New Caledonia. The income declaration filed electronically must reach the administration by 30 June at the latest … These payments should be made by 31 March and 15 July of each fiscal year.

sources.title: Déclaration de la retenue à la source (Direction des Services Fiscaux de Nouvelle-Calédonie)
sources.said: La retenue à la source s'applique aux rémunérations versées à des salariés détachés en Nouvelle-Calédonie par des entreprises établies hors de la Nouvelle-Calédonie. La base imposable de cette retenue est constituée par le montant net des sommes versées, après application de la déduction forfaitaire prévue au B de l'article Lp 97 et de l'abattement de 20 % résultant du II de l'article Lp 97, sous les mêmes conditions de plafond et limites. La retenue est calculée selon le tarif mentionné à l'article R 59-2 . Elle est libératoire de l'impôt sur le revenu.

sources.said: Toutes les personnes physiques domiciliées(1) en Polynésie française sont assujetties à la Contribution de Solidarité Territoriale sur les traitements, salaires, pensions, rentes viagères et indemnités diverses (CST-S) … 0,5 % à la fraction de revenus qui n’excède pas 150 000 F CFP 3% à la fraction de revenus compris entre 150 001 et 250 000 F CFP 5% à la fraction de revenus compris entre 250 001 et 400 000 F CFP 9% à la fraction de revenus compris entre 400 001 et 700 000 F CFP 11 % à la fraction de revenus compris entre 700 001 et 1 000 000 de F CFP 15 % à la fraction de revenus compris entre 1 000 001 et 1 250 000 de F CFP 18 % à la fraction de revenus compris entre 1 250 001 et 1 500 000 de F CFP 21 % à la fraction de revenus compris entre 1 500 001 et 1 750 000 de F CFP 24 % à la fraction de revenus compris entre 1 750 001 et 2 000 000 de F CFP 26 % à la fraction de revenus compris entre 2 000 001 et 2 500 000 de F CFP 28 % à la fraction de revenus supérieurs à 2 500 000 de F CFP … Lorsque le montant de la contribution est inférieur à 750 F CFP, soit pour tout revenu inférieur à 150 000 F CFP, elle n’est pas précomptée sur le salaire ou le revenu de remplacement. … Les employeurs et organismes de retraite ou de protection sociale doivent déclarer et reverser mensuellement la CST-S auprès de la recette des impôts de la DICP. sources.title: Singapore - Individual - Other taxes (PwC, reviewed 2 July 2026)
sources.said: Contributions are payable by Singapore citizens and Singapore Permanent Residents (i.e. SPR obtained via immigration rules) only. Employers and employees contribute 17% and 20%, respectively, of monthly ordinary wages (OW), up to an OW ceiling of SGD 8,000. Their respective maximum contributions are therefore SGD 1,360 and SGD 1,600 per m

sources.title: Singapore - Individual - Tax administration (PwC, reviewed 2 July 2026)
sources.said: Singapore does not have payroll withholding. … The tax assessed is payable within one month of the date of the assessment … The tax year in Singapore is the calendar year. An individual’s income from a preceding calendar year is assessed to tax in the following calendar year (i.e. year of assessment). … The tax return must be filed on a calendar-year basis and must be submitted by 18 April.

sources.title: Tax obligations of non-resident public entertainer (IRAS)
sources.said: A non-resident public entertainer is subject to a withholding tax of 15% on taxable income from services performed in Singapore. … The concessionary tax rate of 10% will lapse after 31 Mar 2022. sources.title: Singapore - Corporate - Withholding taxes (PwC, reviewed 2 July 2026)
sources.said: For public entertainers, this is a final tax unless they qualify to be taxed as Singapore tax residents. … Royalty payments are subject to WHT at the rate of 10%. sources.title: Singapore - Corporate - Other taxes (PwC, reviewed 2 July 2026)
sources.said: GST is charged at 9% on the supply of goods and services made in Singapore by a taxable person … GST registration is required if a business makes taxable supplies in excess of SGD 1 million for a 12-month period.

sources.said: Tax deducted according to the withholding tax scheme for Svalbard is entirely gross tax. No deductions for the tax calculation basis are granted. … The employer must deduct tax from salary/pension when this is paid to the employee/benefit recipient. sources.said: Taxable income (SSP) Rate* Up to 20,000 0% 20,001–40,000 5% 40,001–57,000 10% 57,001–90,000 15% Over 90,000 20% … Once the taxable income has been determined to fall under an income bracket, the whole of the taxable income is subjected to the tax rate applicable to that particular bracket (e.g., where taxable income is SSP 30,000, the 5% tax rate is applied to the whole amount and not only the amount in excess of SSP 20,000). … Monthly income of less than SSP 5,000 (zero rate). … Generally, the individual income tax rates for residents and nonresidents are progressive from 0% to 20%. … Tax year: The tax year is the calendar year. … The individual income tax return must be submitted before 1 April of the year following the tax period. A resident individual engaged in any entrepreneurial activity or receiving rental income must make advance quarterly payments of income tax. An employer must withhold income tax from an employee’s wages, including bonuses and allowances, for the appropriate payroll period. … Technical/consultancy fees or renumeration for part-time work paid to residents and nonresidents are subject to withholding tax at 20%. … An amount of 5% is deducted from an employee’s gross income as a contribution to the National Social Insurance Fund. … Nonresidents are subject to tax only on South Sudan-source income. … Royalties: Royalties paid to residents and nonresidents are subject to withholding tax at 10%. … Sales tax Rates Standard rate 18%/20% Reduced rate – Taxable transactions: Sales tax applies to manufacturers, importers, and service providers in South Sudan. Sales tax is imposed on the production of goods in South Sudan; the importation of goods and specified services such as hotel, restaurant, and bar services; and telecommunication services. … The rate charged ranges from 1% to 20%.

sources.said: 4. Charge, Rates, and Income Bands or Brackets for FY 2024/2025. (1) Personal income tax is charged for the tax year 2024/2025 on taxable income from wages and entrepreneurial Activities after standard allowable expenses of twenty percent (20%) and other expenses such as town rate, ground rate,etc. are deducted. (2) For that tax year the exemption level is raised to SSP 20,000 per month and the number of income bands or brackets scaled up. ... (a) Taxable incomes less than SSP 20,000 per month are not subject to tax zero per cent (0%). (b) Taxable incomes ranging from 20,001 but does not exceed SSP40,000 per month are charged at the rate of five percent (5%). (c) Taxable income from SSP 40,001 but does not exceed SSP 57,000 per month are charged at the rate of ten percent (10%). (d) Taxable incomes from SSP 57,001 but does not exceed SSP 90,000 are charged at the rate of fifteen percent (15%). (e) Taxable income from SSP 90,001 and above are charged at the rate of twenty percent (20%). ... 5. Deductions ... (2) ... Employee pension contribution of up to five percent (5%) of gross wages to GRS approved funded pension scheme, shall be deducted from gross income. ... Schedule 1(A) ... 2. Of that 6 percent, the employer and the employee pay 3 percent each. … The employee contribution to national insurance and national health insurance is withheld from salary and deposited directly into the relevant funds along with the employer’s contribution. … There are no residency rules for tax purposes as there are no direct personal taxes in TCI. … Value Added Tax (VAT) There is no VAT in TCI.

sources.title: TAAF, Guide pratique de l'hivernant (September 2019), "Principes généraux du système fiscal des TAAF" and "Dix questions ... sur la contribution directe territoriale" (on arrêté territorial n° 2001-29 of 6 August 2001)
sources.said: La contribution directe territoriale (CDT) est un impôt direct proportionnel prélevé sur les revenus tirés d’une activité professionnelle exercée dans les TAAF, et versé aux TAAF par l’employeur. Elle fait l’objet de l’arrêté territorial n° 2001-29 du 6 août 2001, complété par la décision territoriale n° 2001-94. … La contribution directe territoriale est calculée sur la base d’un taux unique de 9% appliqué au montant brut des revenus perçus. Celui-ci est ramené à 6,3 % lorsque le domicile fiscal du contribuable est à La Réunion. … Les revenus imposables sont constitués par le montant brut des revenus perçus lors d’un séjour dans les TAAF, à l’exclusion des prestations familiales, des allocations spécifiques destinées à couvrir des frais, et des indemnités d’éloignement. … Si votre taux effectif d’imposition en métropole ou à La Réunion est inférieur au taux appliqué par les TAAF, ces dernières remboursent le trop prélevé. … Le calcul, la déclaration et le versement de la CDT sont effectués par l’employeur qui en adresse son montant chaque trimestre aux TAAF.

sources.title: BOI-RSA-GEO-30-20210506, Agents de l’État envoyés dans le territoire des TAAF et personnes relevant d’organismes appelés à intervenir dans ce territoire (BOFiP-Impôts, DGFiP)
sources.said: les agents de l’État et les personnes relevant d’organismes appelés à intervenir dans les TAAF qui sont envoyés dans ce territoire sont soumis à un impôt local sur le revenu. … L'arrêté n° 2001-29 du 6 août 2001 instaurant une contribution directe territoriale sur les revenus perçus dans le territoire des Terres australes et antarctiques françaises pris par l’administrateur supérieur du territoire, institue une contribution directe territoriale prélevée à la source par les employeurs sur les revenus perçus au titre d’une activité professionnelle exercée dans le territoire des TAAF. … L’impôt retenu à la source au titre d’une année s’impute sur l’impôt sur le revenu français dû au titre des revenus de cette même année, acquitté l’année suivante. … Lorsque les intéressés sont considérés comme fiscalement domiciliés hors de France, les rémunérations perçues à l’occasion de leur activité dans le territoire des TAAF ne sont pas soumises à l’impôt sur le revenu en France. … Les revenus professionnels correspondant à une activité exercée sur le territoire des TAAF sont soumis à une contribution directe territoriale. Cette contribution est retenue à la source par les employeurs et directement payée auprès de l’administration territoriale.

sources.title: BOFiP-Impôts, BOI-TVA-CHAMP-20-10: TVA - Champ d'application et territorialité - Définition du territoire d'application de la TVA (version en vigueur du 18/01/2023), § 10

sources.said: (2) นักแสดงสาธารณะ … (ก) กรณีมีภูมิลำเนาอยู่ในต่างประเทศ หักภาษี ณ ที่จ่ายโดยคำนวณหักไว้ตามอัตราที่กำหนดในบัญชีอัตราภาษีเงินได้สำหรับบุคคลธรรมดา เว้นแต่นักแสดงสาธารณะที่เป็น นักแสดงภาพยนตร์หรือโทรทัศน์ซึ่งมีภูมิลำเนาอยู่ในต่างประเทศ เฉพาะกรณีที่มีการดำเนินการถ่ายทำ ภาพยนตร์หรือโทรทัศน์ในประเทศไทยโดยบริษัทหรือห้างหุ้นส่วนนิติบุคคลที่ตั้งขึ้นตามกฎหมายของต่างประเทศ … หักภาษี ณ ที่จ่ายโดยคำนวณหักไว้ในอัตราร้อยละ 10.0 … นักแสดงละคร ภาพยนตร์ วิทยุและโทรทัศน์ นักร้อง นักดนตรี นักกีฬาอาชีพหรือนักแสดงเพื่อความบันเทิงใด ๆ

sources.said: Employment income: resident Up to 10 million 5% Over 10 million and up to 30 million 10% Over 30 million and up to 60 million 20% Over 60 million and up to 100 million 30% Over 100 million 35% … Other tax deductions include a personal deduction and a dependent deduction of VND 15.5 million per taxpayer and VND 6.2 million per dependent (subject to frequent adjustments) … private business income with annual revenue exceeding VND 500 million … Tax on employment income is withheld by the employer and remitted to the tax authorities on a monthly or quarterly basis. … However, where there is no labor contract or the contractual term is less than three months, the income derived is subject to a flat rate of 10% on payments of VND 2 million and above. … Tax year: The tax year generally is the calendar year. … For individuals who file tax returns directly with the tax authorities, the normal deadline for tax return submission and tax payment is the last day of the fourth month following the calendar year end. … For Vietnamese employees, the employer is required to make SI, HI, UI, and labor accident and occupational disease insurance contributions of 17.5%, 3%, 1%, and 0.5% (0.3% for special cases with official approval), respectively. Vietnamese employees are required to make SI, HI, and UI contributions at rates of 8%, 1.5%, and 1% of the employee’s salary, allowances, and other additional income, respectively. … For foreign employees, in certain circumstances, the employer is required to contribute to HI at a rate of 3% and to SI at a rate of 17.5% (17.3% for special cases with official approval). … Foreign employees are required to make HI contributions at a rate of 1.5% in certain circumstances and retirement and death fund contributions for SI at a rate of 8%. … Employment income of nonresidents is subject to a flat rate of 20%. … Employment income: nonresident 20% … A 5% withholding tax rate applies to royalties paid to resident and nonresident individuals, while a 10% rate applies to royalties paid to nonresident companies. … A temporarily reduced standard rate of VAT of 8% applies to most goods and services until 31 December 2026. For goods and services that are excluded from the temporary reduction, the standard rate of VAT is 10%. … All organizations and individuals carrying on the production or trading of taxable goods and services in Vietnam must register for VAT purposes.

sources.title: Employing children in acting and modelling (NSW Office of the Children's Guardian)
sources.said: A child is a performer or model who is under 16 years of age.

sources.title: Authority to employ children (NSW Office of the Children's Guardian)
sources.said: and you employ children under 16 years of age for work in exhibition or entertainment, still photography or modelling.

sources.title: Requirements for different aged children (NSW Office of the Children's Guardian, 27 May 2026)
sources.said: Under 6 months 1 day 6.00am - 6.00pm 4 hours 6 months to under 3 years 2 days 6.00am - 6.00pm 4 hours 3 years to under 8 years 4 days 6.00am - 11.00pm 6 hours 8 years to under 16 years 5 days 6:00am -11:00pm 8 hours … a child does not start work less than 12 hours after previously finishing work

sources.title: Employing children in entertainment (Workforce Inspectorate Victoria)
sources.said: There is no minimum age of employment in entertainment, but you need a licence to employ anyone under 15.

sources.title: Guide to the employment of children in the Victorian entertainment industry (Workforce Inspectorate Victoria), Mandatory Code of Practice cl. 22
sources.said: Under 3 years 3 6am-6pm 4 hours 3 3 years and under 8 years 4 6am-11pm* 6 hours** 4 8 years and under 15 years 5 6am-11pm* 8 hours** 5

sources.title: Information for Applicants (Screen Australia)
sources.said: 2.1 An individual applicant must: a. be an Australian citizen; or b. be an Australian permanent resident (holding a permanent visa). c. not be: i. under the age of 18;

sources.title: Corporations Act 2001, Volume 1, Compilation No. 149 (Federal Register of Legislation)
sources.said: Only an individual who is at least 18 may be appointed as a director of a company.

sources.title: Law Reform Act 1995 (Qld), current in-force version, Queensland Legislation
sources.said: 17 What is age of majority The age of majority is 18 years.

sources.title: Age of Majority Act 1972 (WA), reprint 02-a0-11, WA Legislation
sources.said: (a)a person who, on or after the commencing day, attains the age of 18 years attains full age and full capacity on attaining that age;

sources.title: Age of Majority Act 1977 (Vic), authorised version 014 (in force from 1 August 2015)
sources.said: a person who, on or after the day of commencement of this Act attains the age of eighteen years, attains full age and full capacity on attaining that age;

sources.title: Age of Majority Act 1974 (ACT), current republication, ACT Legislation Register
sources.said: (1) Subject to this Act, a person attains full age for all purposes of the law of the Territory when the person attains the age of 18 years.

sources.title: Legal Aid NSW, When Can I? (legal sources researched October 2023)
sources.said: Sign a contract to buy a mobile phone, car, motorbike, gym membership or rent a place to live 18 Or Any age as long as it is for your benefit and you understand what you are signing ss18 and 19, Minors (Property and Contracts) Act 1970 … Get a job Any age (as long as your job doesn’t stop you going to school if you haven’t completed Year 10)

sources.title: Legal Services Commission of South Australia, Law Handbook: Who can make a contract
sources.said: A minor may make a binding contract with the consent of a court . The minor's parents can apply on the minor’s behalf, if the minor wishes to be bound; or the other party can apply, if they wants to make the contract enforceable against the minor. If the court decides to approve the contract, it will then be legally binding [ Minors Contracts (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 1979 (SA) s 6].

sources.title: Workforce Inspectorate Victoria: Employing children under 15 years old (updated 25 August 2026)
sources.said: In Victoria, a child must be: 11 to deliver newspapers and advertising material 13 to deliver pharmaceutical products or do other types of work, such as retail or hospitality. There is no age limit for working in entertainment, but there are industry-specific requirements .

sources.title: Business Queensland: Restrictions on children working in Queensland (other than in the entertainment industry)
sources.said: The Child Employment Act 2006 prohibits the employment of children below the ages specified in the Child Employment Regulation 2016 . Generally the minimum age for employment is 13. This is lowered to 11 where the child carries out supervised delivery work

sources.title: Government of Western Australia: When children can work in Western Australia (updated 4 September 2026)
sources.said: As long as the work does not prevent school attendance, children of any age can: work in a family business; perform professionally as an actor, musician, entertainer or in an advertisement; … Children aged 13 and 14 Are allowed to: deliver newspapers, pamphlets or advertising material; work in a shop, fast food outlet, cafe, restaurant;

sources.title: Children and Young People Act 2008 (ACT), republication R97 effective 16 November 2025, ss 795-796
sources.said: (1) A person commits an offence if— (a) the person employs a child or young person; and (b) the child or young person is under 15 years old. … (1) Section 795 (1) does not apply to the employment of a child or young person if— (a) the employment is in light work; and (b) the child or young person is employed for 10 hours per week or less.

sources.title: Legal Services Commission of South Australia, Law Handbook: When can I start work?
sources.said: You can work before reaching this age provided you do not work during school hours and the work does not interfere with your ability to attend school [Education and Children's Services Act 2019 (SA) s 74(1)].

sources.title: Lei nº 10.406/2002 (Código Civil), texto atualizado, Câmara dos Deputados, Legislação Informatizada
sources.said: Art. 3º São absolutamente incapazes de exercer pessoalmente os atos da vida civil os menores de 16 (dezesseis) anos. ... I - os maiores de dezesseis e menores de dezoito anos; ... VII - representá-los judicial e extrajudicialmente até os 16 (dezesseis) anos, nos atos da vida civil, e assisti-los, após essa idade, nos atos em que forem partes, suprindo-lhes o consentimento; ... Art. 1.691. Não podem os pais alienar, ou gravar de ônus real os imóveis dos filhos, nem contrair, em nome deles, obrigações que ultrapassem os limites da simples administração, salvo por necessidade ou evidente interesse da prole, mediante prévia autorização do juiz. ... II - os valores auferidos pelo filho maior de dezesseis anos, no exercício de atividade profissional e os bens com tais recursos adquiridos; … Art. 972. Podem exercer a atividade de empresário os que estiverem em pleno gozo da capacidade civil e não forem legalmente impedidos. ... I - o sócio incapaz não pode exercer a administração da sociedade; II - o capital social deve ser totalmente integralizado; ... I - pela concessão dos pais, ou de um deles na falta do outro, mediante instrumento público, independentemente de homologação judicial, ou por sentença do juiz, ouvido o tutor, se o menor tiver dezesseis anos completos; ... V - pelo estabelecimento civil ou comercial, ou pela existência de relação de emprego, desde que, em função deles, o menor com dezesseis anos completos tenha economia própria.

sources.title: Conselho Nacional do Ministério Público, Recomendação nº 24, de 10 de março de 2014 (parâmetros de proteção no trabalho infantil artístico)
sources.said: III - prévia autorização de seus representantes legais e concessão de alvará judicial, para cada novo trabalho realizado; ... V - matrícula, frequência e bom aproveitamento escolares, além de reforço escolar, em caso de mau desempenho; ... IX - depósito, em caderneta de poupança, de percentual mínimo incidente sobre a remuneração devida; ... XI - acompanhamento do responsável legal do artista, ou quem o represente, durante a prestação do serviço;

sources.title: Lei nº 8.069/1990 (Estatuto da Criança e do Adolescente), texto atualizado, Câmara dos Deputados
sources.said: Art. 149. Compete à autoridade judiciária disciplinar, através de portaria, ou autorizar, mediante alvará: ... II - a participação de criança e adolescente em: a) espetáculos públicos e seus ensaios; b) certames de beleza. ... § 2º As medidas adotadas na conformidade deste artigo deverão ser fundamentadas, caso a caso, vedadas as determinações de caráter geral.

sources.title: Decreto-Lei nº 5.452/1943 (Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho), texto atualizado, Câmara dos Deputados
sources.said: Art. 403. É proibido qualquer trabalho a menores de dezesseis anos de idade, salvo na condição de aprendiz, a partir dos quatorze anos. ... Art. 404. Ao menor de 18 (dezoito) anos é vedado o trabalho noturno, considerado este o que for executado no período compreendido entre as 22 (vinte e duas) horas e as 5 (cinco) horas. ... a) prestado de qualquer modo em teatros de revista, cinemas, boates, cassinos, cabarés, dancings e estabelecimentos análogos; ... Art. 406. O Juiz de Menores poderá autorizar ao menor o trabalho a que se referem as letras a e b do § 3º do art. 405:

sources.title: Real Decreto 1435/1985 (consolidado), art. 2.1
sources.said: La autoridad laboral podrá autorizar excepcionalmente la participación de menores de dieciséis años en espectáculos públicos, siempre que dicha participación no suponga peligro para su salud física ni para su formación profesional y humana. La autorización habrá de solicitarse por los representantes legales del menor, acompañando el consentimiento de éste, si tuviera suficiente juicio, y la concesión de la misma deberá constar por escrito, especificando el espectáculo o la actuación para la que se concede. Concedida la autorización, corresponde al padre o tutor la celebración del correspondiente contrato, requiriéndose también el previo consentimiento del menor, si tuviere suficiente juicio; … de cine, de orquesta, de adaptación musical, de escena, de realización, de coreografía, de obra audiovisual; artista de circo, artista de marionetas, magia, guionistas,

sources.title: Real Decreto 607/2026, art. 11.3 i) and disposición final segunda
sources.said: Concedida la autorización, corresponde al representante legal de la persona menor la celebración del correspondiente contrato de trabajo, que incorporará como anexo la autorización de la autoridad laboral, requiriéndose también el previo consentimiento de la persona menor que tenga doce o más años. … El presente real decreto entrará en vigor a los diez meses de su publicación en el «Boletín Oficial del Estado». … La persona menor debe contar durante la actividad laboral con la presencia de un familiar de hasta segundo grado inclusive, por consanguinidad o afinidad o, en su defecto, de una persona nombrada por la empresa con el acuerdo de los representantes legales de la persona menor, que velará por el bienestar y las necesidades de aquella. … 1.ª Hasta dos meses, no se puede autorizar trabajo alguno. 2.ª Desde dos meses y un día hasta un año, se podrá trabajar hasta dos horas diarias y un máximo de cuatro horas semanales. 3.ª Desde un año y un día hasta tres años, se podrá trabajar hasta tres horas diarias y un máximo de seis horas semanales. 4.ª Desde tres años y un día hasta seis años, se podrá trabajar hasta cuatro horas diarias y un máximo de diez horas semanales. … 6.ª De doce años y un día a dieciséis años, se podrá trabajar hasta seis horas diarias y un máximo de veinticuatro horas semanales, ampliables a treinta horas semanales si la actividad laboral se desarrolla durante el periodo no lectivo. … En todos los supuestos la realización de trabajo nocturno se podrá llevar a cabo durante, como máximo, tres días a la semana y garantizando, en todo caso, un descanso posterior a cada jornada de, como mínimo, dieciséis horas. … de dirección artística, de cine, de orquesta, de adaptación musical, de escena, de realización, de coreografía, de obra audiovisual; artista de circo, artista de marionetas, magia, guionistas,

sources.title: Código Civil (consolidado), art. 162
sources.said: Para celebrar contratos que obliguen al hijo a realizar prestaciones personales se requiere el previo consentimiento de éste si tuviere suficiente juicio, sin perjuicio de lo establecido en el artículo 158. … Pertenecen siempre al hijo no emancipado los frutos de sus bienes, así como todo lo que adquiera con su trabajo o industria.

sources.title: Texto refundido de la Ley de Propiedad Intelectual (consolidado), art. 44
sources.said: Los autores menores de dieciocho años y mayores de dieciséis, que vivan de forma independiente con consentimiento de sus padres o tutores o con autorización de la persona o institución que los tengan a su cargo, tienen plena capacidad para ceder derechos de explotación.

sources.title: Ley 55/2007, del Cine (consolidada), art. 7.1 b)
sources.said: Las personas físicas o jurídicas titulares de las empresas establecidas en España que realicen actividades relacionadas con la actividad cinematográfica y audiovisual y que soliciten alguna de las medidas contempladas en esta Ley.

sources.title: Ley de Sociedades de Capital (consolidada), art. 213.1
sources.said: No pueden ser administradores los menores de edad no emancipados,

sources.title: Código de Comercio (consolidado), arts. 4-5
sources.said: Tendrán capacidad para el ejercicio habitual del comercio las personas mayores de edad y que tengan la libre disposición de sus bienes.

sources.title: Ley Federal del Trabajo (última reforma DOF 14-05-2026), art. 175 Bis
sources.said: La relación establecida con el solicitante deberá constar por escrito y contendrá el consentimiento expreso que en nombre del menor manifiesten los padres, tutores o quienes ejerzan la patria potestad, … realicen los menores de quince años relacionadas con la creación artística, el desarrollo científico, deportivo o de talento, la ejecución musical o la interpretación artística en cualquiera de sus manifestaciones, … Las contraprestaciones que reciba el menor por las actividades que realice nunca serán menores a las que por concepto de salario recibiría un mayor de quince y menor de dieciocho años. … Los mayores de quince y menores de dieciséis necesitan autorización de sus padres o tutores y a falta de ellos, del sindicato a que pertenezcan, del Tribunal, del Inspector del Trabajo o de la Autoridad Política. … Las actividades que realice el menor no podrán interferir con su educación, esparcimiento y recreación en los términos que establezca el derecho aplicable, tampoco implicarán riesgo para su integridad o salud … La jornada de trabajo de los menores de dieciséis años no podrá exceder de seis horas diarias y deberán dividirse en períodos máximos de tres horas. Entre los distintos períodos de la jornada, disfrutarán de reposos de una hora por lo menos. … Los mayores de quince y menores de dieciocho años, deberán obtener un certificado médico que acredite su aptitud para el trabajo … Queda prohibida la utilización del trabajo de los menores de dieciocho años: Párrafo reformado DOF 12-06-2015 I. En establecimientos no industriales después de las diez de la noche; … Queda prohibida la utilización del trabajo de los menores de dieciocho años, en horas extraordinarias y en los días domingos y de descanso obligatorio. … Artículo 362. Pueden formar parte de los sindicatos, los trabajadores mayores de quince años.

sources.title: Child's Rights Act, Cap. C50 LFN 2004 (Act No. 26 of 2003), text hosted by the Policy and Legal Advocacy Centre (PLAC), quoting the Act of the National Assembly (Act No. 26 of 2003; LFN 2004, Cap. C50)
sources.said: "child" means, a person under the age of eighteen years; ... no action shall be brought against a child by a person after the child has attained the age of majority, to pay a debt contracted before majority … (1) Subject to this Act, no child shall be‐ (a) subjected to any forced or exploitative labour; or (b) employed to work in any capacity except where he is employed by a member of his family on light work of an agricultural, horticultural or domestic character; or … (2) No child shall be employed or work in an industrial undertaking … The provisions relating to young persons in sections 58, 59, 60, 61, 62 and 63 of the Labour Act shall apply to children under this Act. … "child" means, a person under the age of eighteen years; … 18. Contractual rights of a child (1) No child shall enter into a contract, except as provided in this section. (2) Any contract, except a contact for necessaries, entered into by a child for repayment of money lent or for payment of goods supplied to the child, shall be void.

sources.title: Labour Act, Cap. L1 LFN 2004, text hosted by PLAC, quoting the Act of the National Assembly (Laws of the Federation of Nigeria 2004, Cap. L1)
sources.said: (1) No child shall- (a) be employed or work in any capacity except where he is employed by a mem- ber of his fantily on light work of an agricultural, horticultural or domestic character approved by the Minister; … (2) No young person under the age of fifteen years shall be employed or work in any industrial undertaking: … (3) A young person under the age of fourteen years may be employed only- (a) on a daily wage; (b) on a day-to-day basis; and … (8) No young person under the age of sixteen years shall be required to work for a longer period than four consecutive hours or permitted to work for more than eight working hours in one day: … (a) in the case of young persons under the age of sixteen years, the interval be- tween ten o'clock in the evening and six o'clock in the morning; … "child" means a young person under the age oftwelve years; … "young person" means a person under the age of eighteen years. … (4) No young person under the age of sixteen years shall be employed in circum- stances in which it is not reasonably possible for him to return each day to the place of residence of his parent or guardian except- (a) with the approval of an authorised labour officer; and (b) on a written contract (which, notwithstanding any law to the contrary, shall not be voidable on the ground of incapacity to contract due to infancy)

sources.said: Artikel 234 1 Een minderjarige is, mits hij met toestemming van zijn wettelijke vertegenwoordiger handelt, bekwaam rechtshandelingen te verrichten, voor zover de wet niet anders bepaalt. 2 De toestemming kan slechts worden verleend voor een bepaalde rechtshandeling of voor een bepaald doel. ... 1 Handlichting waarbij aan een minderjarige bepaalde bevoegdheden van een meerderjarige worden toegekend, kan wanneer de minderjarige de leeftijd van zestien jaren heeft bereikt, op zijn verzoek door de kantonrechter worden verleend. ... entries.sought: What age changes for screen work in Honduras

sources.title: Secretaría de Trabajo y Seguridad Social: Código del Trabajo y sus reformas (Decreto 189-59)
sources.said: Los menores de catorce (14) años y los que habiendo cumplido esa edad, sigan sometidos a la enseñanza en virtud de la legislación nacional, no podrán ser ocupados en ninguna clase de trabajo. Las autoridades encargadas de vigilar el trabajo de estos menores podrán autorizar su ocupación cuando lo consideren indispensable para la subsistencia de los mismos o de sus padres o hermanos, y siempre que ello no impida cumplir con el mínimo de instrucción obligatoria. Para menores de dieciséis (16) años, la jornada de trabajo, que deberá ser diurna, no podrá exceder de seis (6) horas y de treinta y seis (36) semanales, en cualquier clase de trabajo. … Es prohibido el trabajo nocturno y la jornada extraordinaria de los menores de diez y seis (16) años también se prohíbe el trabajo de los mismos en clubes, teatros, circos, cafés, cantinas, expendios de bebidas embriagantes de consumo inmediato y casas de asignación. … Dentro de la jornada ordinaria de trabajo, las mujeres y los menores gozaran de un descanso intermedio de dos (2) horas. … Tienen capacidad para celebrar el contrato individual de trabajo las personas que hayan cumplido dieciséis (16) años de edad. … Los menores de dieciséis (16) años necesitan autorización escrita de sus representantes legales, y en defecto de estos, de un inspector de trabajo. A falta de inspector de trabajo, la autorización la dará el jefe del concejo de distrito o alcalde municipal del término en que deba cumplirse el contrato, sin perjuicio de lo que establezca la ley de menores. La autorización debe concederse cuando, a juicio del funcionario, no haya perjuicio aparente, físico ni moral para el menor, en el ejercicio de la actividad de que se trata. … pueden formar parte de las organizaciones sindicales las personas mayores de dieciséis (16) años. También podrán formar parte los mayores de catorce (14) aros con autorización expresa de su representante legal. … Pueden ser miembros de un sindicato todos los trabajadores mayores de catorce (14) años; pero los menores de edad no pueden ser miembros de sus órganos directivos.

sources.title: Ísland.is: Reglugerð nr. 426/1999 um vinnu barna og unglinga
sources.said: 34. gr. Vinna barna. Börn, þ. á m. börn undir 13 ára aldri, er heimilt að ráða til að taka þátt í menningar- eða listviðburðum og íþrótta- eða auglýsingastarfsemi. Afla skal leyfis frá Vinnueftirliti ríkisins áður en til ráðningar kemur vegna vinnu barna yngri en 13 ára. Börn eldri en 13 ára er heimilt að ráða til að taka þátt í starfsemi skv. 1. mgr. án sérstaks leyfis. Afla skal leyfis Vinnueftirlits ríkisins þegar vikið er frá ákvæðum reglugerðar þessarar um vinnutíma, hvíldartíma og frítíma við vinnu barna skv. 2. mgr. Í umsókn um leyfi skal geta um daglegan vinnutíma, næturvinnu, hvíldartíma og heildarvinnutíma á viku. Leyfi má gefa tímabundið til tilgreindra verkefna. ... Vinnutími barna á aldrinum 13-15 ára eða þeirra, sem eru í skyldunámi, má vera tvær klst. á skóladegi og 12 klst. á viku þegar um er ræða vinnu sem fram fer á starfstíma skóla en utan skipulegs skólatíma. Vinnutími barna á aldrinum 13-14 ára má vera 7 klst. á dag og 35 klst. á viku þegar um er að ræða vinnu sem fram fer á tíma þegar skólinn starfar ekki. Daglegur vinnutími 15 ára barna má þó vera 8 klst. og 40 tímar á viku. ... Börn mega ekki vinna á tímabilinu frá kl. 20 til kl. 6. ... Börn skulu fá minnst 14 klst. samfellda hvíld á hverjum sólarhring. ... Samfelld hvíld skal þó aldrei fara niður fyrir 11 klst. á sólarhring. ... Unglingum við slík störf er heimilt að vinna kvöld- og næturvinnu án takmarkana við ákveðna tíma sólarhringsins.

sources.said: La participation des enfants, à des fins lucratives ou à titre professionnel, dans des activités audiovisuelles ou de nature culturelle, artistique, sportive, publicitaire ainsi que dans le domaine de la mode est interdite. … une autorisation individuelle préalable peut être délivrée par le ministre ayant le Travail dans ses attributions, sur avis du directeur de l’Inspection du travail et des mines ou son délégué, des ministres ayant l’Education nationale, la Formation professionnelle et la Famille dans leurs attributions et du médecin traitant. … Aucune autorisation ne peut être délivrée pour des spectacles de variétés ou cabarets. … ils doivent être âgés d’au moins six ans, sans préjudice du paragraphe (3); 2. ils ne peuvent pas participer aux activités après vingt-trois heures; 3. ils doivent jouir d’un repos ininterrompu d’au moins quatorze heures entre deux participations … sur demande écrite de l’organisateur d’une activité visée par les deux premiers alinéas du paragraphe (1), accompagnée d’une autorisation écrite du représentant légal de l’enfant … les indemnités auxquelles l’enfant a droit doivent être versées sur un compte d’épargne bloqué au nom de l’enfant.

sources.title: Latvijas Vēstnesis: Darba likums (20 June 2001), as published 6 July 2001, No. 105 (original text; later amendments not shown there)
sources.said: 37.pants. Nodarbināšanas aizliegumi un ierobežojumi (1) Aizliegts pastāvīgā darbā nodarbināt bērnus. Bērns šā likuma izpratnē ir persona, kura ir jaunāka par 15 gadiem vai kura līdz 18 gadu vecuma sasniegšanai turpina iegūt pamatizglītību. (2) Izņēmuma gadījumā bērnus vecumā no 13 gadiem, ja viens no vecākiem (aizbildnis) devis rakstveida piekrišanu, no mācībām brīvajā laikā var nodarbināt vieglā, bērna drošībai, veselībai, tikumībai un attīstībai nekaitīgā darbā. ... (3) Izņēmuma gadījumos, ja viens no vecākiem (aizbildnis) devis rakstveida piekrišanu un saņemta Valsts darba inspekcijas atļauja, bērnu kā izpildītāju var nodarbināt kultūras, mākslas, sporta un reklāmas pasākumos, ja šāda nodarbināšana nav kaitīga bērna drošībai, veselībai, tikumībai un attīstībai. Šāda nodarbināšana nedrīkst kavēt bērna izglītošanos. Kārtību, kādā tiek izsniegtas atļaujas bērnu kā izpildītāju nodarbināšanai kultūras, mākslas, sporta un reklāmas pasākumos, kā arī atļaujā ietveramos ierobežojumus attiecībā uz darba apstākļiem un nodarbinātības noteikumiem nosaka Ministru kabinets. … (1) Aizliegts pastāvīgā darbā nodarbināt bērnus. Bērns šā likuma izpratnē ir persona, kura ir jaunāka par 15 gadiem vai kura līdz 18 gadu vecuma sasniegšanai turpina iegūt pamatizglītību. ... Pusaudzis šā likuma izpratnē ir persona vecumā no 15 līdz 18 gadiem, kura nav uzskatāma par bērnu šā panta pirmās daļas izpratnē.

(3) Izuzetno od stava 2 ovog člana lice koje ima 15 godina života, a koje se nalazi na obaveznom osnovnom školovanju, u skladu sa posebnim zakonom, ne može da se zaposli. … (4) Zaposlenom mlađem od 18 godina života ne može da se odredi da radi prekovremeno, odnosno duže od osam časova dnevno, niti noću. (7) Zaposleni mlađi od 18 godina života ima pravo na godišnji odmor u trajanju od najmanje 24 radna dana. … (1) Ugovor o radu može da se zaključi sa licem mlađim od 18 godina života, uz neophodnu pisanu saglasnost roditelja, usvojioca, hranitelja ili staratelja, ako takav rad ne ugrožava njegovo zdravlje, razvoj, moral i obrazovanje, odnosno ako takav rad nije zabranjen zakonom.
